His eyes stayed on Seris’ familiar face, and his mind almost immediately started analyzing everything.
It was really her, the girl who had helped him escape from the Ruined Realm, he had expected that they would meet again sooner or later.
But not here.
The Pendragon family, they had been invited, this meant the ceremony that was about to happen was truly important if even that family had been invited.
But this created one problem, the Vorhelms and the Pendragons had never had a warm relationship.
They were not blood enemies, and they were not allies, but they were definitely not friends either, in fact they were closer to being enemies, and they had even had small conflicts over the years.
The two families had competed with each other in many fields for decades.
Economic companies, huge Federation projects, political influence, international quotas, and even the younger generation of both families had always been competing.
In many competitions, tournaments, and large missions, the names Vorhelm and Pendragon were usually seen together.
Two great powers, two giants, two rivals, and because of that, Seris being here was a little strange, he did not think his family would invite them as well.
’Then why did they invite them?’ That question stayed in his mind for a few moments, but he had no answer.
"You’ve been staring at me for too long." At that moment, Seris was the first one to break the silence.
"Because I didn’t expect to see you here." Lian laughed.
Seris shrugged and said nothing.
"I thought you had already gone back to the Ruined Realm, it’s strange that you still haven’t returned." He said, as far as he remembered, this girl loved fighting and excitement.

He expected that she had already gone back to the Ruined Realm and started hunting again, but it seemed he had been wrong, and once again both of them were in the same boat, and for some reason neither of them had been able to return to the Realm yet.
"We were invited, so we came." The girl looked at him for a few moments and then said.
"Honestly, I didn’t expect the Pendragon family to be invited, even if you were invited, I didn’t expect you to come." Lian raised an eyebrow and said.
"I don’t make decisions about these things, and I don’t know." The answer was completely direct, exactly what Lian expected from Seris.
The girl was not interested in politics, power games, or family discussions.
It was obvious that she had almost no interest in relationships between families, that was also why she had not reacted much when she learned he was a Vorhelm in the Ruined Realm.
"But there’s something else too." She paused for a moment and then added.
"What?"
"I didn’t expect to see you here either, I thought you would still be at that academy."
"So you looked into my real identity?" Lian smiled, when they first met it had been obvious that Seris knew nothing about him.
But now that she knew he was here instead of being at the academy, it was clear that she had looked into him.
Without the slightest embarrassment, Seris nodded.
"Of course, after what happened in the Realm, it would have been strange if I didn’t, I would have done the same."
Lian could not blame her for that, after everything that had happened in the Ruined Realm, it was natural for any reasonable person to want to know more about the people who had traveled with them.
Silence stayed between them for a few moments, during that time, Lian had the chance to look at her more carefully.
Seris had almost not changed at all, the same long hair, the same silver eyes, the same cold and calm look, but something about her presence had changed.

It was as if the invisible pressure around her had become stronger, like a sword that was slowly becoming sharper, it was obvious that after the Ruined Realm this girl had not been idle either, and had spent all of her time becoming stronger.
In fact, that was exactly what had happened, Seris had spent every day and every night training and improving her sword skills, and honestly, she did not want to be here at all.
She did not like parties, she did not like formal meetings, she did not like family politics, and she did not like speeches.
The only thing she wanted was to return to the Ruined Realm.
Fight, train, become stronger... that was all.
But now that she had seen Lian... maybe this trip was not so bad after all.
"Were you looking around?" Lian looked at her.
"Yeah, I wanted to see what this place looks like."
"Do you want me to show you around?"
Seris stayed silent for a few moments and then quietly said.
"Sure."
They started walking together, and as they walked, different parts of the Vorhelm family territory passed before them.

The family’s central square, where hundreds of people were walking around, the training buildings for the younger generation, practice halls, battle grounds, large halls, the huge family library, towers that were hundreds of years old, and in the center of all of them stood the giant statue of the founder of the Vorhelm family.
The statue of a man holding a huge sword toward the sky.
As they walked, many people looked at them, but the interesting thing was that not all of those looks were directed at Lian.
"Isn’t that the Pendragon girl?"
"The Silver Swordswoman?"
"That famous genius?"
"Is that really her?"
"I’m not sure, but she looks exactly like the pictures, but what’s she doing here?"
Seris showed no reaction, it was as if she had not even noticed those words, or maybe she simply did not care.
After a while, she brought up another topic herself.
"Did you tell your family anything?"
"What do you mean?" Lian looked at her.
"About what happened in the Realm."
He immediately understood what she meant.
"No, just like you asked, I didn’t tell the Federation anything, I also only told my family that I got help from a few people, what about you?"
"I gave the same explanation you told me, and they accepted it without any problem." Seris answered.
Lian gave a bitter smile, that was natural, Seris had been a real genius from the very beginning, of course they would believe that this girl could defeat any monster below level twenty.
From the first day, her family had trusted her, unlike him, who had needed a lot of time and effort just to make Aldric believe that he was not lying, and in the end he still failed.
"But there’s one more person, Alisa’s daughter, she might tell everyone everything." Seris said again.
"Alisa? Even if she tells the truth, no one will believe her." This time Lian laughed, this was his smallest concern, actually, it was not a concern at all.
Seris stayed silent.
"Why?"

"Because she has no proof, and no one will take the words of a non-Awakened seriously when she talks about an Unholy Monster, there is no way anyone will believe that girl managed to escape from an Unholy Monster, even with the help of two other young Awakened."
Seris thought for a few moments and then nodded.
"That’s true."
For a while, both of them walked in silence, until suddenly the girl asked another question.
"When will the duels be held?"
"You know about the duels too?" Lian turned and looked at her.
"My family tempted me with that so I would come, they said I could fight the best people of the Vorhelm family, and maybe many others too."
For a few seconds, Lian truly did not know how to answer, this girl was really crazy about fighting.
Most people their age, if they came to a ceremony like this, would be looking for political connections, relationships, or business opportunities.
But Seris? The only thing that mattered to her was finding stronger opponents.
In the end, he said.
"I didn’t see your name on the participant list, I don’t think you’re going to compete."
"But my family said I’ll still fight even without registering, because that’s how this competition works." Seris shrugged.
At that moment... Lian suddenly stopped.
Seris walked a few more steps, then noticed and turned back.
"What happened?"
But Lian was no longer hearing her voice, his mind had started working very quickly.
If what Seris said was true... then this was not a simple tournament, actually, maybe it was not even a tournament in the normal sense.
It was probably an open challenge, the main participants would choose opponents from among everyone else for duels, that was why his uncle and the others kept calling it a duel.
But if his guess was correct... why would it be like this? Why would his family hold a competition that would let outsiders gain access to the Heavenly Treasury?
Were they too confident in themselves? But he doubted the Council of Elders would allow a competition like that, it was impossible that they would accept such a risk.
Unless they had no other choice.
’Could this also be Father’s order? But why?’ The pieces of the puzzle slowly started coming together.
A few seconds later, he finally came back to himself.
Seris was still waiting for an answer.
Lian looked toward the huge duel arena that could be seen in the distance.
"Nothing." He quietly said.
Then he started walking again, but in reality... he had finally gained a general idea of the true form of the upcoming competition, and that made him even more interested in it.

chapters.title: Chapter 109: The Banquet I
paragraphs: Lian and Seris walked in silence until they reached one of the Vorhelm family’s smaller training grounds, after some time, the stone path split into two.
One path led toward the residences of the foreign guests and the other led toward the residence area of the family members.
"I think we should separate here." Seris stopped there.
"Yeah." Lian nodded.
The girl stayed silent for a few moments, then suddenly asked.
"Do you think we’ll meet each other in the competition?" For the first time, a little emotion could be seen in her eyes...more exactly, excitement.

Lian gave a faint smile, he could tell that more than fighting other people, this girl wanted to fight him, and if his guess about the duels was correct, then the chance that they would fight each other was almost certain.
After all, other than his oldest brother, he doubted anyone else could defeat this girl.
"Probably, yeah."
"I hope so." Seris’s silver eyes shined for a moment.
That was the only answer she gave, then without saying anything else, she turned around and walked toward the Pendragon family’s residence.
Just like always, direct, simple and without needing to explain anything.
Lian watched her leave for a few seconds, then he also started walking back toward his own mansion.
On the way back, he suddenly noticed something, whenever he talked with this girl, he always felt comfortable and relaxed, he did not have any extra feeling of worry.
He was not worried that he had to hide his real self.
He was not worried that they had different views that would lead to conflict between them.
He was not worried that the girl would try to use him, make plans against him or have any bad intentions toward him.
They simply talked.
After leaving the Ruined Realm, he had met many people, Federation officials, soldiers, family members and even made a few new friends.
But none of them really knew what he had gone through.
None of them knew how those days had passed.
None of them knew what kind of monsters he had stood against.
But Seris knew.
She had been there.
She had seen that same hell.
Maybe that was why talking with her felt different.
Or maybe it was because of the girl’s personality.
When he reached his mansion, it was already completely dark, the servants had prepared everything in advance.

The family’s formal clothes were placed on the bed, black and silver clothes with the Vorhelm emblem on the chest, the design was much simpler than normal noble clothes, but the quality looked excellent.
Beside them was an official envelope.
Lian picked it up.
The Vorhelm family seal was printed on it.
After opening the invitation, he quickly read its contents.
Tomorrow’s schedule was written clearly.
In the morning, the birthday ceremony would officially begin, but the main banquet would be held at night.

Lian looked at the paper for a few seconds, then threw the invitation onto the table, based on this, he could tell that tomorrow would only be a general banquet for Diana’s birthday and her first official appearance in front of many of the world’s most important people.
Nothing special had been prepared for tomorrow.
It was mostly a banquet for discussions and conversations between the strongest people, and for the younger generation to get to know each other or, if they were smart enough, build connections.
But none of those events mattered to him.
Not the celebration.
Not the banquet.
Not politics.
Not the display of the families’ power.
The only thing that mattered to him...was the Heavenly Treasury.
Nothing else.
The next morning.
Sunlight passed through the curtains.
Lian slowly opened his eyes, it took him a few seconds to remember where he was.
Then he got out of bed, walked to the window and pulled the curtain aside.
The entire Vorhelm territory had changed.
It was somewhat like yesterday, but even busier, hundreds of servants were moving around.
Many caravans were entering through the outer gates, luxury cars were driving one after another on the special roads.
The flags of many different families could be seen all over the territory.
Even from far away, the foreign guests could be recognized.
It looked more like a global summit.
After getting ready, Lian left the mansion, the farther he walked, the more people he saw.
The Pendragon family.
The Blackstone family.
The Ashbourne family.
Several other great families whose names even he had only heard before.
Among the crowd, there were executives from huge international companies.
Army generals.
High-ranking politicians.
Federation representatives.
And even a few nationally famous Awakened.
People whose names had appeared in the news many times.
People who, by themselves, could change the direction of the country and maybe even the world.
For the first time, Lian truly realized it.
This was not just a family event.
It was a display of power.
A display for the entire country and maybe even beyond it.
Some time later, in one of the family’s main squares, his eyes stopped on a few familiar faces.
Cassius Vorhelm, the family’s oldest son, tall, golden hair and a presence that almost put pressure on everyone around him.
A few meters away stood Isabella Vorhelm, with eyes that always looked as if they were calculating something.
No conversation happened between them, but their eyes met several times.
And Lian clearly understood.
They were judging him.
In fact...almost everyone was judging him.
Cassius, Isabella and the other children of the family were welcoming the guests and receiving them.
Short conversations were taking place and everyone was getting along.
There was still no sign of the senior members of the Vorhelm family, and it was expected that they would appear at night.
He simply stood in one corner.
It was not like he needed to do anything.
Seeing that nothing special would probably happen until night, he wanted to return to his mansion.
But then suddenly, the atmosphere inside the Vorhelm territory changed, the guards started lining up, the servants cleared the main paths.
Even the family’s children seemed to have come to welcome an important guest.
For a few seconds, whispers spread through the crowd.
"The Patriarch is back?"
"Is it really him?"
"Is that possible?"
Even Lian unconsciously looked toward the main entrance.
But in the end...someone else entered.
One of the Federation’s highest-ranking figures, the Deputy Secretary-General and the future leader of the Federation.
But not the person everyone had expected, the whispers slowly disappeared, but the name that remained in everyone’s mind...was still the same, the Patriarch.
When night arrived.
The main banquet began.
Inside the central palace, the Vorhelm family’s largest hall.
High ceilings.
Huge chandeliers.
Dozens of noble tables.
Hundreds of guests.
And the quiet sound of music in the background.
Every important person was there.
Lian was also standing among the crowd.
One of the attendants came closer and placed a glass of the ceremony’s special drink in front of him.
Without saying anything, he took it.
Then he slowly looked around.
He recognized some faces.
He did not recognize others.
In one corner, the members of the Pendragon family could be seen.
In another area, several army generals were talking with each other.
A few executives from major companies were also busy negotiating.
Lian silently looked at the crowd.
He felt this banquet was much more boring than he had expected.
He doubted he would be able to stay for the whole banquet if it continued to be this boring.
He continued looking around from time to time.
Until suddenly...he stopped moving.
His eyes fixed on one face.
A face he knew well.
Far too well.
A young man who was talking with several members of the Pendragon family.
At first glance, he looked like a respectable young man with a successful future.
But to Lian, he looked different...
This man was Elena’s brother.
The brother of his former fiancée.
And at that exact moment...as if he had sensed something, he raised his head and his eyes met Lian’s directly.
"Oh?"

Without saying anything, he took it.
Then he slowly looked around.
He recognized some faces.
He did not recognize others.
In one corner, the members of the Pendragon family could be seen.
In another area, several army generals were talking with each other.
A few executives from major companies were also busy negotiating.
Lian silently looked at the crowd.
He felt this banquet was much more boring than he had expected.
He doubted he would be able to stay for the whole banquet if it continued to be this boring.
He continued looking around from time to time.
Until suddenly...he stopped moving.
His eyes fixed on one face.
A face he knew well.
Far too well.
A young man who was talking with several members of the Pendragon family.
At first glance, he looked like a respectable young man with a successful future.
But to Lian, he looked different...
This man was Elena’s brother.
The brother of his former fiancée.
And at that exact moment...as if he had sensed something, he raised his head and his eyes met Lian’s directly.
"Oh?"

chapters.title: Chapter 110: The Banquet II
paragraphs: Victor Aldren, Elena’s older brother.
Victor had also seen him, for a few seconds, their eyes met across the crowd.
Then the young man gave a short and professional smile and walked toward him, there was no hurry in his steps and no hesitation.
Just like a politician who had spent years dealing with influential people.
When he stopped in front of Lian, his smile became a little deeper.
"To be honest...I didn’t think I would see you here again."
"Interesting. I thought the same thing about you." Lian also gave a faint smile.
Victor’s eyes flashed for a moment.
"I guess neither of us planned for this meeting."
"Probably."
The two of them stayed silent for a few seconds.
A silence that might have looked strange to ordinary people, but for people who had grown up in political and noble circles, it was completely normal.
"Unfortunately, Elena didn’t come." Victor was the first one to speak again.
Lian did not expect this explanation, but he said nothing.
"She and Roderick entered the Ruined Realm a few days ago."
"I heard."
"They probably won’t come back for a long time."
Lian only nodded, to him, the matter was not very important, he had already left Elena behind a long time ago, but he could tell that this man did not want to let this subject go.
One of the people who had pushed the hardest to cancel his engagement with Elena was Victor himself.
This man had an absolute political mind.
Everything in his eyes was about profit.
Only profit and his own power.
And if Elena had married him, her future would have been damaged.
It was true that Lian was from the Vorhelm family, but at that time, after the news of his failed Awakening spread, he was no different from an outsider.
His importance inside the family had fallen to the lowest possible level.
And the fact that the Patriarch’s two wives had problems with him became another concern for Victor.
Elena wanted to end the engagement, and her brother gave her his full support.
He convinced their parents, and they handled the situation in a way that did not damage the relationship between the two families.
"I thought your father would come instead of you." Lian said something random to change the subject.
"Our family is more focused on politics, so they usually leave events like this to me." He picked up his glass.
"After all, someone has to talk with the different families."
Lian gave a quick look around.
Almost every ten meters, there was a politician, businessman or member of an important family.
Victor’s presence in a gathering like this was completely natural.
After all, as a politician with great potential, he could shine here.
A few seconds later, Victor smiled again.
"My sister has been very busy these days, I guess having a new boyfriend also brings its own problems."
"I heard, but don’t you have your own life? Why do you keep talking about your sister?" Lian answered without changing his expression, and he could tell that this bastard was trying to provoke him.
In a way, this man was one of the First Wife’s dogs.
Because besides the help he received from his own family, it was with the First Wife’s support that he was able to cancel the engagement and later enter the country’s Congress.
Being able to enter Congress at Victor’s current age of thirty was a very great achievement.
There were even many rumors that many people saw him as one of the country’s future presidents.
But all of that was only possible because of the Patriarch’s First Wife.
Otherwise, even the Aldren family did not have that much power.
The only reason the Vorhelm family had been willing to form a marriage alliance with them was because of the mines they had found in Europe.
Chaos Stone mines.
Victor looked at him for a few moments.
There was no anger on his face.
It was as if he had not heard those words at all.
In the end, he laughed quietly.
"You know? I thought after everything that happened, you would never come back.
"I thought so too, but it seems life always has its own plans." This time, Lian also laughed shortly.
Victor let out a quiet breath.
"Anyway, I’m happy to see you, I wish you the best, there are more important people I need to talk to."
"Thanks."
"You’re welcome, and oh, I hope things go better this time, I hope they don’t throw you out again."
After saying that, Victor took one step back.
Then he put the same diplomatic smile back on his face.
"I have to go, there are many people I need to talk to tonight."
"Good luck."
"I’m always successful."
Victor nodded in farewell and disappeared into the crowd.
In less than a few minutes, Lian saw the young man talking with three different families and two political officials.
"So annoying." He let out a sigh, that bastard kept trying to make him angry, it did not work, but it was still annoying.
Unfortunately, he could not beat him up here.
Otherwise, it would only bring him trouble.
"Anyway, where’s Seris?"
Then Lian’s eyes naturally stopped on another part of the hall.
The Pendragon family.
The senior members of the family were standing near one of the main tables, and among them...was Seris, and complete boredom could be seen in her eyes.
For a moment, their eyes met.
But at that exact moment, Seris looked past him.
As if she had not seen him at all.
No greeting.
No sign.
Not even the smallest change in her expression.
Completely formal and completely indifferent.
Lian only looked at her for a moment, then looked away.
He understood the reason.
Logically, they were not supposed to know each other.
At the same time, while he was looking around, he noticed that many other people were also looking at him.
Some politicians.
Some businessmen.
Some members of the great families.
And even a few of the Vorhelm elders.
From time to time, all of them looked at him and watched him.
The rumors from the Border City had spread.
Everyone here knew about his reputation.
But no one had a complete picture of him yet.
They also did not know what the Vorhelm family’s current attitude toward him was.
That made everyone act carefully.
But it was clear that many people wanted to talk with him.
Among those looks, there were a few others as well.
His brothers and sisters.
The different children of the family.
Sometimes one of them looked at him from far away.
Then acted as if they were busy with something else.
Sometimes another one gave him a short look.
But no one came closer.
No one knew yet how they should treat him.
At the same time, Lian noticed something else as well.
Not all of his brothers and sisters were here.
He quickly counted.
Out of the seven of them...he could not see two at all.
Not inside the hall.
Not among the guests.
Not even near the family.
They were probably not even in the country.
He had a guess about where they might be.
At that moment...the music suddenly stopped.
The noise inside the hall became quiet.
All eyes turned toward the main entrance.
The guards lined up on both sides of the path.
The servants stepped back.
Even many of the family’s elders stood up from their seats.
Then the loud voice of one of the ceremony hosts echoed through the hall.
"Lady Diana Vorhelm."
The entire hall became silent.
And then...she appeared.
A young girl with bright golden hair that shined under the light of the chandeliers.
Her bright blue eyes moved across the crowd.
The Vorhelm family’s formal dress had been made for her with great care.
But more than her appearance, what attracted attention was her popularity.
Many guests smiled.
Many family members looked at her with respect.
Even some of the foreign guests showed positive reactions.
Diana was truly popular.
And it could be understood just from the atmosphere inside the hall.
Walking beside her was a woman whose presence attracted just as much attention.
Lady Celestia Vorhelm.
The Patriarch’s Second Wife.
Long golden hair.
A beautiful but cold face.
And eyes that gave off a feeling of power even from far away.
She walked calmly.
But almost half of the hall was unconsciously watching her movements.
At that moment, Lian completely understood.
This woman’s real influence was much greater than he had imagined.
Years of power.
Years of management.
Years spent building a network of allies.
And the result of all that...was this position.
Diana was greeting the guests.
She smiled.
She talked with different people.
After all, she was the main star of this banquet.
Until...her eyes landed on Lian.
She suddenly stopped.
The smile on her face froze.
Her blue eyes widened slightly.
For several full seconds...she did not move.
"It’s been a while, Diana." Lian simply looked at her and said with a smile on his face.

chapters.title: Chapter 111: The Banquet III
paragraphs: The moment Diana’s eyes stopped on Lian, time seemed to stop for a few seconds.
Among hundreds of guests, dozens of politicians, famous Awakened, military commanders, and members of great families, she was the only one who showed a real reaction.
Not because of the Border City fame, and not because of the rumors everyone had been talking about these days.
But because he was her brother.
Two years, a full two years had passed since the last time they had seen each other.
And unlike many of the people in the hall, Diana had never forgotten him.
A few seconds later, the young girl gathered herself.
A gentle smile appeared on her face, and while many people in the hall followed her with their eyes, she walked through the crowd.
The sound of conversations around them slowly became quieter.
Even a few of the family elders looked over with curiosity.
When she stopped a few steps away from Lian, she gave him a small bow with the grace that had been taught to every child of the Vorhelm Family.
"Welcome home, big brother." Her voice was calm.
But in the hall that had suddenly become quiet, almost everyone heard it.
Lian looked at her for a few seconds.
Bright golden hair, clear blue eyes, and a face that looked very similar to their father.
A picture suddenly appeared in his mind, of a little girl who always walked behind him and asked him to spar with her using practice swords.
Time had really passed quickly.
A faint smile appeared on his face.
Among all of their brothers and sisters, he and Diana had one of the closest relationships.
The reason was simple, their age difference was not large, and they had grown up together.
Of course, Celestia had not been happy about that at the time, but she had not cared enough to stop it.
Although as they grew older, the distance between them became greater and greater, until Lian thought Diana had become like everyone else.
"Happy birthday, Diana."
"Thank you." The girl’s smile became a little wider.
They looked at each other for a few more seconds.
But Diana quickly composed herself.
Tonight, she was not only Lian’s little sister.
She was the main host of this event, and hundreds of people had come to see her.
"Sorry, I have to go take care of the guests."
"Go ahead." Lian nodded.
Diana smiled, then turned around and walked back toward the crowd.
Almost immediately, several nobles and politicians walked toward her.
It was as if the main star of the event had finally appeared.
Lian silently watched the scene.
And the longer he watched, the more he realized how different Diana’s position really was.
In this country, great families held birthday parties for their children.
But an event on this level?
Almost never.
In fact, even in the Vorhelm Family, a celebration like this would normally never be held.
The only exception was when someone from the younger generation awakened a Five-Star Class.
A class that could change not only one person’s future, but the future of an entire family.
That was why today looked much more like a national summit than the birthday party of a sixteen-year-old girl.
Generals, CEOs of multi-billion-dollar companies, members of Congress, heirs of great families, all of them were waiting to congratulate Diana.
In the eyes of many of them, Diana was not just a young girl.
She was a valuable investment for the future.
A national talent, maybe even one of the future pillars of this country and this world.
Five-Star Classes were that rare.
They were so rare that many families even hid the fact that one of their children had awakened a Five-Star Class for safety reasons.
Just like Seris, whose class was still completely unknown.
But Lian guessed that she most likely had a Five-Star Warrior Class.
Among all of the Patriarch’s children, only one other person was publicly known to have a Five-Star Class, and that was the eldest son.
As time passed, more and more people entered the hall.
Members of the different branches of the Vorhelm Family, uncles, aunts, cousins.
The atmosphere inside the hall slowly became heavier and more formal.
This was no longer just a party.
This was the gathering of the entire family.
But among all the faces, one absence was very noticeable.
The Patriarch’s first wife.
The strongest woman in the family.
The woman many people considered the true second most powerful person in the family.
But Lian was not surprised at all.
She rarely attended events like this, so her absence was almost normal.
At that moment, someone separated from the crowd and walked directly toward Lian.
Damian.
At the same moment, several curious eyes turned toward them.
Damian was one of the most important people in the family.
He could sit beside politicians, stand beside army commanders, or talk with the family elders.
But instead of all of them, he came directly to Lian.
There could not have been a clearer message than that.
"So, what do you think?" Damian stood beside him.
"It looks more like a global summit than a birthday party." Lian looked at the crowd.
"Welcome to the Vorhelm Family, if you stop being stubborn, you might have the chance to fight for control of this family." Damian laughed.
"Even if I don’t stay here, I can come back whenever I want and take the position of family leader."
"It’s fine if you say that in front of me, but don’t say it in front of the others, they might explode from anger."
Lian shrugged as if he did not care, then looked toward another part of the hall again.
The Pendragon Family.
They were gathered on the eastern side of the hall.
And the longer he watched them, the stranger the relationship between the two families looked.
There was no conflict.
There was no disrespect either.
But the distance between them was obvious.
The members of the two families only spoke when it was necessary.
The conversations were short.
The smiles were fake.
And almost no one stayed beside the other side for more than a few minutes.
It was as if everyone had agreed to be polite... but nothing more.
"If they really dislike each other this much, then why were the Pendragons invited?" Lian slowly raised an eyebrow.
"Politics, inviting them was necessary to avoid creating hostility." Damian only shrugged.
That one word explained almost everything.
Lian thought about it.
No matter how many problems the two sides had, they had never called each other enemies.
And it seemed both sides were trying to make sure their conflict would never become true hostility, or even worse, an existential conflict.
"Where’s Aron?" he then asked.
"With the other young people, he has many friends among them, and maybe he can also find himself a good wife." Damian answered without taking his eyes off the hall.
A few minutes later, one of the family elders stepped onto the central stage.
An old man with white hair and a formal robe.
The noise inside the hall slowly disappeared.
Then his voice echoed throughout the hall.
"Before the banquet ends, I need to announce the rules of tomorrow’s competition."
Almost everyone’s attention was drawn to him.
Even the politicians.
Even the foreign guests.
Many of them had come here exactly for this announcement.
The old man continued.

"All main participants will be free to choose their own opponent, the winner of each battle will advance to the next round, and then will once again choose the next opponent from among those who have already won."
Whispers spread through the crowd.
But the old man continued.
"This process will continue until only three people remain."
Then he paused and spoke the most important sentence.
"The final three people, no matter which family they belong to, will receive permission to enter the Heavenly Treasury.
A short silence filled the hall.
Even some of the foreign guests were shocked.
The Heavenly Treasury.
A name that almost everyone had heard.
But very few people had ever seen it.
They had never expected that the reward would be access to the Heavenly Treasury.
Everyone’s expression became serious.
They immediately told the younger members of their families how important it was to win.
Time passed.
Slowly, the banquet reached its final hours.
The music was still playing.
But more and more guests were starting to leave.
Lian looked at the time, then said to Damian,
"I think I’ll head back to my room."
"No problem, tomorrow will be a long day for you."
Lian placed his glass on the table and prepared to leave the hall.
There was nothing for him to do here.
From the very beginning, his attendance had only been a way to show respect for Diana.
But at that exact moment... a woman’s voice echoed throughout the hall.
"Wait."
Silence instantly filled the hall.
The music stopped.
Hundreds of people turned at the same time.
Every eye stopped on one person.
Celestia Vorhelm.
The Patriarch’s second wife.
Diana’s mother.
She slowly stepped out of the crowd.
Her face was calm.
But there was power in her eyes that made many people fall silent without even realizing it.
For the first time since the banquet had begun, she looked directly at Lian.
A few seconds of silence passed.
"Since you arrived, you haven’t even bothered to come and greet your stepmother, and now you’re leaving without saying goodbye? Didn’t anyone teach you manners?" she said.
Lian stared at her.
He could see the mockery in her eyes.
This woman had a plan against him.
"My apologies, greetings to the Second Matriarch." he calmly replied, intentionally using the word "Second."
Celestia’s expression immediately became stiff when she heard "Second Matriarch."
It was as if she had heard a very sensitive word, one that could drive her mad.
She spoke in a cold voice.
"I heard you plan to participate in tomorrow’s competition."
"That’s right." Lian answered without changing his expression.
Celestia slowly nodded.
"Good, then I hope that unlike your manners and your lack of respect, at least you won’t bring shame to this family during the duels."
In an instant, it felt as if the temperature inside the hall had dropped by several degrees.
Some people held their breath, others completely froze, this was not just a sentence, it was a public challenge...From one of the most powerful women in the family.
Directly in front of hundreds of witnesses.
Lian let out a quiet sigh.
He had decided not to cause any trouble during this banquet.
But it seemed that fate... had other plans.
I feel like it’s been a bit weaker than the previous ones, but I think we need a slower arc like this so I can properly set things up for the next one.
Anyway, if you have any questions, criticism, or suggestions, I’d be happy to hear them.

Generals, CEOs of multi-billion-dollar companies, members of Congress, heirs of great families, all of them were waiting to congratulate Diana.
In the eyes of many of them, Diana was not just a young girl.
She was a valuable investment for the future.
A national talent, maybe even one of the future pillars of this country and this world.
Five-Star Classes were that rare.
They were so rare that many families even hid the fact that one of their children had awakened a Five-Star Class for safety reasons.
Just like Seris, whose class was still completely unknown.
But Lian guessed that she most likely had a Five-Star Warrior Class.
Among all of the Patriarch’s children, only one other person was publicly known to have a Five-Star Class, and that was the eldest son.
As time passed, more and more people entered the hall.
Members of the different branches of the Vorhelm Family, uncles, aunts, cousins.
The atmosphere inside the hall slowly became heavier and more formal.
This was no longer just a party.
This was the gathering of the entire family.
But among all the faces, one absence was very noticeable.
The Patriarch’s first wife.
The strongest woman in the family.
The woman many people considered the true second most powerful person in the family.
But Lian was not surprised at all.
She rarely attended events like this, so her absence was almost normal.
At that moment, someone separated from the crowd and walked directly toward Lian.
Damian.
At the same moment, several curious eyes turned toward them.
Damian was one of the most important people in the family.
He could sit beside politicians, stand beside army commanders, or talk with the family elders.
But instead of all of them, he came directly to Lian.
There could not have been a clearer message than that.
"So, what do you think?" Damian stood beside him.
"It looks more like a global summit than a birthday party." Lian looked at the crowd.
"Welcome to the Vorhelm Family, if you stop being stubborn, you might have the chance to fight for control of this family." Damian laughed.
"Even if I don’t stay here, I can come back whenever I want and take the position of family leader."
"It’s fine if you say that in front of me, but don’t say it in front of the others, they might explode from anger."
Lian shrugged as if he did not care, then looked toward another part of the hall again.
The Pendragon Family.
They were gathered on the eastern side of the hall.
And the longer he watched them, the stranger the relationship between the two families looked.
There was no conflict.
There was no disrespect either.
But the distance between them was obvious.
The members of the two families only spoke when it was necessary.
The conversations were short.
The smiles were fake.
And almost no one stayed beside the other side for more than a few minutes.
It was as if everyone had agreed to be polite... but nothing more.
"If they really dislike each other this much, then why were the Pendragons invited?" Lian slowly raised an eyebrow.
"Politics, inviting them was necessary to avoid creating hostility." Damian only shrugged.
That one word explained almost everything.
Lian thought about it.
No matter how many problems the two sides had, they had never called each other enemies.
And it seemed both sides were trying to make sure their conflict would never become true hostility, or even worse, an existential conflict.
"Where’s Aron?" he then asked.
"With the other young people, he has many friends among them, and maybe he can also find himself a good wife." Damian answered without taking his eyes off the hall.
A few minutes later, one of the family elders stepped onto the central stage.
An old man with white hair and a formal robe.
The noise inside the hall slowly disappeared.
Then his voice echoed throughout the hall.
"Before the banquet ends, I need to announce the rules of tomorrow’s competition."
Almost everyone’s attention was drawn to him.
Even the politicians.
Even the foreign guests.
Many of them had come here exactly for this announcement.
The old man continued.

"All main participants will be free to choose their own opponent, the winner of each battle will advance to the next round, and then will once again choose the next opponent from among those who have already won."
Whispers spread through the crowd.
But the old man continued.
"This process will continue until only three people remain."
Then he paused and spoke the most important sentence.
"The final three people, no matter which family they belong to, will receive permission to enter the Heavenly Treasury.
A short silence filled the hall.
Even some of the foreign guests were shocked.
The Heavenly Treasury.
A name that almost everyone had heard.
But very few people had ever seen it.
They had never expected that the reward would be access to the Heavenly Treasury.
Everyone’s expression became serious.
They immediately told the younger members of their families how important it was to win.
Time passed.
Slowly, the banquet reached its final hours.
The music was still playing.
But more and more guests were starting to leave.
Lian looked at the time, then said to Damian,
"I think I’ll head back to my room."
"No problem, tomorrow will be a long day for you."
Lian placed his glass on the table and prepared to leave the hall.
There was nothing for him to do here.
From the very beginning, his attendance had only been a way to show respect for Diana.
But at that exact moment... a woman’s voice echoed throughout the hall.
"Wait."
Silence instantly filled the hall.
The music stopped.
Hundreds of people turned at the same time.
Every eye stopped on one person.
Celestia Vorhelm.
The Patriarch’s second wife.
Diana’s mother.
She slowly stepped out of the crowd.
Her face was calm.
But there was power in her eyes that made many people fall silent without even realizing it.
For the first time since the banquet had begun, she looked directly at Lian.
A few seconds of silence passed.
"Since you arrived, you haven’t even bothered to come and greet your stepmother, and now you’re leaving without saying goodbye?
Didn’t anyone teach you manners?" she said.
Lian stared at her.
He could see the mockery in her eyes.
This woman had a plan against him.
"My apologies, greetings to the Second Matriarch." he calmly replied, intentionally using the word "Second."
Celestia’s expression immediately became stiff when she heard "Second Matriarch."
It was as if she had heard a very sensitive word, one that could drive her mad.
She spoke in a cold voice.
"I heard you plan to participate in tomorrow’s competition."
"That’s right." Lian answered without changing his expression.
Celestia slowly nodded.
"Good, then I hope that unlike your manners and your lack of respect, at least you won’t bring shame to this family during the duels."
In an instant, it felt as if the temperature inside the hall had dropped by several degrees.
Some people held their breath, others completely froze, this was not just a sentence, it was a public challenge...From one of the most powerful women in the family.
Directly in front of hundreds of witnesses.
Lian let out a quiet sigh.
He had decided not to cause any trouble during this banquet.
But it seemed that fate... had other plans.
I feel like it’s been a bit weaker than the previous ones, but I think we need a slower arc like this so I can properly set things up for the next one.
Anyway, if you have any questions, criticism, or suggestions, I’d be happy to hear them.

chapters.title: Chapter 112: A Big Mistake?
paragraphs: A heavy silence fell over the hall.
Hundreds of guests, dozens of great families, politicians, generals, CEOs of huge companies, and the elders of the Vorhelm family.
Everyone was waiting, waiting for Lian’s reaction.
Celestia Vorhelm was still standing in the center of the hall.
Her face looked calm, but anyone who knew her could understand how much pressure was hidden behind that calm expression.

She had asked that question on purpose, deliberately, because she wanted to put this boy in front of everyone, she wanted to see whether Lian was still the weak and inexperienced teenager from the past or not.
She wanted to see whether he could control his anger or not. If he answered the matriarch of the family in an insulting or disrespectful way, she could use that as an excuse to suppress him.
But Lian did not get angry, did not get upset, and did not even frown, he only looked at her for a few seconds.
After making that bet with Damian, he had changed his plans a little and wanted to act more carefully, but it seemed he had no choice, and he calmly said,
"If by embarrassing the family you mean losing, then don’t worry, until today I have never entered a fight to lose or to experience defeat."
"I only entered to win."
Silence, complete silence filled the hall, even the soft music in the background could no longer be heard.
Several politicians looked at each other in surprise.
One of the generals smiled.
Some of the young members of the Vorhelm family frowned, and several elders unconsciously raised their eyebrows.

Those words were not boasting, at least his tone did not sound like boasting, and that was exactly the problem, he had said them with such calmness that it sounded like he was simply stating an obvious fact.
And that was what made it dangerous, he spoke as if he had absolute confidence in every word he said and saw them as the truth.
More importantly, he said all of it with complete calmness.
At that moment Diana stepped forward, she clearly understood that things were moving toward a conflict, a gentle smile appeared on her face, then she looked at her mother and said,
"Mother." Her voice was soft, but loud enough for everyone to hear.
"Tonight is a birthday celebration, I don’t think anyone wants to talk about tomorrow’s competition." Then she looked at Lian and gave him a small smile.
"Right, big brother?"
Lian looked at her for a moment, then shrugged.
"I don’t have a problem with it." He was not the one who had started this discussion, he was only answering.
But the real event happened after that, the Pendragon family had been watching this whole scene from the beginning, and as the Vorhelm family’s long-time rivals... they naturally enjoyed it.
But unlike what many people expected, no one stepped in directly.
At least... not at first. A few seconds later, a woman stepped out from the crowd, she was wearing a formal black dress.
Long silver hair, silver eyes exactly like Seris, and a smile that looked a little too perfect, a woman whom many politicians in the country feared.

Lady Aurelia Pendragon, the chief diplomat of the Pendragon family, a woman who had served two terms as the Prime Minister of a country, and now worked as the Secretary General of Foreign Affairs for the Pendragon family.
She slowly walked forward and stopped directly in front of Lian, then smiled.
"So you’re Lian Vorhelm."
"And you must be Lady Aurelia Pendragon." Lian gave her a short look, it was hard not to know this woman, besides her stunning beauty, she was famous across all of North and South America.
Several people around them immediately paid more attention.
"Oh, it seems you know me quite well." Aurelia laughed.
"There is no need to know you, if I ever see a face as beautiful as yours anywhere, I will definitely remember it forever." Lian answered calmly.
Several members of the Pendragon family laughed, and even Aurelia’s smile became deeper, it was obvious that she liked that answer very much.
What woman would not be happy to have her beauty praised? Especially by a Vorhelm, by one of the Patriarch’s sons.
When Celestia saw that she had been completely pushed out of the conversation, she wanted to say something, but Aurelia did not give her the chance.
Then... the conversation began. At first it was only a simple conversation between the two of them, but little by little it changed.
Aurelia talked about politics, about the competition between neighboring countries, about other continents, about the new economic pressure, about the condition of mana crystal exports.
Her goal was simple, she wanted to test this boy, a boy who had almost become one of history’s forgotten people not long ago, and then suddenly? He drew everyone’s attention by saving one city.
If it had been someone else, maybe the Pendragon family would not have cared so much, but by fate, he was a Vorhelm, a Vorhelm who had been cast aside by his own family.

And Lian answered every question and every topic. As someone who truly thought deeply, he talked about border trade routes, about the effect monsters had on the economy of the outer regions, about how the market for Awakened equipment was growing, and about the real problems of the border cities.
He had always liked sharing his ideas about these subjects, he just had never had the chance before.
But now he could finally talk about these things with someone.

Little by little, Aurelia realized that something was strange, this boy was not only intelligent, he had reasons and logical arguments behind every opinion, and even she slowly started thinking that maybe they could make use of some of this boy’s ideas.
More and more people slowly came closer, they had become curious about their conversation.
First one politician came, then one company director, then one general, then several family elders, and then several more people.
Within only a few minutes, a small circle had formed around Lian.
"Boy, how old are you?" the old general asked with a laugh.
"Eighteen.
The general stayed silent for a few seconds, then said with admiration,
"When I was eighteen, I couldn’t even say half of these things."
Laughter spread through the group.
Their discussion became more and more lively, the more they talked with him, the more they enjoyed talking with him.
The people who only a few minutes ago wanted to leave the banquet as soon as possible, now no longer cared about the time, and simply spent their time talking with one young man.
Not too far away... Damian was watching the whole scene, another family elder was standing beside him.
"What is he doing?" he asked in surprise.
"Nothing, he’s just talking, and maybe that’s even more dangerous than using a sword, he stole everyone’s attention just by talking." Damian laughed.
On the other side of the hall... Celestia saw everything, all the politicians, generals, investors, family elders, they had all gathered around Lian.
And worst of all... even Diana was standing beside him, her own daughter!
This was the exact opposite of what she wanted, she wanted to make this boy look small, she wanted to remind everyone that Lian was only an exiled son.
But now... the entire banquet’s attention was focused on him, even the attention that should have belonged to Diana!
If this is how things are going to be, then it’s time for this banquet to end.
For a brief moment Celestia’s expression changed, only for a moment, but that one moment was enough, then her smile returned and she calmly said,
"The banquet has come to an end." Her voice echoed through the hall.
"Everyone may leave and get some rest."
Then without even looking at Lian one more time... she turned around and left the hall.
The crowd slowly began to scatter, and the guests started leaving. Aurelia was the last person still standing in front of Lian, she smiled.
"I think tomorrow’s competition will be very interesting, Mr. Vorhelm. I hope you do well, and it was a pleasure meeting you."
"I think so too." Lian smiled as well.
Aurelia nodded and left the hall together with the members of the Pendragon family.
After waving to Damian, Lian also returned to his residence. He had achieved what he wanted, he had stolen all the attention that was supposed to belong to the Vorhelm family and Celestia.
A few minutes later, when almost everyone had already left, one of the Vorhelm family elders who supported Celestia quietly looked toward the exit and muttered,
"Maybe..." He paused, his eyes stayed fixed on the place where Lian had been standing only moments before.
"...bringing that boy back was a huge mistake."

chapters.title: Chapter 113: The Duels I
paragraphs: The day of the competition finally arrived.
Lian woke up before the sun had fully risen. For a few seconds, he sat on the bed and listened to the silence of the room.
But it was not real silence, even through the thick windows of the mansion, he could hear the noise outside of here
The sound of footsteps, the sound of people who had been preparing for the event since the early morning.
He stood up and pulled the curtains aside, and for a moment, even he paused.
The entire Vorhelm family territory had changed. The flags of many different families had been placed in different areas.
Groups of guards were patrolling, servants were constantly moving between the buildings.
"I doubt that woman will leave me alone so easily." Lian muttered to himself as he thought about what had happened last night.
At first, he thought that woman might not try to cause trouble or confront him in front of so many people, but he had been wrong. Celestia had tried to make him look small in front of everyone.
If he wanted to say what he really thought, then he would say that woman was worried, worried that the current balance would be broken because of him.
Even now, she was already fighting against the First Matriarch, the Patriarch’s first wife, and she was clearly losing that fight, something that could end with her downfall.

And now Lian, the boy who had suddenly received the Patriarch’s attention, had appeared. All of this was like a huge pressure on her, and that pressure made her try to isolate him last night by making him look small, so he would not become a threat.
But unfortunately, she failed badly, and that failure cost her a lot. But Lian doubted Celestia would give up that easily. Instead, she would definitely make a bigger move against him.
And that move would definitely happen today.
"So much trouble that I have to deal with." He laughed sarcastically.

"At least last night’s banquet wasn’t only a headache. I managed to make connections with many famous and powerful people, and it’s clear that the Pendragon family now has a good opinion of me." He did not have a bad opinion of the Pendragon family, and having a connection with them was definitely not a bad thing.
But in his eyes, none of those connections were as important as his own strength.
After putting on the Vorhelm family’s formal clothes, Lian left the mansion.
On the way, almost everyone he saw was moving in the same direction, toward the duel arena, the main center of the competition.
A few minutes later.
When he saw the arena from up close for the first time, even he could not stay calm.
The arena was enormous, much bigger than it had been until yesterday. Rows of seats surrounded the arena like huge rings.
Tens of thousands of people could easily sit there. In the northern section of the arena was the special area for the family elders.

It was a high platform with a full view of the entire arena. In the east was the area for the important families and the foreign guests. In the west sat the politicians, generals, and national figures.
And in the southern section were the young generation of the families and the participants.
Dozens of special guards were standing around the arena, not ordinary guards, but Awakened whose heavy presence could be felt even from far away.
After almost every seat was filled, one of the family elders appeared on the central platform.
He was an old man with white hair, but his voice was still powerful.
"Welcome to this year’s Vorhelm family competition." His voice echoed across the entire arena, then he announced the rules.
Rules that most people already knew part of, but not all of them.
"The young members of the Vorhelm family will have priority when choosing their opponents."
Whispers spread through the crowd. It seemed unfair, but after all, this was a competition hosted by them, and the reward was so great that nobody cared.
"They may choose anyone from the young generation attending this event, of course, only those who wish to participate in the competition."
"No one may refuse a match that has been assigned to them and ask to fight someone else. The opponent cannot be changed." Then he paused.
"Of course, they may refuse to accept the match, but in that case they will be considered defeated, and naturally, both their personal reputation and their family’s reputation will be damaged."
"As you all know, this is a friendly competition, a stage for the young generation to show their talent, and a chance to build their reputation."
Some people smiled, but almost everyone knew that this was only half of the truth. No one was going to reveal all of their strength in a competition like this.
And the only reason everyone was here was the Heavenly Treasury.
The first person to enter the arena was... Cassius Vorhelm, and the moment he entered, the entire arena became silent.
The eldest son, the person many believed would become the future heir of the family.
Tall, well dressed, calm, and carrying the confidence that could only be seen in people who had spent years preparing to rule.
Without wasting any time, he chose his opponent, a young man around twenty years old. Strangely, he did not choose a powerful opponent.
First his level was limited to 20, then the battle began.
And less than one minute later, it ended.
Cassius did not even need to become serious once. Three moves, three strikes, and a complete victory.
Cheers filled the arena.
But Lian only watched, analyzing, the movements, the speed, the mana control, the fighting style, he stored everything in his mind.
After that it was Isabella’s turn, then Evangelin, then Adrian, and Aron.
Each of them showed their strength. Isabella was precise and ruthless. Evangelin’s magic was fast and impossible to predict.
Adrian also showed skill far beyond his age. But what caught Lian’s attention was not the battles themselves, but the choices.
Almost every member of the family was choosing weaker opponents, and even stranger, some specific people were still untouched.
At first it looked like a coincidence, but as time passed, the pattern became clearer. They were removing the weaker participants.
They were organizing the battlefield, preparing the stage for something bigger, as if they wanted to make sure Lian would have no choice except to fight the strongest outsider.
Lian smiled calmly. So this was the plan they had prepared against him.
Several more battles took place, until finally a name was announced that caught everyone’s attention.
Lucas Vorhelm.
The arena suddenly became silent, and the next moment, a man entered the arena who looked more like a human monster than an ordinary Awakened.
Tall, broad shoulders, muscles that could be seen even under his clothes, there was no elegance in him.
Everything about him screamed: warrior.
After Diana, he was the newest genius of the Vorhelm family to become famous during the past two years, and he had a great future ahead of him.
A smile appeared on his face, a smile that looked nothing like a friendly one. Then he raised his head and looked toward the participants’ area.
His eyes passed over several people, over Lian, over Adrian, over the others, and finally stopped on a girl with silver eyes.
Seris Pendragon.
For one short moment... complete silence filled the arena. Then Lucas said in a loud voice,
"I’ve chosen my opponent."
Everyone was waiting, even the family elders were watching him.
Lucas raised his hand and pointed directly toward the Pendragon family’s area.
"Seris Pendragon."
For one second... nobody said anything. Then... the entire arena exploded.
Even some of the elders could not hide their reactions.
Lucas Vorhelm...
One of the strongest young members of the family... instead of choosing an easy opponent... had chosen one of the most famous geniuses of the country’s new generation.

And in the middle of all that noise... Lian only looked at Seris, the girl who was sitting several rows away, and for the first time since she had arrived here, a very faint smile could be seen on her lips.
It was as if she had been waiting for exactly this.
That she could finally fight!

Celestia had tried to make him look small in front of everyone.
If he wanted to say what he really thought, then he would say that woman was worried, worried that the current balance would be broken because of him.
Even now, she was already fighting against the First Matriarch, the Patriarch’s first wife, and she was clearly losing that fight, something that could end with her downfall.
And now Lian, the boy who had suddenly received the Patriarch’s attention, had appeared.
All of this was like a huge pressure on her, and that pressure made her try to isolate him last night by making him look small, so he would not become a threat.
But unfortunately, she failed badly, and that failure cost her a lot.
But Lian doubted Celestia would give up that easily.
Instead, she would definitely make a bigger move against him.
And that move would definitely happen today.
"So much trouble that I have to deal with." He laughed sarcastically.
"At least last night’s banquet wasn’t only a headache.

I managed to make connections with many famous and powerful people, and it’s clear that the Pendragon family now has a good opinion of me." He did not have a bad opinion of the Pendragon family, and having a connection with them was definitely not a bad thing.
But in his eyes, none of those connections were as important as his own strength.
After putting on the Vorhelm family’s formal clothes, Lian left the mansion.
On the way, almost everyone he saw was moving in the same direction, toward the duel arena, the main center of the competition.
A few minutes later.
When he saw the arena from up close for the first time, even he could not stay calm.
The arena was enormous, much bigger than it had been until yesterday.
Rows of seats surrounded the arena like huge rings.
Tens of thousands of people could easily sit there.
In the northern section of the arena was the special area for the family elders.
It was a high platform with a full view of the entire arena.
In the east was the area for the important families and the foreign guests.
In the west sat the politicians, generals, and national figures.
And in the southern section were the young generation of the families and the participants.
Dozens of special guards were standing around the arena, not ordinary guards, but Awakened whose heavy presence could be felt even from far away.
After almost every seat was filled, one of the family elders appeared on the central platform.
He was an old man with white hair, but his voice was still powerful.
"Welcome to this year’s Vorhelm family competition." His voice echoed across the entire arena, then he announced the rules.
Rules that most people already knew part of, but not all of them.
"The young members of the Vorhelm family will have priority when choosing their opponents."
Whispers spread through the crowd.
It seemed unfair, but after all, this was a competition hosted by them, and the reward was so great that nobody cared.
"They may choose anyone from the young generation attending this event, of course, only those who wish to participate in the competition."
"No one may refuse a match that has been assigned to them and ask to fight someone else.
The opponent cannot be changed." Then he paused.
"Of course, they may refuse to accept the match, but in that case they will be considered defeated, and naturally, both their personal reputation and their family’s reputation will be damaged."
"As you all know, this is a friendly competition, a stage for the young generation to show their talent, and a chance to build their reputation."
Some people smiled, but almost everyone knew that this was only half of the truth.
No one was going to reveal all of their strength in a competition like this.
And the only reason everyone was here was the Heavenly Treasury.
The first person to enter the arena was...
Cassius Vorhelm, and the moment he entered, the entire arena became silent.
The eldest son, the person many believed would become the future heir of the family.
Tall, well dressed, calm, and carrying the confidence that could only be seen in people who had spent years preparing to rule.
Without wasting any time, he chose his opponent, a young man around twenty years old.
Strangely, he did not choose a powerful opponent.
First his level was limited to 20, then the battle began.
And less than one minute later, it ended.
Cassius did not even need to become serious once.
Three moves, three strikes, and a complete victory.
Cheers filled the arena.
But Lian only watched, analyzing, the movements, the speed, the mana control, the fighting style, he stored everything in his mind.
After that it was Isabella’s turn, then Evangelin, then Adrian, and Aron.
Each of them showed their strength.
Isabella was precise and ruthless.
Evangelin’s magic was fast and impossible to predict.
Adrian also showed skill far beyond his age.
But what caught Lian’s attention was not the battles themselves, but the choices.
Almost every member of the family was choosing weaker opponents, and even stranger, some specific people were still untouched.
At first it looked like a coincidence, but as time passed, the pattern became clearer.
They were removing the weaker participants.
They were organizing the battlefield, preparing the stage for something bigger, as if they wanted to make sure Lian would have no choice except to fight the strongest outsider.
Lian smiled calmly.
So this was the plan they had prepared against him.
Several more battles took place, until finally a name was announced that caught everyone’s attention.
Lucas Vorhelm.
The arena suddenly became silent, and the next moment, a man entered the arena who looked more like a human monster than an ordinary Awakened.
Tall, broad shoulders, muscles that could be seen even under his clothes, there was no elegance in him.
Everything about him screamed: warrior.
After Diana, he was the newest genius of the Vorhelm family to become famous during the past two years, and he had a great future ahead of him.
A smile appeared on his face, a smile that looked nothing like a friendly one.
Then he raised his head and looked toward the participants’ area.
His eyes passed over several people, over Lian, over Adrian, over the others, and finally stopped on a girl with silver eyes.
Seris Pendragon.
For one short moment... complete silence filled the arena.
Then Lucas said in a loud voice,
"I’ve chosen my opponent."
Everyone was waiting, even the family elders were watching him.
Lucas raised his hand and pointed directly toward the Pendragon family’s area.
"Seris Pendragon."
For one second... nobody said anything.
Then... the entire arena exploded.
Even some of the elders could not hide their reactions.
Lucas Vorhelm...
One of the strongest young members of the family... instead of choosing an easy opponent... had chosen one of the most famous geniuses of the country’s new generation.
And in the middle of all that noise...
Lian only looked at Seris, the girl who was sitting several rows away, and for the first time since she had arrived here, a very faint smile could be seen on her lips.
It was as if she had been waiting for exactly this.
That she could finally fight!

chapters.title: Chapter 114: The Duels II
paragraphs: For a few seconds after Lucas made his choice, a strange silence covered the entire stadium.
Then suddenly, an explosion of voices began, the noise of the crowd rose like a huge wave from every direction.
"Has he gone crazy?!"
"That’s Seris Pendragon!"
"Why would he choose an opponent like that?"
"He could have easily gone to the next round!"
"He’s destroying himself!"
Tens of thousands of people were talking at the same time, even many of the foreign guests could not hide their surprise.
Lucas Vorhelm was one of the stars of the younger generation of the family.
A monster who had gained a great reputation over the past two years.

Because he was neither a direct child of the Patriarch nor a member of the main branch, but came from one of the side branches, his rise had attracted a lot of attention both inside and outside the family.
But now, everyone was sure that he had made the wrong decision.
The problem was that his opponent was Seris Pendragon.
A girl whose name had spread among the younger generation like a living legend.
In the elders’ section, many looks were exchanged between the family members.
Some were frowning, some were surprised, and some looked completely unhappy, it was clear that this was not an order they had given Lucas.
Celestia only stared at the arena.
Her face looked calm, but behind that calmness, clear dissatisfaction was hidden.
On the other side, Damian looked at the arena with an amused expression.
"This kid has really lost his mind."
But unlike his words, a small smile could be seen at the corner of his lips.
Nearby, Diana was also looking at the arena with worry.
She had heard about Seris’s strength, but hearing about it and seeing it were two different things.
Until now, most of the winners had been young members of the Vorhelm family, and Lucas was a great talent.
They were worried that if he lost, it would affect the family’s reputation.
Among everyone present, the calmest person was Lian.
He only looked at Seris, and he knew that this choice...was a very big mistake.
Everyone waited for Seris’s reaction.
Seris slowly stood up.
She turned her neck left and right, the quiet sound of her joints could be heard in the silence around her.
Then without the smallest change in her expression, she said,
"So someone finally showed up."
Even the crowd forgot to speak for a few moments.
Lucas was standing in the arena.
One of the strongest fighters of the younger generation of the Vorhelm family.
But in Seris’s eyes...he looked like nothing more than an ordinary opponent.
A few seconds later, Seris entered the arena.
Her steps were calm.
She was not in a hurry, and she was not excited.
There was not even the smallest sign of tension in her body.
She walked with her usual calmness to the center of the arena.
Many Awakened of the older generation unconsciously stared at her.
There was something strange about this girl.
Not her mana, not the pressure of her presence, but her calmness.
It was as if she had not entered a battlefield, it was as if she had entered the yard of her own home.
If they knew this girl’s personality, they would understand why they felt that way.
"Looks like everyone thinks I’m going to lose."
Lucas looked at her and said with sarcasm.
"I guess."
Seris shrugged, clearly not caring.
"Today I’ll prove they’re wrong, I’ll prove that I deserve it more than all of the Patriarch’s children, and I’ll prove that I have enough talent to lead the family!"
He continued in an arrogant tone.
"Can we just start?"
Seris did not care about his nonsense.
The veins on Lucas’s forehead bulged.
This was the first time he had met someone who looked down on him like this.
He had to make sure to teach her a good lesson.
"Begin!
As soon as the referee announced it, Lucas moved immediately.
Despite his rough appearance, his speed was extremely high.
The ground under his feet cracked.
The distance between them disappeared almost in the blink of an eye.
His huge fist flew toward Seris with a sound like exploding air.
The crowd held their breath.
But Seris only took half a step back.
The fist passed beside her face.
Lucas continued.
Second punch.
Third punch.
Fourth punch.
Every one of them could have shattered concrete walls.
But none of them hit their target.
Seris only dodged.
Calmly and accurately, without even a single unnecessary movement.
A few minutes passed.
Lucas kept attacking.
But he still could not touch her even once.
Slowly, the smiles returned to the crowd.
"Maybe he actually has a chance."
"At least he’s holding on."
"Lucas still isn’t serious."
But Lian only shook his head.
They were wrong.
Completely wrong.
Suddenly, Seris stopped.
For the first time, she did not step back anymore.
She did not dodge anymore.
Lucas smiled.
He thought he had finally found his chance.
He clenched his fist, and every muscle in his body tightened.
Then he threw his final punch.
At that exact moment...Seris moved.
Only one step.
Only one strike.
The sound of the collision echoed across the entire arena.
An explosion of air shook the area around them.
Then...Lucas’s body was thrown backward like a fired bullet.
Three meters.
Five meters.
Eight meters.
Finally, he crashed onto the ground with great force.
The sound of breaking bones could be heard clearly.
Lucas’s face twisted in pain.
Blood flowed from the corner of his mouth.
For the first time...his smile disappeared.
In the audience, many people had stood up.
Their eyes were wide with disbelief.
"What...?"
"It was only one strike!"
"That’s impossible!"
Even some of the family elders were shocked.
But Lian only looked at the arena calmly.
He knew the truth better than anyone.
Seris had not even become serious yet.
This was not even close to her real strength.
She had deliberately limited herself.
Inside the Ruined Realm, Lian had seen a version of this girl who could cut down deadly monsters like weeds.
What everyone was seeing in the arena now...was only a shadow of that power.
After that strike, the battle was practically over.
Lucas stood up again.
He tried to attack.
But this time, the difference in strength was completely clear.
Every attack was stopped.
Every movement was read.
Every attempt was useless.
A few minutes later...he fell to the ground for the third time.
This time, he could not stand up anymore.
"The winner...Seris Pendragon!"
The referee announced immediately.
No one cheered.
No one shouted.
Everyone only stared.
They had expected an amazing battle.
They knew Seris would win, but not this easily.
A tense fight.
But what they had seen...was a one-sided slaughter.
A complete defeat.
A complete humiliation.
"How boring, I thought the Vorhelms had good fighters...maybe Lian is an exception?"
Without the smallest change in her expression, Seris left the arena.
It was as if nothing special had happened.
She returned to her seat.
She sat down.
She quietly looked at the arena.
That was all.
But the Vorhelm family did not have that calmness.
They had been humiliated.
Right in front of tens of thousands of spectators.
The first round continued.
But now the situation had changed.
The remaining members of the Vorhelm family no longer chose strong opponents.
One after another, each of them chose the weakest opponent possible.
Easy victories.
Short battles.
Battles with no excitement.
Because of that, the crowd began to mock them.
"So this is the great family?"
"They got scared after Seris?"
"None of them dares to fight a real opponent."
"And the Heavenly Treasury is for them?"
The faces of many family elders became uglier and uglier.
It was not that they chose weak opponents because they were afraid.
They simply had no choice...because the Matriarch had ordered all the weak opponents to be eliminated.
During these battles, two more members of the family were also defeated.
Three people won.
Slowly...the number of participants became smaller and smaller.
Until finally...only one name remained.
One of the family elders stood up and the stadium became quiet, everyone’s eyes turned toward him.
The old man looked at the list, then he announced in a loud voice,
"It is now...Lian Vorhelm’s turn."
A heavy silence covered the entire stadium.
Thousands of eyes...all focused on one person at the same time.
Lian.
