chapters.title: Chapter 115: The Duels III
paragraphs: After Lian’s name was announced, the noise in the stadium became noticeably quieter.
Tens of thousands of people were sitting on the stone and metal seats around the arena, but at that moment, almost every gaze was focused on only one person.
Lian Vorhelm, the exiled son of the family, the hero of the Border City, and the biggest question mark in this competition.
Everyone was waiting to see who he would choose, but it quickly became clear that there was no choice.
Because only one person was left, a young man with dark hair and gray eyes who was standing on the contestants’ platform and calmly watching the arena.
Darius Blackthorn, the second son of the Blackthorn Family, one of the six great families of the world.
Unlike many of the young people present, who had spent most of their lives in academies and training centers, Darius had spent a large part of his youth on real battlefields.
He was eighteen years old, Level nineteen, and had a reputation earned through blood and battle.
Among the younger generation, his name had been mentioned many times alongside operations to clear corrupted areas and hunt high-level monsters.
He even had his own title, the White Lion, a title he earned after one of his famous operations, an operation where he almost wiped out an entire monster pack by himself.
Before the competition began, many believed that if the strongest foreign guest in this tournament had to be named, that person would be Darius.
But until now, he had not fought even a single battle.
Because the members of the Vorhelm Family, knowingly or unknowingly, had arranged the tournament in a way that left him untouched until the end of the first round.
Lian’s gaze stopped on the elders’ platform for a moment, several of them immediately looked away.
That was enough, he understood everything.
First, the weak participants had been eliminated, then the troublesome ones had been removed, and now the only opponent left was Darius Blackthorn.
If Lian wanted to enter the second round, he had to get past this obstacle, he laughed to himself.
"So much effort for this?" But this made him look at the current leadership of the family with complete contempt.
These idiots let the family become the laughingstock of everyone just because Celestia wanted to eliminate him? He had never seen such a level of weakness and helplessness.
If the Vorhelm Family kept going like this, they might soon lose the title of one of the strongest families, and after another century, no one might even remember their name.
The whispers of the crowd became louder again.
"He’s unlucky."
"This is where it ends."
"Darius has much more experience."
"Talent is important, but real battle experience is something else."
"The Border City is one thing, facing Darius is another."
"Besides, Darius has very high talent too, did you forget? He has a four-star class."
Almost no one was talking about Lian winning.
The only question was how long he would last.
One minute?
Three minutes?
Maybe five minutes?
It was not that they thought he was weak, they just did not think it was possible to close the gap between the two.
At the Pendragon Family’s platform, Aurelia Pendragon calmly looked at the arena, the same smile was still on her face.
Beside her, Seris was sitting on her seat and staring at the arena.
"How long do you think it will take?" Aurelia asked without taking her eyes off the arena.
Seris did not answer.
"I mean, how long will Lian last?" Aurelia asked again.
A few seconds of silence passed, then Seris said in a completely normal voice.
"I don’t know."
"What?" Aurelia raised an eyebrow.
"I don’t know, because Lian will win easily.
For the first time since the ceremony had started, the smile on Aurelia’s face slightly shook, she was truly surprised.

"Are you sure? The experience gap is huge, there is also a level gap, that boy has fought for years, his family is one of the six great families like ours, and they are almost always fighting monsters on the Fallen Continent."
"If this fight lasts more than one minute, I will be surprised." Seris only shrugged, her opinion was firm.
Aurelia stared at her for a few seconds, then looked back at the arena, this was the first time she had doubted her own judgment.
At the center of the arena, Darius calmly walked in, with every step he took, the mana pressure around him became stronger.
The air around him seemed heavier, unlike Lucas, there was no pride or carelessness on his face.
He was serious, completely serious, because he knew who was standing in front of him.
Even if he did not believe Lian was stronger than him, he knew that he should never underestimate him.
As a soldier, he had learned since childhood to never underestimate his enemies.
On the opposite side, Lian calmly walked into the arena.
He did not release any mana pressure, he did not put on any show, he did not even look at the crowd, he simply walked into the arena.
That was all.
The two looked at each other, but neither of them said anything.
They had nothing to say, both of them were the type of people who preferred silence.
The referee stood between them.
A few seconds of silence passed, then he lowered his hand.
"Begin!"
Almost at the same moment, the ground under Darius exploded.
A wave of mana spread around him, his speed increased explosively, the crowd could only see a shadow.
He charged straight at Lian.
Without a word, without a warning, without testing him, he released all of his power from the very beginning.
Only one thought appeared in the minds of most of the spectators.
The battle had begun.
But in reality... the battle ended at that very moment.
Lian only took one step forward.
No complicated technique was activated, no legendary skill, no mana explosion, only one simple movement.
One punch, a direct, simple, and merciless punch.
The moment they collided.
BOOM!
A deafening sound shook the entire arena, the shockwave spread through the whole stadium like a storm.
The air split apart, the ground under Lian cracked, and Darius... disappeared.
Or at least, that was how it looked to many of the spectators.
His body was thrown backward like a cannonball.
Ten meters.
Twenty meters.
Thirty meters.
And in the end, he crashed into the protective wall of the arena with terrifying force.
Silence... complete silence filled the entire place... tens of thousands of people could only stare, no one understood what had happened.
Everyone was in shock, shocked because they did not understand what had just happened.
A few seconds passed, and the referee walked toward Darius.
He checked his pulse, fortunately, he was still alive.
The referee stayed silent for a moment, then turned around and loudly announced.
"The winner... Lian Vorhelm."
The silence continued, then suddenly the entire stadium exploded with noise.
"What?!"
"It’s over?"
"Darius couldn’t even defend himself!"
"I didn’t even see his movement!"
"What was that?!"
Several generals had stood up, some politicians looked at the arena in disbelief, the elders of the different families were no longer calm.
Even the expressions of some of them had turned pale.
At the Vorhelm Family’s platform, Damian laughed loudly, a laugh that was completely different from the shocked atmosphere around him.
He knew something like this could happen, but even he had not expected it to be this one-sided.
On the other side, for the first time, Celestia truly lost control of her expression.
Only for a moment, but that one moment was enough.
Her face completely twisted.
’Damn it!’
If she could, she would tear Darius apart with her own hands right now.
Why was that trash so useless?
Beside her, Diana could not hide her smile, her eyes were shining.
At the Pendragon platform, Aurelia was still silent, then after a few seconds she turned her head toward Seris.
A few seconds later, she turned her head toward Seris.
"You already knew."
"Yeah." Seris nodded.
"And how did you know?"
"A warrior’s instinct."
Aurelia stayed silent.
For the first time during this entire ceremony, she was truly surprised.
Darius was not weak.
He was definitely weaker than Seris, but he was not weak.
He was not someone who could be defeated this easily.
In fact, this was beyond easy, Lian had practically one-shotted him.
Aurelia could not believe that such a genius had been abandoned by the Vorhelm Family.
"Maybe we should make him a member of our own family?" She looked at Seris.
These two are the same age, right? They would definitely make a great couple!
But then she shook her head.
She doubted that this girl was interested in anything other than fighting.
In the arena, Lian did not even look at Darius.
But he also did not turn around and simply leave.
Instead, with a smile full of mockery, he looked at Celestia and the other young members of the Vorhelm Family.
"Thank you for defeating all the strong opponents, so I could face such a weak opponent this easily and advance to the next round." He said calmly.

sentences.text: After Lian’s name was announced, the noise in the stadium became noticeably quieter.
Tens of thousands of people were sitting on the stone and metal seats around the arena, but at that moment, almost every gaze was focused on only one person.
Lian Vorhelm, the exiled son of the family, the hero of the Border City, and the biggest question mark in this competition.
Everyone was waiting to see who he would choose, but it quickly became clear that there was no choice.
Because only one person was left, a young man with dark hair and gray eyes who was standing on the contestants’ platform and calmly watching the arena.
Darius Blackthorn, the second son of the Blackthorn Family, one of the six great families of the world.
Unlike many of the young people present, who had spent most of their lives in academies and training centers, Darius had spent a large part of his youth on real battlefields.
He was eighteen years old, Level nineteen, and had a reputation earned through blood and battle.
Among the younger generation, his name had been mentioned many times alongside operations to clear corrupted areas and hunt high-level monsters.
He even had his own title, the White Lion, a title he earned after one of his famous operations, an operation where he almost wiped out an entire monster pack by himself.
Before the competition began, many believed that if the strongest foreign guest in this tournament had to be named, that person would be Darius.
But until now, he had not fought even a single battle.
Because the members of the Vorhelm Family, knowingly or unknowingly, had arranged the tournament in a way that left him untouched until the end of the first round.
Lian’s gaze stopped on the elders’ platform for a moment, several of them immediately looked away.
That was enough, he understood everything.
First, the weak participants had been eliminated, then the troublesome ones had been removed, and now the only opponent left was Darius Blackthorn.
If Lian wanted to enter the second round, he had to get past this obstacle, he laughed to himself.
"So much effort for this?" But this made him look at the current leadership of the family with complete contempt.
These idiots let the family become the laughingstock of everyone just because Celestia wanted to eliminate him?
He had never seen such a level of weakness and helplessness.
If the Vorhelm Family kept going like this, they might soon lose the title of one of the strongest families, and after another century, no one might even remember their name.
The whispers of the crowd became louder again.
"He’s unlucky."
"This is where it ends."
"Darius has much more experience."
"Talent is important, but real battle experience is something else."
"The Border City is one thing, facing Darius is another."
"Besides, Darius has very high talent too, did you forget?
He has a four-star class."
Almost no one was talking about Lian winning.
The only question was how long he would last.
One minute?
Three minutes?
Maybe five minutes?
It was not that they thought he was weak, they just did not think it was possible to close the gap between the two.

Beside her, Seris was sitting on her seat and staring at the arena.
"How long do you think it will take?" Aurelia asked without taking her eyes off the arena.
Seris did not answer.
"I mean, how long will Lian last?" Aurelia asked again.
A few seconds of silence passed, then Seris said in a completely normal voice.
"I don’t know."
"What?" Aurelia raised an eyebrow.
"I don’t know, because Lian will win easily.
For the first time since the ceremony had started, the smile on Aurelia’s face slightly shook, she was truly surprised.
"Are you sure?

The experience gap is huge, there is also a level gap, that boy has fought for years, his family is one of the six great families like ours, and they are almost always fighting monsters on the Fallen Continent."
"If this fight lasts more than one minute, I will be surprised." Seris only shrugged, her opinion was firm.
Aurelia stared at her for a few seconds, then looked back at the arena, this was the first time she had doubted her own judgment.
At the center of the arena, Darius calmly walked in, with every step he took, the mana pressure around him became stronger.
The air around him seemed heavier, unlike Lucas, there was no pride or carelessness on his face.
He was serious, completely serious, because he knew who was standing in front of him.
Even if he did not believe Lian was stronger than him, he knew that he should never underestimate him.
As a soldier, he had learned since childhood to never underestimate his enemies.
On the opposite side, Lian calmly walked into the arena.
He did not release any mana pressure, he did not put on any show, he did not even look at the crowd, he simply walked into the arena.
That was all.
The two looked at each other, but neither of them said anything.
They had nothing to say, both of them were the type of people who preferred silence.
The referee stood between them.
A few seconds of silence passed, then he lowered his hand.
"Begin!"
Almost at the same moment, the ground under Darius exploded.
A wave of mana spread around him, his speed increased explosively, the crowd could only see a shadow.
He charged straight at Lian.
Without a word, without a warning, without testing him, he released all of his power from the very beginning.
Only one thought appeared in the minds of most of the spectators.
The battle had begun.
But in reality... the battle ended at that very moment.
Lian only took one step forward.
No complicated technique was activated, no legendary skill, no mana explosion, only one simple movement.
One punch, a direct, simple, and merciless punch.
The moment they collided.
BOOM!
A deafening sound shook the entire arena, the shockwave spread through the whole stadium like a storm.
The air split apart, the ground under Lian cracked, and Darius... disappeared.
Or at least, that was how it looked to many of the spectators.
His body was thrown backward like a cannonball.
Ten meters.
Twenty meters.
Thirty meters.
And in the end, he crashed into the protective wall of the arena with terrifying force.
Silence... complete silence filled the entire place... tens of thousands of people could only stare, no one understood what had happened.
Everyone was in shock, shocked because they did not understand what had just happened.
A few seconds passed, and the referee walked toward Darius.
He checked his pulse, fortunately, he was still alive.
The referee stayed silent for a moment, then turned around and loudly announced.
"The winner...
Lian Vorhelm."
The silence continued, then suddenly the entire stadium exploded with noise.
"What?!"
"It’s over?"
"Darius couldn’t even defend himself!"
"I didn’t even see his movement!"
"What was that?!"
Several generals had stood up, some politicians looked at the arena in disbelief, the elders of the different families were no longer calm.
Even the expressions of some of them had turned pale.
At the Vorhelm Family’s platform, Damian laughed loudly, a laugh that was completely different from the shocked atmosphere around him.
He knew something like this could happen, but even he had not expected it to be this one-sided.
On the other side, for the first time, Celestia truly lost control of her expression.
Only for a moment, but that one moment was enough.
Her face completely twisted.
’Damn it!’
If she could, she would tear Darius apart with her own hands right now.
Why was that trash so useless?
Beside her, Diana could not hide her smile, her eyes were shining.
At the Pendragon platform, Aurelia was still silent, then after a few seconds she turned her head toward Seris.
A few seconds later, she turned her head toward Seris.
"You already knew."
"Yeah." Seris nodded.
"And how did you know?"
"A warrior’s instinct."
Aurelia stayed silent.
For the first time during this entire ceremony, she was truly surprised.
Darius was not weak.
He was definitely weaker than Seris, but he was not weak.
He was not someone who could be defeated this easily.
In fact, this was beyond easy, Lian had practically one-shotted him.
Aurelia could not believe that such a genius had been abandoned by the Vorhelm Family.
"Maybe we should make him a member of our own family?" She looked at Seris.
These two are the same age, right?
They would definitely make a great couple!
But then she shook her head.
She doubted that this girl was interested in anything other than fighting.
In the arena, Lian did not even look at Darius.
But he also did not turn around and simply leave.
Instead, with a smile full of mockery, he looked at Celestia and the other young members of the Vorhelm Family.
"Thank you for defeating all the strong opponents, so I could face such a weak opponent this easily and advance to the next round." He said calmly.

chapters.title: Chapter 116: The Duels IV
paragraphs: After hearing Lian’s words, Celestia’s expression became even uglier and more twisted, anyone with common sense could easily understand that this was a huge mockery and humiliation.
Throughout the tournament, the young members of the Vorhelm family had been fighting the weak opponents, and the strongest opponent was left for Lian, unless Seris was counted.
And this boy one-shotted his opponent.
The expressions of the young members and the elders of the Vorhelm family also turned ugly, they could see the mockery on the faces of everyone present, they just did not dare to show it.
"Hahaha, what a bunch of idiots." Only Aurelia laughed without any worry, she was a Pendragon and did not care at all if the Vorhelms became angry.
The more time passed, the more she liked Lian, and the more certain she became that this boy had to become a member of their family.
When was the last time someone humiliated the Vorhelms like this? Even she could not remember.
One of the Vorhelm elders immediately stood up to change the atmosphere, his voice echoed through the entire stadium.
"The second round begins."
But unlike what the organizers expected, the crowd’s attention was not on the second round, instead the entire stadium was still focused on what had happened a few minutes ago.
Lian Vorhelm, the boy whom many believed had become the victim of the elders’ plan, the boy who was supposed to be stopped by Darius Blackthorn.
The boy who was supposed to learn how big the gap between talent and real experience was, and that same boy... defeated Darius with a single punch.
Not a long battle, not an intense fight, not even a full display of his strength, just one punch.
Because of that, almost every conversation in the stadium was about him.
"What’s his real level?"
"The reports said ten."
"That’s nonsense."
"No level ten can defeat Darius like that."
"Maybe his skill is unusual."
"Maybe he has a five-star class."
"Maybe the information that was released was fake."
The army generals were taking notes, the political representatives were quietly discussing with each other, and the representatives of the great families were sending messages to their own people.
Almost everyone was gathering information, and the center of all those discussions was only one person, Lian Vorhelm.
The boy who was the biggest question mark at this event, the boy who had stolen all the attention since last night, and the more time passed, the more interested everyone became in him.
In the special seats of the Vorhelm family, the atmosphere was completely different, some of the elders were openly happy.
"After all, he is a member of our family." One of them said with a smile.
"His victory increases the family’s reputation."
"Reputation? Or trouble? If his strength keeps growing like this, the entire balance of the family will be destroyed." A man from the northern branch immediately replied.
"He just humiliated all of us!"
Several others also nodded and agreed.

That was exactly the problem, if Lian was weak, he could be ignored, if he was average, he could be controlled, but if he was really as strong as some people were guessing... then it would no longer be possible to ignore him so easily.
For the first time in many years, the disagreement between the different branches of the family had become clear.
Celestia sat silently in her seat, her face looked calm, she had finally managed to calm herself down.
But only those who had known her for many years could understand what kind of storm was hidden behind that calm face.

She had never expected Lian to win, at least not like this, not with such a huge gap, not with such obvious humiliation, and he had clearly understood their plan and humiliated all of them in front of everyone.
She was sure that that bitch, her husband’s first wife, was definitely laughing right now.
"What do we do?" A middle-aged man from her allied branch quietly asked beside her.
Celestia stayed silent for a few seconds and kept her eyes on the arena, then she quietly said.
"We can’t let him reach the Heavenly Treasury."
"Do you really think he can win?" The middle-aged man was silent for a moment.
Celestia did not take her eyes off the arena.
"I don’t know, but I don’t want to take the risk." For the first time, real worry could be heard in her voice.
The second round began.
Now there were far fewer participants left, the people who remained were no longer weak, each of them had already earned at least one victory today.
And this time they had to choose from among each other, they had to choose their own opponent, and if the other side agreed, the battle would take place.
At that moment everyone waited to see who would dare to say Lian’s name.
But no one did it, not one person, not two, not three, every time it was someone’s turn to choose, their eyes would move toward Lian for a moment.
And then they immediately looked away.
It was as if no one wanted to be the first person to stand against him again.
The strength he had shown was enough to turn him into a terrifying monster that no one dared to face.
Lian quietly watched this scene, before the battle against Darius, the looks around him had been completely different.
At that time he had only been a rumor, the exiled son, the hero of the border city, and an interesting topic for discussion, but now... he had become a real threat.
Even those who had looked at him with mockery before no longer said anything, fear could be seen on some of their faces, and Lian found that interesting.
Because he himself had done nothing, he had only thrown one punch.
"That woman must be going crazy right now, right?" He laughed as he thought about Celestia’s face, but he did not lower his guard, that woman would definitely try something else to stop him.
The first important battle of the second round began.
Cassius Vorhelm entered the arena, the Patriarch’s eldest son and one of the main candidates to win the tournament, he chose his opponent without any delay.
Eliza.
The young girl who had mocked Lian together with Adrian yesterday.
The battle was short but beautiful, Eliza showed considerable resistance, but in the end the gap between the two of them was simply too large.
Cassius won.
After that, Evangelin entered the arena, the girl whom many considered one of the most talented children of the Patriarch.
She chose one of the foreign guests, the battle lasted a little longer, but the result was no different, Evangelin also won.
One after another, the participants were eliminated, and the number of people left became smaller and smaller.
But throughout all of this, one thing was completely clear, everyone was avoiding Lian, it was as if he had become invisible, or maybe the opposite, he was being seen too much.
Time passed.
Another battle ended.
Then the next battle.
Little by little, the number of remaining participants became so small that there were no longer many choices left.
Among them, Adrian was still standing, his face looked calm, but inside he was not calm, he knew what order he had received.
From the very beginning, even before the tournament had started, if he got the chance, he had to fight Lian.
He had to do everything he could to eliminate him.
Now that moment had arrived.
Adrian stepped into the arena.
The stadium became quiet.
Everyone waited for his choice.
He looked at the remaining participants.
Then his eyes stopped on two people.
Seris Pendragon.
And Lian Vorhelm.
A few seconds of silence passed.
Seris looked at him without any emotion.
Lian also stood there calmly, as if the result did not matter to him.
Adrian took a deep breath and made his decision.
"I’ve chosen my opponent."
The entire stadium became silent.
Then he raised his hand and pointed directly at Lian.
"Lian Vorhelm."
A heavy wave of whispers spread through the crowd.
Some people were surprised.
Some smiled.
Some immediately understood that this choice was probably not random.
But everyone looked at him as if they were looking at an idiot, because there was no way this boy could win against Lian.
Lian raised his head.
His eyes stopped on Adrian.
For a few seconds, neither of them said anything.
Then... for the first time since the tournament had begun, a small smile appeared on Lian’s face.
It was not a smile of mockery.
It was not a smile of pride.
It was like someone who had finally found what he had been waiting for, as if after all this time... someone had finally dared to stand in front of him.
And fortunately, that person was someone he had wanted to teach a lesson to for many years, and now he had finally found the chance.
At that exact moment, the referee’s voice echoed through the entire stadium.
"Lian Vorhelm, do you accept this battle?"
"I accept."
"Then the next battle... will be between Adrian Vorhelm and Lian Vorhelm."

chapters.title: Chapter 117: The Duels V
paragraphs: This time, unlike the battle against Darius, the atmosphere of the arena was different.
Heavier, colder, and stranger, because this time Lian’s opponent was someone he knew very well.
And he knew his opponent as well... Adrian Vorhelm, one of the young members of the family, a boy who had spent years using his position and talent to humiliate others.
And among everyone who had looked down on Lian when they were children, he had been one of the most active.
When his name was announced as Lian’s opponent, he kept his smile, even yesterday he had tried to cause trouble for him.
Lian was an extremely vengeful person, the chance that he would give up on revenge was lower than zero.
In the previous battle, after he won, he could have simply returned to his seat without humiliating Celestia.
But did he let it go?
Of course not.
He made sure to repay the plan that had been prepared against him, and now the situation was no different.
He walked into the arena.
Scattered applause could be heard, but no one was as excited as before, not after what Lian had done to Darius.
Because everyone already knew the result of the duel.
Adrian stood there, clenched his fists, and fixed his eyes on Lian.
For a brief moment, old memories passed through his mind.
Many years ago.
Back when Lian still lived in the family, back when everyone believed his future was over, and Adrian had been one of the people who enjoyed that the most.
But now... the same boy he had laughed at was standing in front of him, and for the first time in his life, Adrian felt fear.
Fear of losing... fear that after his defeat, he would be the one everyone laughed at.
"Are you scared? Don’t worry, I’ll finish it in one hit, although it will be a painful hit." Lian laughed when he saw his face.
"Shut up! What makes you think you’re going to win? No matter what happens, I’ll be the winner!" Adrian growled coldly.

"Calm down, save your energy, you’ll need it after the battle when the whole family throws you away like a piece of trash, so you can at least become someone’s dog by licking their boots and continue your miserable life."
"Bastard, I’ll kill you with my own hands!"
"Start!"
As soon as the referee gave the signal, mana exploded out of Adrian’s body.
A strong wind covered the arena, the veins on his arm swelled, and his skill activated.
His body shot forward like an arrow, everyone understood, he had put everything on the line from the very beginning.
There was no testing, no caution, nothing held back, he was practically attacking with the intention to kill.
His speed reached its peak, he crossed the distance in the blink of an eye.
In the guest seats, several people nodded.
"Good."
"At least this one is serious."
"Maybe he can last a few minutes."
But Lian did not even move.
He only watched, calm, indifferent, as if there was no battle happening at all.
When Adrian came within a few meters... Lian finally moved.
Just one step, one simple movement, without any extra motion and without any display, and then... he threw his fist forward.
[ Glacial Reaper Claw ]
His hand suddenly turned into a deadly and destructive ice claw, the air became several degrees colder, and Adrian felt a freezing cold run through his entire spine.
Lian did not need to activate this skill at all...
But why not?
The attack landed.
BOOOOOOM!!
The explosion from the impact shook the entire arena, the air rippled, dust rose from the ground, Adrian’s body was thrown into the air like a lifeless doll.
Ten meters.
Twenty meters.
Thirty meters.
And then he crashed heavily into the protective wall of the arena, but it seemed that the wall was not strong enough, and a huge dent appeared in it.
The sound of the impact echoed through the entire stadium.
Silence... once again that same silence.
No one said a word.
This time it was not even shock.
Only acceptance.
Acceptance of the fact that Lian was on another level.
But everyone looked at each other with concern, if this continued, with the strength they had just seen, no one would be able to stop this boy.
The greatest geniuses of their families were not here, most of them had gone to the Ruined Realm.
The people here were mostly the second or third children.
But at this rate, sooner or later this boy would face the greatest geniuses of their families and organizations.
They had to do something about this.
They had to warn those geniuses...
Or if necessary, they would have to eliminate this monster before he fully matured.
The referee walked over and checked Adrian’s condition.
"My God... take him to the medical center right now!"
He was shocked after checking his body.
Every bone in his body had been broken, his internal organs had been torn apart, and he was no different from a dead man who could still breathe.
The guards immediately carried Adrian to the medical center.
Then the referee raised his hand.
"The winner... Lian Vorhelm."
Scattered applause began, but most people only watched.
On the Vorhelm side, several people sighed.
Celestia’s face no longer looked calm.
There was only coldness and indifference, as if a destructive storm was hidden inside her.
But the tournament was not over yet.
The next battle drew everyone’s attention.

Not even once.

chapters.title: Chapter 118: The Duels VI
paragraphs: Six participants remained.
The six people who had reached this stage from among dozens of geniuses, family heirs, and foreign guests.

And what was even more interesting was that among the six participants, only three of them carried the Vorhelm name, and one of them was even an outcast...this was a situation the Vorhelm family had never expected.
They had not planned for outsiders to shine in this event, they wanted their own children to gain honor.
But it seemed fate was not on their side.
Before everyone’s attention turned to the main battles, there was one more match.
Raphael Stormheart against Nova Lionheart.
Two geniuses and two well-known names among the young generation.
When both of them entered the arena, the crowd clapped for them with respect.
Raphael rested his long silver spear on his shoulder, his face was calm, but the desire for battle could be seen in his eyes.
On the other side, Nova stood with red hair and eyes that shined like flames.
The moment the referee announced the start of the battle, the ground beneath them exploded.
Raphael’s spear moved like lightning, every strike cut through the air.
In response, pillars of fire rose from the ground one after another.
The heat of the arena became so high that many people in the front rows had to activate their mana barriers.
Raphael closed the distance several times, his spear passed through walls of fire, but every time Nova answered with another spell.
The battle continued for almost ten minutes.
Finally, when Raphael gathered all of his power into one final strike, Nova smiled.
A huge magic circle appeared behind her, dozens of fire snakes jumped out from it...Raphael managed to destroy several of them, but there were simply too many.
A huge explosion covered the entire arena.
When the smoke disappeared, Raphael was kneeling on one knee, and his spear was lying several meters away on the ground.
The referee raised his hand.
"The winner, Nova Lionheart."

Scattered applause spread through the stadium, but it was not surprising for anyone, these two were well-known rivals and since both of them came from the same country, they competed against each other from time to time.
Their battle was not especially exciting for anyone, and the truth was that most people were thinking about something else.
Everyone was waiting for the next battle.
The battle that everyone had been talking about since the drawing.
Evangelin Vorhelm against Seris Pendragon, a battle between two young princesses, between two beauties from two rival families, a battle between a mage and a swordswoman.
No matter how they looked at it, this battle was perfect.
At the Vorhelm family section, Evangelin was sitting calmly, unlike many of the younger family members, there was no sign of nervousness on her face.
She was one of the greatest geniuses of the family’s new generation, many believed that if Cassius did not exist, she would have been the main heir candidate of the family.
Some of the elders even secretly believed that her talent was greater than Cassius’s.
Of course, this opinion was not shared by everyone, because there was still another child of the Vorhelm family with monstrous talent...but that person was not here today.
On the other side, Seris was sitting in her seat, her silver eyes were calm.
It was as if she was not taking part in a competition at all, as if the result had already been decided long ago.
Aurelia, who was sitting beside her, looked at her for a few moments and then said.
"Are you going to fight seriously this time?"
"It depends, but no." Seris answered without taking her eyes off the arena.
Aurelia smiled, she had known Seris for a long time and knew very well that this answer was never good news for her opponent.
This answer had only one meaning, this girl had absolute confidence that she was much stronger than her opponent.
It looked like the Vorhelm family was going to suffer a little more.
A few minutes later, both of them entered the arena.
The cheers of the crowd reached their highest point, the genius mage of the Vorhelm family against the silver swordswoman of the Pendragon family.
The two looked at each other, they were judging each other, but neither of them spoke, they did not waste their energy on useless words.
The result would speak louder than any words.
The moment the battle started, Evangelin raised her hand.
Dozens of magic circles appeared in the air at the same time, ice spears were fired toward Seris from every direction.
Waves of wind moved behind them and increased their speed many times.
But Seris simply took a step, one step to the right, one step forward and one small turn, every attack passed beside her body.
At first the crowd thought she was just lucky.
But then the second attack came.
The third.
The fourth.
The fifth.
Hundreds of different spells, and every time Seris only walked, as if she already knew every attack path, as if she could see the future, or she was simply so fast that they could not notice it.
A wave of whispers spread among the audience.
"What...?"
"How is this possible?"
"She’s not even defending."
At the foreign guests’ section, several people looked at each other in surprise.
Even some family elders slowly frowned, this battle was very important, because it was a battle against their greatest rival family.
They could not lose no matter what.
Evangelin realized it as well, she could not land even one effective hit, for the first time, real seriousness appeared on her face.
Mana burst out from her body, the air in the arena suddenly froze and white clouds formed in the sky, then hundreds of ice blades appeared from every direction.
The ground cracked and a layer of ice covered the whole arena, a huge storm of snow and ice appeared.
The crowd exploded.
"It’s her main spell!"
"That’s the Ice Storm!"
"It’s over!"
Even several Vorhelm elders smiled.
But at that moment...for the first time, Seris placed her hand on the handle of her sword.
The sound of metal echoed through the air and the silver sword left its sheath, a cold light flowed across its blade, for one moment, even the ice storm seemed weaker.
Seris took one calm breath.
Then she moved her sword, only once, only one simple slash, and because of it there was no huge explosion, no shout, no legendary skill.
Only one simple slash.
But in the next moment...the entire storm was cut apart, hundreds of ice blades were split in half, Evangelin’s spells broke apart and the ground of the arena cracked.
And when everyone could see again...the blade of the sword was resting against Evangelin’s throat.
Complete silence filled the arena...no one spoke, no one could speak because of the shock, not even Evangelin herself, her eyes were still open.
It was as if her mind could not understand what had happened, she blinked once, then slowly looked at the sword and then at Seris and understood.
She had lost, completely, without even realizing how.
Was the gap between them really that big? But how...they did not even have a big age difference...then what was the reason for such a huge difference in strength?
"The winner...Seris Pendragon." the referee announced in a heavy voice.
This time the stadium reacted differently, no one clapped, no one shouted, everyone only watched.
"How old is this girl?" one of the Vorhelm elders quietly said.
"Where did the Pendragons find a monster like this?" another man beside him whispered.
Damian, who had stayed silent until then, quietly said.
"No...this is not the level of a normal Awakened, our guesses were most likely correct, this girl has a five-star class."
Seris had been under the Vorhelm family’s attention for a long time.
But there was almost no information about this girl, and the Pendragons protected her like a treasure.
The Vorhelms had guessed that this girl had a five-star class, and now it seemed they were right.
Damian secretly looked at Celestia with a mocking smile, her face looked uglier and angrier than ever, this event was her responsibility.
And now the Vorhelm family was being humiliated in this event, and the more the Vorhelms suffered, the more Celestia would have to answer for it after this event.
No matter how much power and influence she had, her power was not absolute, and maybe this would finally become the chance to pull her down.
On the other side, Aurelia was smiling, a smile that showed she was enjoying the shocked faces of everyone.
Many people present realized that Lian was not the only problem in this competition, Seris was also a monster who had destroyed all of their calculations.
After the battle ended, only four people remained.
Lian Vorhelm, Cassius Vorhelm.
Seris Pendragon.
Nova Lionheart.
The atmosphere inside the stadium had completely changed, no one was talking about the previous battles anymore.
Not about Raphael.
Not about Evangelin.
Not even about Darius.
Everyone only had one topic.
The battle between two brothers...the heir candidate of the family, against the exiled son.
At the Vorhelm family section, Cassius stood up.

This time there was no smile on his face, no pride, no clear mockery, only seriousness, he had received orders from the two women at the top of the family that he had to win this battle no matter what, otherwise he would be punished.

He could not understand why his mother and stepmother kept making mistakes, then instead of cleaning up their own mess, they threw all the responsibility onto his shoulders, and after that they even took out their anger on him.
It only made him even more pissed off, but there was nothing he could say.
He slowly walked toward the arena.
At the same moment, Lian also stood up.
All eyes were fixed on the two of them, thousands of people had even forgotten to breathe.
The referee looked at both of them for a few moments, then took a deep breath and announced in a loud voice that echoed through the entire place.
"The next battle...Cassius Vorhelm...against...Lian Vorhelm...begins."

chapters.title: Chapter 119: The Duels VII
paragraphs: A heavy silence covered the entire stadium.
Dozens of thousands of people were sitting in their seats, but no one spoke, even the sound of the wind could be heard more clearly than the whispers of the crowd at that moment.
Because this was no longer just a battle, this was not only a fight between two members of the Vorhelm family, this was a battle between two different futures.
On one side, the most likely heir of the family, and on the other side, the boy who had been driven out of the family years ago and had now returned like a storm.
When both of them stood in the center of the arena, their eyes locked for a few seconds, many years had passed.
Years in which each of them had walked a different path, years in which they had not seen each other.

Even though they were brothers, they had practically grown up in two different worlds, one had become isolated from childhood because he had no mother and did not have many friends or supporters inside the family.
And the other, because he was the first son, had shined like a star throughout the entire family, everyone liked him and he was always respected and admired.
One was practically cast out of the family after the Awakening process, and the other became the center and core of the family after the Awakening process.
Cassius was the first one to break the silence.
"So, we finally reached this point." His voice was calm, it had neither hostility nor friendliness.
"Looks like it." Lian shrugged.
"To be honest, I never thought you would come back, actually, that you would be able to come back."
"A lot of people thought that, and all of them were wrong." A very faint smile appeared on Lian’s lips.
"Looks like that’s true, no one expected you to suddenly become an Awakened." This time it was Cassius who smiled for a moment, but it disappeared just as quickly.
"How about you surrender? This way the battle will end without you getting hurt." Then he added.
"I would rather lose with honor if I have to lose... and what makes you think you can win?"
"Still as stubborn as ever." Cassius laughed and then became silent.
Both of them knew this conversation could not continue anymore, because what stood between them was years of distance, rivalry, and fate.
At the elders’ platform, one of the old men stood up and his voice echoed through the entire stadium.
"Because of the difference in level, battle restrictions have been applied."
"Cassius Vorhelm’s level has been lowered to Level 15."
"His physical strength, speed, stamina, and mana reserve have been returned to what they were at that level."
The spectators nodded, all of these restrictions had also been used in the previous rounds, and this was fair.
Otherwise, no one from the younger generation here would be able to fight against a Level 41 Awakened.
But the next sentence made everyone frown again.
"However, his combat skills, experience, battle understanding, and the abilities gained from his Evolutions will remain."
Several people looked at each other.
"That’s not a restriction at all, that’s a complete advantage." One of them muttered.
Another one sighed.
"Exactly."
In the arena, Cassius drew his sword, the sound of metal echoed across the entire field.
At that same moment, the referee raised his hand.
"Begin!"
And Cassius disappeared.
He really disappeared.
For many spectators, his body turned into nothing more than a streak of light.
[Heaven Severing Flash]
A skill whose name was famous throughout the entire country.
When they saw him use it, the spectators realized that this boy wanted to end the battle as quickly as possible.
A white flash appeared in the arena, and then the sword appeared directly in front of Lian’s throat.
Just one moment.
Just one moment away from the end of the battle.
But that single moment was enough for the surface of Lian’s skin to suddenly turn into a metallic shine.
[Diamond Skin]
A loud impact echoed through the arena, the entire field shook.
Cassius’ sword struck Lian’s neck, but it could not cut through.
Instead, the shockwave from the impact pushed Lian several steps backward.
The stadium exploded.
"He moved back!"
"Lian was pushed back!"
"For the first time!"

Since the beginning of the tournament, no one had been able to force him to step back, even though they had expected that attack to end the battle, the fact that he had been pushed back was already an achievement.
But Cassius had done it.
And he still did not stop.
His body suddenly disappeared again.
[Void Step]
His image appeared and disappeared all over the arena.
Left... right... above... behind.
He was practically attacking from impossible positions every moment.
His sword filled the arena like a deadly storm, attacks came one after another and did not even give his enemy a chance to breathe.
Lian was forced to defend completely, the sounds of constant clashes echoed one after another, dozens of attacks every second, dozens of deadly angles every second.
Lian had reached a position where he could not simply move forward and throw a punch.
Cassius was truly dangerous and powerful, and it could be said that this was finally the first battle in this tournament that had become a real challenge for Lian.
"Now I understand why they call him the future heir." Aurelia quietly whispered from the guests’ platform.
Even Seris did not take her eyes off the arena, her eyes were shining with excitement, this was one of the coolest battles she had ever seen.
She was feeling jealous of the two of them... she wished she could also have a battle like this.
"I can’t keep going like this." In the arena, Lian took a deep breath and muttered to himself, he needed to leave his defensive position.
Suddenly, purple lightning appeared around his body.
[Thunder Calamity]
The sound of thunder echoed across the entire arena.
Lightning flowed over his skin, but he knew this was not enough, he had to become fast enough to match his opponent.
[Fallen Wolf Speed]
And finally he was able to keep up with Void Step.
The images of both fighters became blurred across the arena.
The spectators could only see lightning explosions and flashes from the sword.
But even so... Cassius still had a slight advantage.
"He’s much better than I thought, how is he this powerful?" He thought to himself.
His younger brother had become much stronger during this time.
Even with all of his experience, he had barely managed to keep his small advantage.
Then, after realizing he had no other choice, he revealed one of his trump cards.
His eyes shined for a moment, the mana around him changed, and the atmosphere of the arena suddenly became heavy.
[Imperial Sword Domain]
An invisible area formed around him, every movement of his sword became faster, every attack angle became more deadly, and every escape path became strangely limited.
Lian immediately felt the change, it was as if the entire arena was helping Cassius.
The sword appeared from every direction, every attack was more accurate than the one before.
A small frown appeared on his face, he still had not removed his enemy’s advantage, and now that advantage had suddenly become even greater?
"Damn it."
At that same moment, a deadly cold spread across the arena.
His hands changed, dark blue ice grew over his skin, and a huge deadly claw was formed.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
Purple lightning flowed across the surface of the ice, two completely different powers stood side by side.
The spectators were so excited by this battle that they could not even breathe.
Cassius attacked.
Lian attacked as well.
The next collision was like the explosion of a bomb.
White light covered the entire arena, the ground split apart, stones were crushed, and part of the arena’s barriers cracked.
The shockwave from the collision even reached the front rows of the spectators.
When the dust disappeared, both of them were still standing.
But now there were several meters between them.
The arena no longer looked like a friendly competition, it looked like a real battlefield... deep cracks could be seen everywhere.
Part of the arena floor had been destroyed, and even some of the protective walls had been damaged.
The stadium fell into complete silence.
No one had expected this.
For the first time, Lian had failed to defeat his opponent within a few seconds, he could no longer almost send his opponent to the afterlife with just one punch.
And Cassius had realized that something was still wrong.
Because despite all this pressure... Lian was still calm.
Still far too calm.
His eyes narrowed.
He clearly understood that this calmness was not normal.
And that could only mean one thing.
Lian still had not used his full power.
’How is this possible? How can he keep up with me? Damn it.’ He grumbled.
At first he thought he could end this battle quickly.
But he had been wrong...
At this rate, he might even be forced to use his other trump cards.
At that very moment, Lian slowly raised his hand.
The mana around him began to tremble.
The atmosphere of the arena changed.
Cassius frowned even more deeply, a frown that showed he had sensed danger.
From the spectators’ platform, Damian stared at the arena without moving his eyes.
The battle was going very differently from what he had expected.
"Battle is finally getting serious..." He quietly muttered.

chapters.title: Chapter 120: Ascended Mana
paragraphs: Lian stood calmly, the purple lightning of Thunder Calamity was still dancing across his body.
The icy claw of Glacial Reaper Claw was extending from his right hand.
On the opposite side, Cassius was still frowning, he was no longer smiling, he no longer looked calm, he had understood.
This battle was not going to be like what he had expected, and that made him angry, he wanted a complete victory.
But at this rate? Something like that was not even close to possible, and he doubted that he could even win unless he made his advantage absolute by using his other trump cards.
A few seconds of silence filled the space between them, Lian did not attack because he was preparing for a devastating attack and needed his mana to recover again.
Cassius was also thinking... thinking about whether he should use that trump card or not... using it would be a great humiliation for himself.
Should he accept humiliation or defeat?
Then he let out a quiet sigh, lowered his sword a little and said.
"I didn’t want to use this."
At that moment... the expressions of several Vorhelm elders suddenly changed, even some of the foreign guests changed their expressions.
"Is he really going to use it?" Damian quietly muttered.
From what was leaking out of Cassius’ body, he could guess what he was about to use, and that was the very reason why he believed Lian could not win.
Celestia, who had been sitting there cold and emotionless until now, finally showed a faint smile after a long time during this tournament, she knew this power.
Everyone knew it.
But no one expected Cassius to use it in a battle like this, in a battle where his opponent had not even passed the First Evolution.
In the center of the arena... the mana around Cassius’ body started to change.
At first it was only a small vibration, then the blue color of his mana slowly disappeared, and was replaced by white and golden light.
A pure and majestic light, a strange pressure suddenly spread across the entire stadium, even the people sitting in the far seats could feel it.
Several people from the younger generation suddenly turned pale and could feel their souls beginning to tremble.
"Ascended Mana..." one of the guests whispered.
"Is he really going to use something like this against someone who has not even reached the First Evolution?" another one said in disbelief.
"How cowardly! Only a loser would do something like this!"
The light around Cassius became brighter every moment.
Until even the air around him started to shake.
"So he really used it... Ascended Mana..." Damian sighed, his guess had been correct.
In the world of the Awakened... after the Second Evolution, people could raise their mana to a higher stage.
Its nature was still mana, but its quality was completely different, like the difference between raw iron and steel, like the difference between a small flame and the sun.
The same fuel for skills, but many times stronger, a fuel that would automatically increase the power of skills several times when used.
And now... Cassius had used it.
He raised his sword, and the pressure of his presence became even heavier than before.
Lian did not take his eyes off the white light.
"So you finally got serious."
A faint smile appeared on his lips.
He had expected that his brother would use Ascended Mana, and there was no worry on his face... he had prepared for a situation like this.
But he was not completely sure either, because he really did not know how powerful Ascended Mana could be... he only knew that this energy was powerful enough to even allow someone to fly.
Cassius did not reply.
The next moment... he disappeared.
The eyes of many spectators widened, because this time even [Void Step] could not be seen.
Even Lian, who had matched his opponent’s speed just a few minutes ago... could not see anything now.
There was only an explosion of light.
And then... the sword.
CLANG!
Lian raised his arm to block the attack no matter which direction it came from, only his instincts and senses allowed him to react now.
The clash happened.
But this time... the sound of the collision was different.
A thin line appeared on his arm.
A drop of blood ran down his skin.
Lian had been injured... while Diamond Skin had protected him from wounds like this the entire time... this time it had failed.
Even he looked at his arm for a few moments.
His face no longer had complete calmness, because he had finally realized that his defense was no longer enough.
On the other side of the arena... Cassius disappeared again.
But this time it was impossible to follow his movement.
The sword appeared from the right.
Lian dodged.
Then from behind.
From above.
From below.
The attacks came down one after another.
Many of them hit him and created many wounds all over his body... but they still had not managed to cut deeply... at least for now.
[Imperial Sword Domain]
The air around the arena began to change.
The pressure of the sword was everywhere, it was as if the whole arena had become Cassius’ personal domain.
Every step Lian took became harder.
Every movement became more restricted.
Several minutes passed and Lian was completely forced into a defensive position.
He could not find any chance to attack.
If he lowered his guard even for one moment, it would practically mean his defeat.
The spectators were stunned.
This was the Cassius everyone knew... the true monster of the younger generation.
But among the crowd... one person showed no reaction.
Seris.
She was only staring at the arena, and Aurelia, who was sitting beside her, noticed a small change.
Seris had leaned forward a little.
Her silver eyes were completely locked onto the arena.
"So you finally found an opponent worth watching?" Aurelia smiled, she thought this girl had become interested in Cassius.
Seris stayed silent for a few seconds, then quietly said.
"No."
Aurelia raised an eyebrow.
If not, then what exactly are you watching?
"I’m just waiting for Lian’s answer."
Seris did not take her eyes off the arena.
Aurelia froze.
This girl still thought that boy would win?
In the arena... Lian took a slow breath.
He had completely understood now.
If he only fought with raw power... there was a chance he would lose.
But the problem was... raw power had never been his greatest strength.
His greatest strength was that he always analyzed.
He started analyzing every movement, every step, every attack angle, every small change in Cassius’ breathing, like a hunter studying the monster in front of him.
This was the only way he could plan a counterattack.
He would only have one chance to attack, and he wanted to use all of his power in that attack.
If that attack failed... he would lose the entire battle.
Slowly... the patterns became clear.
Lian narrowed his eyes.
At that moment... a smile appeared on his face.
Finally, the opportunity had arrived!
Cassius realized it.
Every cell in his body suddenly warned him of danger!
But it was already too late.
Lian raised his left hand.
Then... he poured eighty percent of his remaining mana into that attack.
[Cataclysm Pulse]
BOOOOOOM!!
The ground of the arena exploded.
Hundreds of new cracks appeared across its surface.
A huge shockwave spread in every direction.
The protective walls shook.
But more importantly... Cassius’ Sword Domain cracked for one moment.
That single moment was enough.
[Thunder Calamity]
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
Both skills were activated at the same time.
He poured the remaining twenty percent of his mana into them.
If this failed, everything would be over for him!
"I have no choice!"
When Cassius saw what his opponent was about to do, he did not retreat.
Instead, he used the opportunity to end the battle and attacked.
Lian attacked as well.
The sword and the fist covered in lightning and ice collided with each other, and the sound of a huge explosion shook the entire area.
The shockwave swept across the arena.
Dust covered everything.
For several seconds... no one saw anything.
No one said anything.
Then... the dust disappeared.
Everyone stared.
Cassius was kneeling on one knee.
His breathing had become heavy.
His sword had fallen several meters away.
Ascended Mana had completely disappeared.
In front of him... Lian was still standing.
His clothes were torn.
His body was covered with wounds.
Blood could be seen all over his body.
But he was still standing.
A strange silence filled the arena.
Cassius looked at him for a few moments.
Then... he sighed.
"Looks like I lost... Mother won’t be happy when she hears this."
"It’s not your fault, just tell your mother that Lian is simply too good and too strong."
Lian stayed silent for a few seconds, then spoke calmly and completely naturally.
Cassius stayed silent for a moment.
He had not expected this level of arrogance...
But then he laughed.
The referee took a deep breath.
Then he raised his hand.
"The winner... Lian Vorhelm!"
The entire stadium exploded.
The sound of cheers filled every corner.
But in the middle of all that noise... one person looked as if she was only watching an ordinary scene...
Naturally, it was Seris.
Aurelia looked at the girl in disbelief.
How had she predicted the result so accurately?
Was this also a warrior’s instinct?
But while everyone was cheering, Celestia and her faction looked furious and ugly.
They had been completely defeated.
Even though Cassius was not her son, she still preferred him to win instead of Lian.
She did not want that bastard to win and gain the right to enter the Heavenly Treasury.
But no matter what she did, she had failed to stop him.
"Only three participants remain."
"Lian Vorhelm."
"Seris Pendragon."
"Nova Drakeheart."
"The next battle will be between Seris Pendragon and Nova Drakeheart."
"And the winner... will face Lian Vorhelm in the finals."
Although in everyone’s eyes there was no need for another battle...
Everyone was already certain who would meet in the final.

Slowly... the patterns became clear.
Lian narrowed his eyes.
At that moment... a smile appeared on his face.
Finally, the opportunity had arrived!
Cassius realized it.
Every cell in his body suddenly warned him of danger!
But it was already too late.
Lian raised his left hand.
Then... he poured eighty percent of his remaining mana into that attack.
[Cataclysm Pulse]
BOOOOOOM!!
The ground of the arena exploded.
Hundreds of new cracks appeared across its surface.
A huge shockwave spread in every direction.
The protective walls shook.
But more importantly...
Cassius’ Sword Domain cracked for one moment.
That single moment was enough.
[Thunder Calamity]
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
Both skills were activated at the same time.
He poured the remaining twenty percent of his mana into them.
If this failed, everything would be over for him!
"I have no choice!"
When Cassius saw what his opponent was about to do, he did not retreat.
Instead, he used the opportunity to end the battle and attacked.
Lian attacked as well.
The sword and the fist covered in lightning and ice collided with each other, and the sound of a huge explosion shook the entire area.
The shockwave swept across the arena.
Dust covered everything.
For several seconds... no one saw anything.
No one said anything.
Then... the dust disappeared.
Everyone stared.
Cassius was kneeling on one knee.
His breathing had become heavy.
His sword had fallen several meters away.
Ascended Mana had completely disappeared.
In front of him...
Lian was still standing.
His clothes were torn.
His body was covered with wounds.
Blood could be seen all over his body.
But he was still standing.
A strange silence filled the arena.
Cassius looked at him for a few moments.
Then... he sighed.
"Looks like I lost...
Mother won’t be happy when she hears this."
"It’s not your fault, just tell your mother that Lian is simply too good and too strong."
Lian stayed silent for a few seconds, then spoke calmly and completely naturally.
Cassius stayed silent for a moment.
He had not expected this level of arrogance...
But then he laughed.
The referee took a deep breath.
Then he raised his hand.
"The winner...
Lian Vorhelm!"
The entire stadium exploded.
The sound of cheers filled every corner.
But in the middle of all that noise... one person looked as if she was only watching an ordinary scene...
Naturally, it was Seris.
Aurelia looked at the girl in disbelief.
How had she predicted the result so accurately?
Was this also a warrior’s instinct?
But while everyone was cheering, Celestia and her faction looked furious and ugly.
They had been completely defeated.
Even though Cassius was not her son, she still preferred him to win instead of Lian.
She did not want that bastard to win and gain the right to enter the Heavenly Treasury.
But no matter what she did, she had failed to stop him.
"Only three participants remain."
"Lian Vorhelm."
"Seris Pendragon."
"Nova Drakeheart."
"The next battle will be between Seris Pendragon and Nova Drakeheart."
"And the winner... will face Lian Vorhelm in the finals."
Although in everyone’s eyes there was no need for another battle...
Everyone was already certain who would meet in the final.

chapters.title: Chapter 121: The Final Battle I
paragraphs: The battle between Nova Drakeheart and Seris Pendragon began.
After the intense battle between Lian and Cassius, the atmosphere inside the stadium had become strange.
The excitement was still there, but it was mixed with exhaustion, the spectators had been sitting in their seats for hours.
They had watched dozens of battles.
They had experienced many surprises, and they had seen battles they never thought were possible, battles that had awakened excitement in all of them.
Because of that, they felt that their standards had become much higher, and their expectations had also become much higher.
But they knew this battle would not satisfy them, the winner was already completely obvious, and they were all waiting for the final battle.
Nova Drakeheart walked into the arena with firm steps, red flames danced around her body, and the air around her became noticeably hotter.
Her fire mana spread across the entire arena like a wave of heat, the daughter of the Drakeheart family had not reached this stage without reason.
She was considered one of the greatest talents of the younger generation.
Her magic had proven itself again and again on real battlefields.
But from the very moment the battle started... everything went differently from what everyone expected.
Nova did not waste even a single second, she raised her hands, and one magic circle after another appeared in the air.
The mana became extremely dense.
Then... a sea of fire covered the entire arena.
Huge flaming snakes jumped out from the flames, the sky above the arena became dark, and a rain of burning meteors fell from above.
The power she displayed was truly amazing.
It was clear that she knew what kind of opponent she was facing, and she wanted to finish her enemy with one powerful attack from the very beginning.
But... Seris simply walked, she was not in a hurry, she was not nervous, and she did not even look like someone who was fighting.
She simply kept walking, every time one of the flaming snakes came close to her, her body moved only a few centimeters.
Every time a meteor fell, she stepped out of its path at the very last moment.
It was as if she had already seen the entire battlefield before, as if everything that was going to happen had already been recorded in her mind several seconds earlier.
This made the spectators certain that this had to be a special defensive skill, otherwise there could not be any other explanation.
Slowly, a frown appeared on Nova’s face, she increased the speed of her attacks, and increased the amount of mana.
Hundreds of different spells were fired one after another.
But the result did not change.
Seris kept walking, calm, indifferent, cold and then... for the first time, she slightly raised her silver sword.
Only a little, once again no huge skill was activated, no wave of mana was released, just like every other time, it was only one simple movement.
One step, one slash, and a sharp sound echoed across the entire arena, all of Nova’s magic was split in half.
The flames went out, the meteors were destroyed, and the flaming snakes turned into mana particles.
And in the next moment... the edge of the silver sword was resting against Nova’s throat.
The end.
Less than two minutes.
Silence spread across the entire stadium, no one was shocked anymore, it was as if everyone had already gotten used to it.
Every time they thought they had already seen Seris’ true limit, she proved them wrong once again.
The referee announced her victory.
Nova gave a bitter smile and stepped back, she had not even gotten the chance to show her full strength, but she herself knew better than anyone that the difference between them was simply too great.
Still, it was not that bad, right? At least she had managed to take third place, besides earning everyone’s respect, she could also enter the famous Heavenly Treasury.
Even among the Six Great Families, the Heavenly Treasury was very well known.
And now... only two people remained.
Lian Vorhelm and Seris Pendragon.
Everyone’s eyes were focused only on those two, the generals leaned forward without thinking, and the politicians forgot about the conversations they had not finished.
Even the elders of the great families had become silent.
Because everyone knew... this was the battle they had been waiting for since the beginning of the tournament.
This was once again another battle between the Vorhelms and the Pendragons... would the Pendragons win once again? Or would the Vorhelms win?
The elders of the Vorhelm family were hoping Lian would win, even though he was a rejected son, he was now the only one who could save their honor and reputation.
After both sides rested for a few minutes, the time for the final battle finally arrived.
Seris calmly stood up and returned to the arena, a beautiful and very faint smile could be seen on her face, a smile that looked more like the shadow of an emotion.
At the same moment, Lian also walked into the arena.
The signs of his battle against Cassius could no longer be seen on his body, he had changed his clothes, and the healers had completely healed him.
His mana had fully recovered, and all of his skills could be used again.
When they stood in front of each other, neither of them spoke for several seconds, they only looked at each other, it was more like they did not know what they should say.
Maybe deep inside, both of them had known from the very beginning that they would face each other in the final battle.
The two people who had fought side by side for their lives only a few weeks ago, were now standing against each other.
Then Seris broke the silence.
"I didn’t think it would take this long."
"I also didn’t think you would be this weak, why did you make every battle take so long?" Lian gave a short laugh.
The corner of Seris’ lips moved upward. But this time it was completely clear that she did not like it.
"Weak? This is the first time someone has called me weak, I don’t like it, don’t say it again."
"I’m sorry, I was only joking." Lian raised his hand.
Seris answered calmly.
"It’s fine, but now I won’t show you even the smallest amount of mercy."
Lian smiled, this was exactly the reaction he wanted.
Several people nearby who heard the conversation looked at each other without thinking.
They had a strange feeling, it seemed these two knew each other much better than they had imagined.
In the Pendragon family’s seating area, Aurelia watched them carefully.
Unlike everyone else... she was happy, because she knew Seris better than anyone else, a girl who normally never spoke more than a few words.
A girl who was indifferent to almost everyone, but now... she was talking with someone, she had taken the first step to talk to someone.
She was really talking.
Aurelia smiled softly. Maybe... maybe her plan would work, although convincing the other leaders of the Pendragon family would not be easy.
But at least for the first time, there was hope.
"Then let’s find out who is stronger." Seris never took her eyes off Lian.
Lian nodded.
Even the referee looked nervous, he looked at both of them, then raised his hand.
"Begin."
There was no explosion of mana, no huge skill was activated, no wave of energy was released... only... both of them moved at the same time.
BOOM!
The sound of the collision echoed across the entire stadium like the explosion of a war cannon.
Lian’s fist and Seris’ sword collided in the center of the arena, and a huge shockwave spread in every direction.
The people in the front rows stepped back without thinking, the ground beneath their feet cracked, but neither of them took even a single step backward.
Their eyes locked for a moment and then... both of them smiled.
At last, Seris truly looked happy, at last she could use all of her strength without worrying that she might suddenly and accidentally kill her opponent.
The battle had begun, and neither side had the advantage.
Attack.
Defense.
Attack.
Defense.
Move.
Attack.
Clash.
Their speed was so great that many spectators could only see shadows, the sound of fists and swords colliding echoed through the stadium without stopping.
Every attack was blocked, every defense was broken, but neither of them stepped back.
Even Damian was giving the battlefield his full attention.
"At last... I found one..." he quietly muttered.
"What?" One of the elders beside him frowned.
"Someone who can stand against her." But in the next moment, he sighed.
To be honest, he was not feeling very well, since the beginning of the tournament, he had thought Lian would be eliminated halfway through.
But now? This boy had reached the final.
And with things like this... his chance of becoming the champion was truly high.
"Damn it..." Damian muttered unhappily.
The more he saw Lian’s strength, the more certain he became that they had to bring him back to the family.
Where had all of this power even come from? He was certain that Lian’s class was at least four stars.
Maybe even five stars, but even then it still made no sense, nothing made sense.
How had he even managed to defeat Cassius after he used Ascended Mana?
Could it really be just as he had claimed, that the reason for this strength was his innate skills?
Several minutes passed.
But neither of them had used their main skills yet.
Not Thunder Calamity, not Glacial Reaper Claw, and Seris had also not used her skills.
It was only a pure fight and only experience, it was completely clear that both sides were testing each other, they wanted to see how close or far they were in terms of pure strength.
And during all this time, neither of them had managed to gain even the smallest advantage, it was clear that their raw strength was very close.
In the end, both of them jumped back at the same time, and several meters of distance appeared between them.
The wind passed between them, Seris slightly raised her silver sword, and Lian opened and closed his fist.
At that moment... the mana around both of them began to shake.
The air in the arena became heavy, an invisible pressure spread across the entire stadium.
The spectators once again felt the same excitement they had felt during Lian and Cassius’ battle... even more than before.
Everyone understood one truth, until this moment... neither of them had gotten serious yet.
But now, their evaluation of each other had finally ended... and the battle entered its serious stage.
