chapters.title: Chapter 128: Celestial Treasury IV
paragraphs: Lian stood motionless in front of the stone platform for a few seconds.
His gaze was fixed on the cracked red core, the dark and ominous aura coming from it could not be compared to anything else in the Celestial Treasury.
Even many of the legendary treasures he had seen until this moment seemed insignificant in front of this strange and terrifying aura.

And in terms of destruction and deadliness... the aura of this core had completely destroyed every trace of vitality and life around it, this place was so abandoned that it was like entering a cemetery.
He knew very well what he was facing.
Monsters had cores, and not just one or two, the number of monster cores could reach tens and hundreds, so a simple monster core should not have any special value.
But what was in front of him was a Demon core, which was a completely different matter.
Demon rank monsters were so rare that many awakened ones spent their entire lives without even seeing one.
Those creatures alone could destroy a country, turn entire armies into killing fields, and could bring hell to any place they passed through.
And now the core of one of those creatures was in front of him.
Its value? Probably this core alone, this same cracked core, could be sold for tens and maybe over a hundred million dollars.
But the problem was that Lian did not know what to do with it, he could not use it like a skill book, he could not read it.
He could not wear it, and he could not use it like a weapon.
The only use that came to his mind was selling it, and he had not come here to find something to sell, he had come here to find items to become stronger.
And at first glance, this thing should not be of any benefit to him.
But... why did his entire being want it?
Why did he feel his blood was going crazy in response to this core? Why was every cell in his body screaming to take it?
And more importantly... why did he feel that if he left it behind right now, he would regret it later?
His gaze fell on the core once more.
"Maybe it has to do with my class..." he then whispered quietly.
This was the only option that seemed logical, he still knew almost nothing about his real class.
The system had given no explanation, no book existed about it, and no teacher could be found to teach it.
The only one who could uncover its secret was himself, and it was possible that the core in front of him was important for his class.
But what importance? What use? What benefit could it have?
Lian sighed and then reached out his hand.
"Even if it has no use right now, I will take it." The moment his fingers touched the core, its dark aura intensified for a second, then disappeared, and the core entered his storage space.
At that same moment, the treasury’s voice echoed in his mind.
"An unexpected choice." He felt that voice was truly surprised.
It seemed it did not expect him to take such a useless thing.
In fact, he himself did not expect it either... he could only hope that his intuition was trustworthy.
At that same moment, part of the space began to ripple.
A corridor that did not exist before appeared in front of him, as if the treasury had decided to show him something more.
Lian entered it without hesitation, and the further he went, the heavier the mana pressure became, and the treasures around him became more valuable.
Along the way he passed by items that each could create a legend.
A black spear that was said to have been used by one of the most powerful awakened ones in the history of the Vorhelms.
A skill book whose pages were shining.
A green crystal that could increase a human’s lifespan by dozens of years.
But none of them caught his attention, not like what was waiting for him at the end of the path.
A few minutes later his steps stopped.
In front of him was a corpse, but not the corpse of a human, not even the corpse of a normal monster.
The massive body of a creature whose size was equal to a multi-story building.
Dark skin, massive bones, and muscles that even after death were releasing a terrifying pressure.
"World Devourer Giant..." Lian’s eyes widened slightly, memories from books of the Ruined Realms appeared in his mind.
An ancient race from the fourth Ruined Realm, creatures that grew stronger by swallowing cities.
Monsters that ate civilizations, a monster that was known for having the strongest defense among all the monster races of the fourth Ruined Realm.
A defense that was said to be as strong as the strongest mountains.
The system immediately appeared.
[ World Devourer Giant ]
[ Rank: Unholy ]
[ Level: 77 ]
Lian let out his breath quietly, an Unholy... and not just any Unholy, but a monster that had passed through three evolutions.
If his guess was correct... this creature had been the leader of its entire race.
The body of such a creature was a complete treasure in itself.
Bones, skin, blood, everything had legendary value.

He had seen several incredible armors in the treasury, but he suddenly understood that none of them could compare to this, with the materials from this body, an armor could be made that would last for generations.
An armor that might even reach Ancient rank, which was a full rank above S rank armors.
For someone like him who fought most of his battles at close range, such a thing had indescribable value.
Lian made his second choice without the slightest hesitation, he could find a ready-made armor, but he had not seen any Ancient rank armor here.
Most of the armors were A rank and S rank, and all of them were inferior in every way to an armor that could be made from this monster’s body.
Now only one choice remained, and time was still passing, he only had 3 minutes left.
He continued searching again, he found many skill books, some so powerful that even looking at them was tempting.
But none of them created that strange feeling, until...
he reached an area that was different from all the other sections of the treasury.
The atmosphere there was heavier, quieter, and more importantly... more protected.
"I suggest you choose another path." Even the treasury’s voice seemed to change for the first time, sounding worried.
"A suggestion, or worry that I might take what is here?" Lian stopped and raised an eyebrow.
The treasury’s voice was silent for a few seconds, and that was enough for him to realize that the second option was true.
The treasury’s consciousness was worried, but this only made Lian more curious.
A few minutes later he reached his destination and was stunned by what he saw in front of him.
In front of him was a massive container, a transparent layer that looked like glass, but only its appearance looked like glass.
The pressure coming from it was insane, even without touching it he could tell that this protection could withstand attacks from level eighty awakened ones.
And in its center... a book was floating.
A golden book, a book with thousands of unclear words engraved on its cover, and the moment Lian’s gaze fell on it, the system notification appeared.
[ Celestial Book of Treasure ]
[ Rank: Mythical ]
Lian just stared for a few seconds.
Mythical... the highest possible rank! Higher than anything he had seen until today.
And suddenly... the transparent container opened without any sound, as if the treasury itself had allowed it.

Although that was not really the case... if the treasury’s consciousness had a visible face, one could see how worried and terrified it was right now... terrified that if the elders of the Vorhelm clan found out this book had been taken, how furious they would be.
Lian calmly moved forward and read the system’s description.
[ Celestial Book of Treasure ]
[ Ability: Identify and display all valuable treasures within a ten kilometer radius, display location, description and approximate value of treasures ]
[ One of the five Celestial Books ]
Lian was completely silent for a few seconds, now he understood, this book was the real reason for the formation of the Celestial Treasury.
The Vorhelm clan had probably used it for centuries, this same book was what guided them to hidden treasures.
This same book was what had made such wealth possible.
And now... it had fallen into his hands.
Another notification appeared.
[ Celestial Books: 1/5 ]
Lian’s heart beat faster, so there were four other books as well, and this was only the beginning of the story, he made his choice without the slightest hesitation and took the book.
He was a little curious to know how the clan had found and obtained this book.
And he was also curious to know how shocked they would be when they found out this book had fallen into his hands, they would probably be more terrified, right?
He chuckled inwardly, even he himself had not expected such a book to exist, he had not read about anything like this in any book.
It was not hard to guess that the Vorhelms had probably hidden it as well as possible.

The treasury’s consciousness, seeing that the book had been taken, cursed inwardly, but it could not interfere against the rules, it felt resentment toward this boy and wanted to get rid of him as soon as possible.
"Three choices completed, time has ended."
Lian was about to look around when suddenly everything turned white, space broke, light filled his entire vision, and the next moment... the ground beneath his feet changed.
When he opened his eyes, he was once again standing in front of the treasury entrance.
Damian was there.
Nova had already returned and was standing a few meters away, and Seris was also standing there.
Both turned their gazes toward him, Damian also seemed curious, everyone wanted to know what he had chosen.
But Lian just smiled.

But the problem was that Lian did not know what to do with it, he could not use it like a skill book, he could not read it.
He could not wear it, and he could not use it like a weapon.
The only use that came to his mind was selling it, and he had not come here to find something to sell, he had come here to find items to become stronger.
And at first glance, this thing should not be of any benefit to him.
But... why did his entire being want it?
Why did he feel his blood was going crazy in response to this core?
Why was every cell in his body screaming to take it?
And more importantly... why did he feel that if he left it behind right now, he would regret it later?
His gaze fell on the core once more.
"Maybe it has to do with my class..." he then whispered quietly.
This was the only option that seemed logical, he still knew almost nothing about his real class.
The system had given no explanation, no book existed about it, and no teacher could be found to teach it.
The only one who could uncover its secret was himself, and it was possible that the core in front of him was important for his class.
But what importance?
What use?
What benefit could it have?
Lian sighed and then reached out his hand.
"Even if it has no use right now, I will take it." The moment his fingers touched the core, its dark aura intensified for a second, then disappeared, and the core entered his storage space.
At that same moment, the treasury’s voice echoed in his mind.
"An unexpected choice." He felt that voice was truly surprised.
It seemed it did not expect him to take such a useless thing.
In fact, he himself did not expect it either... he could only hope that his intuition was trustworthy.
At that same moment, part of the space began to ripple.
A corridor that did not exist before appeared in front of him, as if the treasury had decided to show him something more.
Lian entered it without hesitation, and the further he went, the heavier the mana pressure became, and the treasures around him became more valuable.
Along the way he passed by items that each could create a legend.
A black spear that was said to have been used by one of the most powerful awakened ones in the history of the Vorhelms.
A skill book whose pages were shining.
A green crystal that could increase a human’s lifespan by dozens of years.
But none of them caught his attention, not like what was waiting for him at the end of the path.
A few minutes later his steps stopped.
In front of him was a corpse, but not the corpse of a human, not even the corpse of a normal monster.
The massive body of a creature whose size was equal to a multi-story building.
Dark skin, massive bones, and muscles that even after death were releasing a terrifying pressure.
"World Devourer Giant..." Lian’s eyes widened slightly, memories from books of the Ruined Realms appeared in his mind.
An ancient race from the fourth Ruined Realm, creatures that grew stronger by swallowing cities.
Monsters that ate civilizations, a monster that was known for having the strongest defense among all the monster races of the fourth Ruined Realm.
A defense that was said to be as strong as the strongest mountains.
The system immediately appeared.
[ World Devourer Giant ]
[ Rank: Unholy ]
[ Level: 77 ]
Lian let out his breath quietly, an Unholy... and not just any Unholy, but a monster that had passed through three evolutions.
If his guess was correct... this creature had been the leader of its entire race.
The body of such a creature was a complete treasure in itself.
Bones, skin, blood, everything had legendary value.

He had seen several incredible armors in the treasury, but he suddenly understood that none of them could compare to this, with the materials from this body, an armor could be made that would last for generations.
An armor that might even reach Ancient rank, which was a full rank above S rank armors.
For someone like him who fought most of his battles at close range, such a thing had indescribable value.
Lian made his second choice without the slightest hesitation, he could find a ready-made armor, but he had not seen any Ancient rank armor here.
Most of the armors were A rank and S rank, and all of them were inferior in every way to an armor that could be made from this monster’s body.
Now only one choice remained, and time was still passing, he only had 3 minutes left.
He continued searching again, he found many skill books, some so powerful that even looking at them was tempting.
But none of them created that strange feeling, until...
he reached an area that was different from all the other sections of the treasury.
The atmosphere there was heavier, quieter, and more importantly... more protected.
"I suggest you choose another path." Even the treasury’s voice seemed to change for the first time, sounding worried.
"A suggestion, or worry that I might take what is here?" Lian stopped and raised an eyebrow.
The treasury’s voice was silent for a few seconds, and that was enough for him to realize that the second option was true.
The treasury’s consciousness was worried, but this only made Lian more curious.
A few minutes later he reached his destination and was stunned by what he saw in front of him.
In front of him was a massive container, a transparent layer that looked like glass, but only its appearance looked like glass.
The pressure coming from it was insane, even without touching it he could tell that this protection could withstand attacks from level eighty awakened ones.
And in its center... a book was floating.
A golden book, a book with thousands of unclear words engraved on its cover, and the moment Lian’s gaze fell on it, the system notification appeared.
[ Celestial Book of Treasure ]
[ Rank: Mythical ]
Lian just stared for a few seconds.
Mythical... the highest possible rank!
Higher than anything he had seen until today.
And suddenly... the transparent container opened without any sound, as if the treasury itself had allowed it.

Although that was not really the case... if the treasury’s consciousness had a visible face, one could see how worried and terrified it was right now... terrified that if the elders of the Vorhelm clan found out this book had been taken, how furious they would be.
Lian calmly moved forward and read the system’s description.
[ Celestial Book of Treasure ]
[ Ability: Identify and display all valuable treasures within a ten kilometer radius, display location, description and approximate value of treasures ]
[ One of the five Celestial Books ]
Lian was completely silent for a few seconds, now he understood, this book was the real reason for the formation of the Celestial Treasury.
The Vorhelm clan had probably used it for centuries, this same book was what guided them to hidden treasures.
This same book was what had made such wealth possible.
And now... it had fallen into his hands.
Another notification appeared.
[ Celestial Books: 1/5 ]
Lian’s heart beat faster, so there were four other books as well, and this was only the beginning of the story, he made his choice without the slightest hesitation and took the book.
He was a little curious to know how the clan had found and obtained this book.
And he was also curious to know how shocked they would be when they found out this book had fallen into his hands, they would probably be more terrified, right?
He chuckled inwardly, even he himself had not expected such a book to exist, he had not read about anything like this in any book.
It was not hard to guess that the Vorhelms had probably hidden it as well as possible.

The treasury’s consciousness, seeing that the book had been taken, cursed inwardly, but it could not interfere against the rules, it felt resentment toward this boy and wanted to get rid of him as soon as possible.
"Three choices completed, time has ended."
Lian was about to look around when suddenly everything turned white, space broke, light filled his entire vision, and the next moment... the ground beneath his feet changed.
When he opened his eyes, he was once again standing in front of the treasury entrance.
Damian was there.
Nova had already returned and was standing a few meters away, and Seris was also standing there.
Both turned their gazes toward him, Damian also seemed curious, everyone wanted to know what he had chosen.
But Lian just smiled.

chapters.title: Chapter 129: Leaving The Vorhelm Family
paragraphs: The white light of the Celestial Treasury faded slowly, Lian felt the ground beneath his feet taking shape again.
A moment later he appeared in front of the spatial crack, the air of the main territory of the Vorhelm clan filled his lungs once more.
A few meters away, Seris and Nova were also standing, although a little curiosity could be seen on both of their faces, no one said anything.
All three knew that the others had obtained something.
But no one asked, this was one of the unwritten rules of the awakened world.
Treasures, legacies and skills, these were personal secrets.
Secrets that even the closest people did not ask about, after all, these were secrets that could cause jealousy and ruin relationships and maybe lead to conflict.
Damian gave a quick look at all three, curiosity could be seen in his eyes.
But he did not ask anything, he knew better than anyone that some answers should be revealed at the right time.
However, this did not apply to him, the Vorhelm clan would find out sooner or later what had disappeared from the treasury.
After all, the treasury’s consciousness had witnessed all the choices, and whether it wanted to or not, it would report all the treasures that had been removed from the treasury.
And if it was revealed that the Celestial Book of Treasure had been taken out of the treasury... Damian was not sure even he himself would know how to react.
That book was beyond a normal treasure, that book was part of the history of the Vorhelm clan, part of the reason they became one of the most powerful clans in the world.
But the thought that any of these three could obtain that book had not even crossed his mind... because he was sure the treasury’s consciousness would not even bring them near it.
But the problem was that even the treasury itself did not know how Lian had found his way to that book...
After a while they reached the central section of the clan’s territory.
Calmness ruled the environment, no explosion sounds could be heard, no mana waves were in the air, no insane excitement existed.
Only a quiet silence that announced the end of a long ceremony.
The birthday ceremony and the duels had ended, it was almost night now, but many of the guilds, clans, politicians and military personnel had left this place.
Each of them had their own jobs and troubles and had to return to take care of them.
In the distance a group of people from the Nova’s guild were waiting, when Nova saw them, she understood that the time for parting had come.
She looked at Lian for a few moments and then gave a faint smile.
"I hope next time I see you, I can have a fight with you too."
"Sure." Lian smiled.
Nova rolled her eyes and glanced at Seris and Damian, then raised her hand.
"For now."
"For now."
And then she left with her guild’s people.
After a while, people from the Pendragon clan also arrived, but Seris showed no hurry to leave.
She stood a few meters in front of Lian, there was no battlefield, no sword in her hand, no mana pressure could be felt in the air, only two people looking at each other like two friends.
"I hope to see you again." Seris was silent for a few seconds and then said quietly.
"Me too." Lian smiled.
"Next time I will win." The girl’s silver eyes locked onto his for a moment.
"I don’t think so, but you can try again whenever you want."
A small smile appeared on Seris’s face, a smile that almost no one except Lian had ever seen.
"What is your next plan?"
"I want to go back to the Ruined Realm." Lian answered.
"Then maybe we will see each other again." Seris nodded and then turned around, and left with the Pendragon clan’s people.
Lian watched her until the last moment, until her silver hair disappeared.
In the end only Damian and Lian remained, Damian locked his hands behind his back, looked at him for a few moments and then said.
"Now I am really curious to know what my nephew found."
"I am sure you will find out later." Lian smiled, he had no interest in revealing the truth himself right now.
"That’s right, we will definitely find out." His uncle laughed.
"Honestly, I did not think you would really let us take anything we wanted, even the most important treasures of the clan, treasures that act like pillars of the clan."
Damian was silent for a few moments and then sighed.
"The truth is, this was not what we wanted." And he continued.

"The original plan was for the three winners to enter the treasury but under supervision, we would choose a few treasures and each one would take one of them, not freely roam around the entire treasury."
"But after the patriarch’s interference, everything changed, after he told us he wanted you to definitely participate in the duel ceremony, he personally ordered that no treasure be hidden."
"Nothing be removed from the treasury, and all three winners be given free choice, even appearing in different sections was his direct order."
Lian was truly confused. Every time he heard more about that man... he understood him less.
What if the Celestial Book of Treasure fell into the Pendragons’ hands? What if Nova found it? What if one of the other treasures that acted like pillars of the clan was lost?
Why would he take such a risk? Did he trust the outcome? Or did he know something that others did not?
Many questions formed in his mind, but he had no answers.
"Do you really want to go? Don’t you want to stay longer?"
"I have already stayed longer than I planned, it is time to go." Lian answered without thinking.
Damian sighed, a sigh that sounded more like surrender, of course that did not mean he was willing to give up.
"Say goodbye to Cassius, Diana and Aaron for me."
"Sure." Then he said with a strange tone.
"Of course, I doubt Cassius is in the mood to talk right now, he is probably being punished by those two women right now."
"Same for Evangeline and Adrian, those two are definitely either being punished or being cursed at.
Lian immediately understood what he meant, the two matriarchs would definitely see their children’s weakness as the reason for their failure in this competition and would definitely punish them.
The image of Cassius trapped between those two made him want to laugh, but he knew those two women would definitely be ruthless.
They are definitely angry and humiliated right now, everyone will blame Celestia for the failure in these duels, and more elders will turn against her and she might become more isolated.
"Instead of punishing them, it is better to send them to the Ruined Realm soon, maybe they will become stronger there." Then he shrugged.
Damian nodded.
"In the next few days all of them will enter, you should not be lazy either, if you are lazy that girl will surpass you."
There was no need to say the name, both knew he meant Seris.
Damian continued.
"Diana too, and Rain."
The name Rain made Lian silent for a few moments, a brother he had not seen for years, the owner of a five-star class, one of the greatest talents of the clan.
Diana.
Rain.
Seris.
Cassius.
Everyone was becoming stronger, but he was sure none of them could reach him... except Seris, if he was lazy that girl really might catch up to him.
He was also a little curious to know what that girl had obtained from inside the treasury.
"I am not going to be lazy."
"Good." Damian also smiled.
A few minutes later they reached the main gate of the territory, the moment of farewell had come, Lian did not want to stay here tonight.
He wanted to leave this place before they found out that the Celestial Book of Treasure was in his hands, of course he knew if they really came after him to take it back, he could not do anything.
But if he stayed here, they would definitely bother him and try to persuade him to return the book.
Damian placed his hand on Lian’s shoulder.
"Take care of yourself, as I promised you have one absolute request from me, if you need help you can contact me."
"You take care of yourself too, uncle."
They looked at each other for a few moments.
Then Lian turned around and walked toward the outside.
This time he did not look back, not at the clan’s mansions, not at the massive walls, not at the land that was once his home, and he left directly from there.
The time had come to return to the academy and the Ruined Realm.

chapters.title: Chapter 130: Getting A Lady’s Number
paragraphs: The massive gates of the Vorhelm clan were slowly getting smaller behind Lian.
The stone walls that for hundreds of years had been a symbol of power for one of the largest clans in the world, no longer mattered to him.
For the first time he felt he had truly left that place, his previous departure was not by his own choice, he had no choice but to leave this place.

He had practically been rejected and exiled, at that time it was really hard for him, but now? Now everything was different, now he could finally leave this place with a feeling of peace and without any regret.
And the situation had now reversed, this time it was the Vorhelm clan that regretted it, something he did not think would happen even a month ago.
As he was heading to the city’s transportation center, he felt several powerful and familiar presences behind him.
His steps stopped, when he turned around, he saw a group of people from the Pendragon clan.
Aurelia was standing among them, Seris was a few steps behind, and several powerful guards were accompanying them.
On the surface it seemed they were also leaving the Vorhelm territory.
But Lian easily noticed that Aurelia had stopped intentionally, they should have left this place by now, it was clear they were waiting for something, as if waiting for an opportunity to talk.
And seeing them coming toward him, he realized his guess was completely correct.
"I wanted to talk to you one more time before you leave." Aurelia came forward with the same calm and friendly smile as always.
"Of course." Lian nodded politely, he had not seen any bad treatment from the Pendragon clan, who should be considered his enemies, until now, showing a little respect and modesty was not bad.
Aurelia looked at him for a few moments and then her smile deepened.
"Honestly, I was very happy to see a genius like you, it has been a long time since anyone has made Seris this excited."
She looked toward the silver-haired girl, almost immediately Seris turned her head to the other side, as if she had not heard such a thing at all.
This very reaction made Aurelia laugh.
"See? This is exactly what she does when she is embarrassed."
Seris immediately frowned, gave a quick look at Aurelia, but did not answer, this silence itself was the best confirmation.
Aurelia turned to Lian again and this time her tone became a little more serious.
"If you ever get the chance... definitely visit the Pendragon territory too, I am sure you will be welcomed there."
Lian thought for a few seconds and then shrugged.
"Maybe in the future." It was neither acceptance nor rejection, just a cautious answer, because the country under the Pendragons’ control was an extremely powerful country.
There was a high chance he would want to visit there in the future, and being welcomed there by them would be a very good thing.
Apparently that was enough for Aurelia, the woman smiled with satisfaction, then took out her phone and asked.
"What is your phone number?"
"My phone number?" Lian was a little surprised and laughed quietly, then he gave his phone number to her and the woman called him briefly so his phone would have her number too.
"If you ever need help, or have a request that falls within the Pendragon clan’s domain, you can contact me."
Lian paused for a moment, it seemed like a simple offer, but in reality such a thing was very valuable.
One of the leaders of the Pendragon clan was directly giving him her personal contact.
Without any middleman, without any limits, he did not even have a way to contact Seris herself yet, but he had directly gotten the phone number of one of the high-level figures?
But considering everything he had done, maybe he should not be too surprised, it was even expected, and he should probably expect more numbers too.
"Thank you."
Aurelia just smiled, a few minutes later the Pendragon clan people continued on their way.
Seris only looked at him for a moment as she passed, she said nothing, but that brief look was enough.
Then they also moved away.
Lian watched them for a while, until they were completely out of sight.
"This woman is too interested in me." He then thought quietly in his mind.
He was sure Aurelia was thinking about recruiting him for the Pendragon clan, but then he realized it was not just the Pendragons.
Guilds, clans, military organizations and even governments, anyone who had seen his power had probably become interested in him.
It was not like all the powers of the world were at this ceremony, the Vorhelms also had many enemies who were not invited, hostile forces.

For example, the current president of the country, that man did not have a good relationship with the Vorhelms at all, he thought they had too much power in the country and directly and indirectly affected the country’s politics, and for that reason they should be limited.
But while the Vorhelms’ relationship with the president and his government was bad, the Vorhelms had a very good relationship with the country’s congress and the national awakened organization.

But this made him a little curious to know how a man who was against the Vorhelms had come to power in this country, really how was such a thing possible? He had no doubt that there was foreign interference and probably some of the Vorhelms’ most powerful enemies had intervened.
But he felt there might be more secrets behind it, anyway he had no information to reason with.
Anyway, fortunately the news of his victory had not spread yet, most of the people present at the ceremony were from the upper classes of society, people who usually spread news with a delay.
But Lian knew this situation was not permanent, sooner or later his name would spread across the continent, for now he was completely known at the national level.
He had a small fame at the continental and world level too, but it was extremely limited, at least for now, and after that nothing would be like before.
He took a deep breath and continued his path toward the transportation station, after arriving he paid the required fee like before and went toward the origin portal.
The portal’s light surrounded his body, space bent, the world blurred for a moment, and a few seconds later he appeared in the capital again.
The city was the same, the streets, the towers, the lights, everything was familiar, after all the strange events of the Vorhelm clan, the capital felt like home.
When he entered the academy, he soon noticed a strange change.
The academy was emptier, much emptier, although it was night, it was not the time when everyone went to sleep, but rather the time when they came out to chat and talk with their friends.
But the areas that were always crowded now seemed half empty.
Even the sound of students had decreased, it did not take more than a few seconds for him to understand the reason.
The Ruined Realms had opened, almost all the serious talents of the academy had already entered them, in fact most of the strong students had no reason to stay in the academy anymore.
And after a few days, now finally the weaker students had also gone.
Lian actually knew from the messages he had received that Cassian and Seraphina had also gone to the Ruined Realm.
Lian nodded, all the people he had gotten used to were now somewhere else.
It was as if the world had moved on without him, but tomorrow he himself would return to that world too, so there was no reason to worry or feel sad.
Before going to the dormitory, he changed his path and went toward Professor Aldric’s office.
He knocked on the door and entered a few seconds later.
Aldric was sitting behind his desk, as usual dealing with his work, and when he saw Lian he just raised an eyebrow slightly.
"You are back?"
"Yeah."
Aldric looked at him for a few moments, but unlike what was expected, he did not ask any questions about the ceremony, no questions about the Vorhelm clan, he just said.
"So I no longer have to worry about being threatened by the Vorhelms for not expelling you?"
"No." A small smile appeared on Lian’s face.
Eldric nodded.
"Good." Then he returned to his work, as if that one answer was enough for him.
And the truth was, this was exactly the behavior expected from him.
Lian did not add anything either, he just said goodbye and left the office.
When he entered the dormitory, a strange silence filled the place, the room was almost the same as he remembered.
The bed, the desk, the window, everything was in its place, after a long time he did nothing, he fell on the bed and stared at the ceiling.
Tomorrow he would enter the Ruined Realm again, after being away for two or three weeks, finally the time had come to return.
His eyes slowly closed, Lian fell asleep without worry... but tomorrow... everything would start all over again.

sentences.text: The massive gates of the Vorhelm clan were slowly getting smaller behind Lian.
The stone walls that for hundreds of years had been a symbol of power for one of the largest clans in the world, no longer mattered to him.
For the first time he felt he had truly left that place, his previous departure was not by his own choice, he had no choice but to leave this place.
He had practically been rejected and exiled, at that time it was really hard for him, but now?
Now everything was different, now he could finally leave this place with a feeling of peace and without any regret.
And the situation had now reversed, this time it was the Vorhelm clan that regretted it, something he did not think would happen even a month ago.
As he was heading to the city’s transportation center, he felt several powerful and familiar presences behind him.
His steps stopped, when he turned around, he saw a group of people from the Pendragon clan.
Aurelia was standing among them, Seris was a few steps behind, and several powerful guards were accompanying them.
On the surface it seemed they were also leaving the Vorhelm territory.
But Lian easily noticed that Aurelia had stopped intentionally, they should have left this place by now, it was clear they were waiting for something, as if waiting for an opportunity to talk.
And seeing them coming toward him, he realized his guess was completely correct.
"I wanted to talk to you one more time before you leave." Aurelia came forward with the same calm and friendly smile as always.
"Of course." Lian nodded politely, he had not seen any bad treatment from the Pendragon clan, who should be considered his enemies, until now, showing a little respect and modesty was not bad.
Aurelia looked at him for a few moments and then her smile deepened.
"Honestly, I was very happy to see a genius like you, it has been a long time since anyone has made Seris this excited."
She looked toward the silver-haired girl, almost immediately Seris turned her head to the other side, as if she had not heard such a thing at all.
This very reaction made Aurelia laugh.
"See?
This is exactly what she does when she is embarrassed."
Seris immediately frowned, gave a quick look at Aurelia, but did not answer, this silence itself was the best confirmation.
Aurelia turned to Lian again and this time her tone became a little more serious.
"If you ever get the chance... definitely visit the Pendragon territory too, I am sure you will be welcomed there."
Lian thought for a few seconds and then shrugged.
"Maybe in the future." It was neither acceptance nor rejection, just a cautious answer, because the country under the Pendragons’ control was an extremely powerful country.
There was a high chance he would want to visit there in the future, and being welcomed there by them would be a very good thing.
Apparently that was enough for Aurelia, the woman smiled with satisfaction, then took out her phone and asked.
"What is your phone number?"
"My phone number?" Lian was a little surprised and laughed quietly, then he gave his phone number to her and the woman called him briefly so his phone would have her number too.
"If you ever need help, or have a request that falls within the Pendragon clan’s domain, you can contact me."
Lian paused for a moment, it seemed like a simple offer, but in reality such a thing was very valuable.
One of the leaders of the Pendragon clan was directly giving him her personal contact.
Without any middleman, without any limits, he did not even have a way to contact Seris herself yet, but he had directly gotten the phone number of one of the high-level figures?
But considering everything he had done, maybe he should not be too surprised, it was even expected, and he should probably expect more numbers too.
"Thank you."
Aurelia just smiled, a few minutes later the Pendragon clan people continued on their way.
Seris only looked at him for a moment as she passed, she said nothing, but that brief look was enough.
Then they also moved away.
Lian watched them for a while, until they were completely out of sight.
"This woman is too interested in me." He then thought quietly in his mind.
He was sure Aurelia was thinking about recruiting him for the Pendragon clan, but then he realized it was not just the Pendragons.
Guilds, clans, military organizations and even governments, anyone who had seen his power had probably become interested in him.
It was not like all the powers of the world were at this ceremony, the Vorhelms also had many enemies who were not invited, hostile forces.

For example, the current president of the country, that man did not have a good relationship with the Vorhelms at all, he thought they had too much power in the country and directly and indirectly affected the country’s politics, and for that reason they should be limited.
But while the Vorhelms’ relationship with the president and his government was bad, the Vorhelms had a very good relationship with the country’s congress and the national awakened organization.
But this made him a little curious to know how a man who was against the Vorhelms had come to power in this country, really how was such a thing possible?
He had no doubt that there was foreign interference and probably some of the Vorhelms’ most powerful enemies had intervened.
But he felt there might be more secrets behind it, anyway he had no information to reason with.
Anyway, fortunately the news of his victory had not spread yet, most of the people present at the ceremony were from the upper classes of society, people who usually spread news with a delay.
But Lian knew this situation was not permanent, sooner or later his name would spread across the continent, for now he was completely known at the national level.
He had a small fame at the continental and world level too, but it was extremely limited, at least for now, and after that nothing would be like before.
He took a deep breath and continued his path toward the transportation station, after arriving he paid the required fee like before and went toward the origin portal.
The portal’s light surrounded his body, space bent, the world blurred for a moment, and a few seconds later he appeared in the capital again.
The city was the same, the streets, the towers, the lights, everything was familiar, after all the strange events of the Vorhelm clan, the capital felt like home.
When he entered the academy, he soon noticed a strange change.
The academy was emptier, much emptier, although it was night, it was not the time when everyone went to sleep, but rather the time when they came out to chat and talk with their friends.
But the areas that were always crowded now seemed half empty.
Even the sound of students had decreased, it did not take more than a few seconds for him to understand the reason.
The Ruined Realms had opened, almost all the serious talents of the academy had already entered them, in fact most of the strong students had no reason to stay in the academy anymore.
And after a few days, now finally the weaker students had also gone.
Lian actually knew from the messages he had received that Cassian and Seraphina had also gone to the Ruined Realm.
Lian nodded, all the people he had gotten used to were now somewhere else.
It was as if the world had moved on without him, but tomorrow he himself would return to that world too, so there was no reason to worry or feel sad.
Before going to the dormitory, he changed his path and went toward Professor Aldric’s office.
He knocked on the door and entered a few seconds later.
Aldric was sitting behind his desk, as usual dealing with his work, and when he saw Lian he just raised an eyebrow slightly.
"You are back?"
"Yeah."
Aldric looked at him for a few moments, but unlike what was expected, he did not ask any questions about the ceremony, no questions about the Vorhelm clan, he just said.
"So I no longer have to worry about being threatened by the Vorhelms for not expelling you?"
"No." A small smile appeared on Lian’s face.
Eldric nodded.
"Good." Then he returned to his work, as if that one answer was enough for him.
And the truth was, this was exactly the behavior expected from him.
Lian did not add anything either, he just said goodbye and left the office.
When he entered the dormitory, a strange silence filled the place, the room was almost the same as he remembered.
The bed, the desk, the window, everything was in its place, after a long time he did nothing, he fell on the bed and stared at the ceiling.
Tomorrow he would enter the Ruined Realm again, after being away for two or three weeks, finally the time had come to return.
His eyes slowly closed, Lian fell asleep without worry... but tomorrow... everything would start all over again.

chapters.title: Chapter 131: Welcome back to the Ruined Realm
paragraphs: It was early morning, the faint light of the sun had passed through the dormitory curtains and fallen on the ceiling of the room.
Lian slowly opened his eyes, unlike the past days when he had to wake up in a hurry because of the ceremony and duels, now he had no rush to get up.

He remained motionless for a few seconds, just staring at the ceiling, the silence of the room had a special peace, but very soon his mind went toward one of the most important things he had obtained from the Celestial Treasury.
The body of the World Devourer Giant, an Unholy creature, a monster at level seventy-seven, a monster that had passed through three complete evolutions.
Even now it was not easy to believe its real value.
Just thinking that such a creature once lived in one of the Ruined Realms, made him understand the greatness of the world better, and also made him understand how weak he still was.
He himself could not even take one hit from that monster and would be turned into thousands of unequal pieces on the spot.
Anyway, if the materials from that body were extracted properly... if the scales, bones, skin and inner cores were processed by a real master...
It would probably be possible to make an armor that would be the best of its kind, maybe even an armor at the Ancient level, something that could stay with him for a very long time.

But the problem was clear. He knew nothing about blacksmithing, he did not even know a high-level blacksmith, the only name that came to his mind was Kain, and even he was not a blacksmith, he just knew blacksmiths.
Lian let out a short sigh.
"Only he can help me find someone who knows how to make an Ancient armor from that corpse."
But this same issue created another problem, he had no idea where Kain was, he was in the Ruined Realm now, but where could he find him?

If he was hunting around the main base and returned every few days, finding him would not be difficult, but if he had decided to explore farther areas... he might not be seen for weeks or even months.
Lian got up from the bed, in the end he decided to enter the Ruined Realm first, then plan to find Kain.
In the worst case, he could find a clue about him through guilds and various hunters.

After washing his face and getting ready, he put on his armor, the same armor that Gareth had given him, compared to the treasures he had seen recently, this armor was no longer anything special, but it was still reliable.
It was still intact, and more importantly it was still usable, an A rank armor.
A few minutes later he left the dormitory, his target was clear, the academy’s portal building.
He could go to the Ruined Realm without portals too, this was an ability that had been given to him by the system itself because he had been able to return from being summoned in the Ruined Realm.
But if he used that ability, he would appear in the Dreadmaw cave, and that was not something he wanted right now.

The building for transferring to the Ruined Realm was located in the eastern section of the academy, a large and independent structure, with white walls and massive pillars that rose several meters high.
Almost all the students who intended to enter the Ruined Realm passed through this path.
When he entered the building, he saw several other students too, some of them were anxious, some excited, and some were looking around with obvious pride.
Most of them were newcomers, those who did not yet know how cruel the Ruined Realm could be.
Lian ignored them and went to the registration desk, the portal officer was a middle-aged man who raised his eyebrows as soon as he saw him.
"Oh, welcome back."
"Hello." Lian nodded.
"You want to enter the Ruined Realm? Student code." The man smiled.
Lian provided the code and a few seconds later his information appeared on the screen, the officer glanced at it and then began explaining.
"The base you are going to be transferred to does not belong to the academy, it was built by the government, the main operations center of the entire country inside the Ruined Realm."
Lian listened carefully.
"In fact, it is a complete city there, equipment shops, monster material vendors, an open market, medical centers."
"Rest areas, training halls, mission registration offices, and almost everything an awakened one might need."
Lian nodded, he had heard about bases before, bases practically acted as hubs and starting points, safe areas where awakened ones could rest without worry.
And more importantly, they were also places for hunters to earn income, places to find talents and...
These bases would gradually expand until they might cover thousands of kilometers.
The man continued.
"Inside the base there is also a special center for the academy, all students are required to register their presence there after entering."
"After that you can take missions, submit reports, receive rewards and use the academy’s services." Then his tone became a little serious.
"And a warning, for your own safety, do not go more than a hundred kilometers from the base for now."
"Within a hundred kilometer radius, the area has been largely cleared and is safe, there are monsters below level 15 for new awakened ones to benefit from."
"But beyond that... the rules are different, powerful monsters, unknown territories and deadly zones are all there."
A few seconds of silence followed and then the man shrugged.
"There is nothing more than this that you need to know, once you are inside, you will find guides who will explain about the areas and monsters around."

"Understood." Lian nodded, he did not take the warning too seriously, but he did not completely ignore it either, he definitely had to check to make sure that by going beyond that hundred kilometers, he would not suddenly face level 50 monsters.
"Then good luck." The man pointed at the portal.

The portal in front of him was shining, a massive circle of blue light with compressed energy flowing inside it, Lian stepped forward without hesitation and a moment later the light covered everything.
Space twisted, time had no meaning for a moment, he felt his body passing through different layers of reality.
And then... when he opened his eyes, he did not move for a few seconds.
He just looked, and the more he looked, the more impressed he became.
The country’s main base, this place was far beyond what he had imagined.
In front of him was a massive city, a city built in the heart of a ruined world, massive walls stretched around it.
Watchtowers could be seen in various places, mana cannons were installed on the walls, and thousands of awakened ones were moving through the streets.
Some of them had just returned from hunting, their armors bloodied, their weapons bearing the marks of battle.
Some were carrying monster corpses on large carts, monsters some of which were several meters long.
In another part of the city, groups of hunters were preparing to leave.
Some were buying equipment, some were examining maps, and some were negotiating to form groups.
The shouts of vendors could be heard from the markets, flags of different guilds were moving in the wind, mission boards were installed in various places.
And a lively energy was flowing through the entire environment, as if the whole city was built for only one purpose.
Hunting, survival and growth, for a moment he really felt like he had entered the lobby of a massive game.
But this was not a game, everything was real, every monster outside the walls could kill him.
And every opportunity he found in this place could change his future, and at that moment a blue window appeared in front of him.
[ Welcome back to the Ruined Realm ]
[ Current Region: Base#3 ]
Lian looked at the notification for a few seconds, each base in the Ruined Realm was recorded by the system and received its own code, and their base’s code was #3.
Then he smiled quietly, he was finally back, this time his goal was clearer than ever, reaching the first evolution.
Of course... after registering and maybe finding Kain.
( The Base’s Visualization )

chapters.title: Chapter 132: The Base#3
paragraphs: After a few minutes of walking through the busy streets of the base and asking several guards for directions, Lian finally found the building he was looking for.
The academy center.
Unlike the grand and calm buildings of the main academy, this place looked more like a military base than an educational center.
A massive building made of metal and stone, with dozens of armed guards at its entrance, students were constantly coming in and out.
But what caught Lian’s attention were their faces.
Some were tired, some were wounded, and some still had their clothes stained with monster blood.
And some others... were standing in front of large boards, staring at the names with heavy faces.
The casualty board, Lian kept his gaze on one of those boards for a few moments.
Dozens of names, dozens of students, all of them from his own academy.
’Probably none of them expected such a thing.’ He sighed.

Young and new awakened ones, when they first enter the Ruined Realms, have an uncontrollable excitement and enthusiasm, they think they are the main character who will reach the peak of the world by hunting monsters, embrace beauties, and obtain endless wealth, legendary treasures and legacies.
But this was not even close to the truth, none of them were special, none of them were main characters with plot armor.
They were just a few excited young people who were not aware of the real danger of this hell, a hell that at first glance looks like a game world.
But in reality it is a place where many can lose their lives daily, and the problem is that for every human who dies, cracks open and monsters can enter their world and start killing and massacring.
The reality of the Ruined Realm reminded itself to him again, and then he entered the building.
After registering his information and announcing his entry to the Ruined Realm, one of the employees issued a wristband for him.

"This is a smart wristband that records all your kills, if you want before leaving, bring it and hand it over and we will add student points to you based on the number of kills, it also determines your alive or dead status."
Lian then nodded, and after putting on the wristband, he went toward the place that had caught his attention the most.
What caught his attention more than anything else was the main hall of the center, dozens of massive holographic screens were floating on the walls.
All the area’s information was displayed on them.
Lian went close to one that was showing the overall statistics of the base.
Current population of awakened ones registered at the base: 24,381 people.
Registered students: 1,209 people.
Last month’s casualties: 1,294 people.
Note: Casualties are shown from the day the base was opened for public use.
Closed areas: 12 areas.
High-level warnings: 7 active.
Lian looked at the numbers for a few seconds, more than a thousand deaths in one month, of course, more precisely, this casualty count was for less than two weeks.
And that was only in this area, this number was even higher than what he had expected.
How exactly did so many casualties happen? Did the awakened ones not pay attention to the warnings at all? Or did they act foolishly and leave the safe zone?
Why would they do such a thing when they did not have the ability for it...?
He checked a few more screens, reports of new monster appearances, reports of activity by large monster packs.
Warnings related to forbidden zones and several military announcements.
After a few minutes of studying, he realized the reason for so many casualties, beyond the 100 kilometer safe zone, there were three specific races of monsters that only moved in herds.
And in very large herds that included dozens and hundreds of monsters, their levels were above 15.
Most of these casualties were from the early days when no one knew about the existence of these three monster races, and it led to widespread massacres of awakened ones.
And now because of that, few dare to leave the safe zone, and professional teams have not yet been formed to hunt those monsters.
Then he changed his path to the registration status section.
His target was clear, Kain.
When he entered his name, it took a few seconds for the AI to find the information, and then a screen appeared.
[ Name: Kain ]
[ Surname: — ]
[ Status: Active / Alive ]
[ Last recorded sighting: 5 days ago ]
[ Location: Unknown ]
Lian took a deep breath.
It was the same as what he expected, Kain was still alive... probably, but the location was unknown?
This gave him practically no useful information, he had to ask the officer again, and after that he understood what these meant.
Status: Active/Alive indicates the wristband given by the academy, this wristband checks the heartbeat at all times and updates the status in the academy system every three hours.
If the heartbeat is normal and still working, it means the person is alive, but if it is semi-active/reduced, it means they are in a bad condition, and if it is inactive/off, it means they are dead.
Whenever they return to the base, the wristband automatically announces the return and registers a check-in.
If no check-in is done for thirty days, the status changes to unknown, missing.
As long as they are within the hundred kilometer radius, their location is completely clear, but if they go beyond that, the location changes to unknown.
Based on all this, the conclusion was simple, Kain was alive but far from the base.
After that he looked at the status of his friends, Selina, Liana, Seraphina, Cassius and Marcus, all of them were alive and of course in unknown areas.
But their last check-in was for two days ago, so they clearly had not gone too far.
Finally he left the information section and went toward the mission hall, massive holographic boards were floating all over the hall.
Hundreds of missions, maybe thousands of missions, from hunting weak monsters to exploration missions, protecting people and caravans, extracting rare resources and assisting in discoveries.
Lian checked them one by one.
The rewards were attractive, but he did not find anything that caught his attention, besides, before choosing any mission, he preferred to get familiar with this place first.
Then he went to the geographical information section, several large 3D maps were floating in the air.
Maps of the surrounding area of the base, and he started examining them, very soon he realized that the portal officer had not lied.
Up to a hundred kilometer radius of the base was truly considered safe, most of the registered monsters were below level fifteen.
Many of them were even below level ten.
For new awakened ones, this area was ideal.
But Lian very soon found something more interesting, up to eight hundred kilometers from the base, there were many areas on the map that had only been initially identified.
Reports showed that most of these areas had only been examined by professional exploration groups.
Mercenary groups, elite guild teams, and special government teams, but many of those areas were still considered unknown.
There was no accurate information about their monsters or resources because they had only been examined in a limited way.
Because of the existence of those three monster races, they could not explore those areas without complete worry.
This made him understand the true greatness of the Ruined Realm better.
After finishing his examinations, Lian finally decided to do the next important thing, buying a mount, he had no interest in running all the way.
Especially now that he would probably have to search vast areas.

In the Ruined Realm, having a suitable means of transport was almost as important as having a good weapon. After a little asking around, he soon found the location of the country’s most famous tame monster store.
Its name was almost known to all awakened ones.
Golden Saddle Consortium
The largest seller of tame monsters in the entire country, it was said that its central branch kept thousands of different monsters.
From simple pack monsters to expensive combat creatures, the entrance of the border base branch was almost the size of a small square.
On a massive golden sign above the building, the image of a winged horse-like monster was carved.
The sound of monsters could be heard from inside, armored horses, riding wolves, giant pack lizards, and even a few stranger creatures that Lian had never seen.
He stood in front of the entrance.
If he was going to stay in the Ruined Realm for a long time, he needed a suitable companion, and this was probably the best place to find one.
With that thought, he opened the massive doors of the store and entered.
And right at that moment, he realized that choosing among all these different monsters would probably be much harder than he had imagined.

Young and new awakened ones, when they first enter the Ruined Realms, have an uncontrollable excitement and enthusiasm, they think they are the main character who will reach the peak of the world by hunting monsters, embrace beauties, and obtain endless wealth, legendary treasures and legacies.
But this was not even close to the truth, none of them were special, none of them were main characters with plot armor.
They were just a few excited young people who were not aware of the real danger of this hell, a hell that at first glance looks like a game world.
But in reality it is a place where many can lose their lives daily, and the problem is that for every human who dies, cracks open and monsters can enter their world and start killing and massacring.
The reality of the Ruined Realm reminded itself to him again, and then he entered the building.
After registering his information and announcing his entry to the Ruined Realm, one of the employees issued a wristband for him.

"This is a smart wristband that records all your kills, if you want before leaving, bring it and hand it over and we will add student points to you based on the number of kills, it also determines your alive or dead status."
Lian then nodded, and after putting on the wristband, he went toward the place that had caught his attention the most.
What caught his attention more than anything else was the main hall of the center, dozens of massive holographic screens were floating on the walls.
All the area’s information was displayed on them.
Lian went close to one that was showing the overall statistics of the base.
Current population of awakened ones registered at the base: 24,381 people.
Registered students: 1,209 people.
Last month’s casualties: 1,294 people.
Note: Casualties are shown from the day the base was opened for public use.
Closed areas: 12 areas.
High-level warnings: 7 active.
Lian looked at the numbers for a few seconds, more than a thousand deaths in one month, of course, more precisely, this casualty count was for less than two weeks.
And that was only in this area, this number was even higher than what he had expected.
How exactly did so many casualties happen?
Did the awakened ones not pay attention to the warnings at all?
Or did they act foolishly and leave the safe zone?
Why would they do such a thing when they did not have the ability for it...?
He checked a few more screens, reports of new monster appearances, reports of activity by large monster packs.
Warnings related to forbidden zones and several military announcements.
After a few minutes of studying, he realized the reason for so many casualties, beyond the 100 kilometer safe zone, there were three specific races of monsters that only moved in herds.
And in very large herds that included dozens and hundreds of monsters, their levels were above 15.
Most of these casualties were from the early days when no one knew about the existence of these three monster races, and it led to widespread massacres of awakened ones.
And now because of that, few dare to leave the safe zone, and professional teams have not yet been formed to hunt those monsters.
Then he changed his path to the registration status section.
His target was clear, Kain.
When he entered his name, it took a few seconds for the AI to find the information, and then a screen appeared.
[ Name: Kain ]
[ Surname: — ]
[ Status: Active / Alive ]
[ Last recorded sighting: 5 days ago ]
[ Location: Unknown ]
Lian took a deep breath.
It was the same as what he expected, Kain was still alive... probably, but the location was unknown?
This gave him practically no useful information, he had to ask the officer again, and after that he understood what these meant.
Status: Active/Alive indicates the wristband given by the academy, this wristband checks the heartbeat at all times and updates the status in the academy system every three hours.
If the heartbeat is normal and still working, it means the person is alive, but if it is semi-active/reduced, it means they are in a bad condition, and if it is inactive/off, it means they are dead.
Whenever they return to the base, the wristband automatically announces the return and registers a check-in.
If no check-in is done for thirty days, the status changes to unknown, missing.
As long as they are within the hundred kilometer radius, their location is completely clear, but if they go beyond that, the location changes to unknown.
Based on all this, the conclusion was simple, Kain was alive but far from the base.
After that he looked at the status of his friends, Selina, Liana, Seraphina, Cassius and Marcus, all of them were alive and of course in unknown areas.
But their last check-in was for two days ago, so they clearly had not gone too far.
Finally he left the information section and went toward the mission hall, massive holographic boards were floating all over the hall.
Hundreds of missions, maybe thousands of missions, from hunting weak monsters to exploration missions, protecting people and caravans, extracting rare resources and assisting in discoveries.
Lian checked them one by one.
The rewards were attractive, but he did not find anything that caught his attention, besides, before choosing any mission, he preferred to get familiar with this place first.
Then he went to the geographical information section, several large 3D maps were floating in the air.
Maps of the surrounding area of the base, and he started examining them, very soon he realized that the portal officer had not lied.
Up to a hundred kilometer radius of the base was truly considered safe, most of the registered monsters were below level fifteen.
Many of them were even below level ten.
For new awakened ones, this area was ideal.
But Lian very soon found something more interesting, up to eight hundred kilometers from the base, there were many areas on the map that had only been initially identified.
Reports showed that most of these areas had only been examined by professional exploration groups.
Mercenary groups, elite guild teams, and special government teams, but many of those areas were still considered unknown.
There was no accurate information about their monsters or resources because they had only been examined in a limited way.
Because of the existence of those three monster races, they could not explore those areas without complete worry.
This made him understand the true greatness of the Ruined Realm better.
After finishing his examinations, Lian finally decided to do the next important thing, buying a mount, he had no interest in running all the way.
Especially now that he would probably have to search vast areas.
In the Ruined Realm, having a suitable means of transport was almost as important as having a good weapon.
After a little asking around, he soon found the location of the country’s most famous tame monster store.
Its name was almost known to all awakened ones.
Golden Saddle Consortium
The largest seller of tame monsters in the entire country, it was said that its central branch kept thousands of different monsters.
From simple pack monsters to expensive combat creatures, the entrance of the border base branch was almost the size of a small square.
On a massive golden sign above the building, the image of a winged horse-like monster was carved.
The sound of monsters could be heard from inside, armored horses, riding wolves, giant pack lizards, and even a few stranger creatures that Lian had never seen.
He stood in front of the entrance.
If he was going to stay in the Ruined Realm for a long time, he needed a suitable companion, and this was probably the best place to find one.
With that thought, he opened the massive doors of the store and entered.
And right at that moment, he realized that choosing among all these different monsters would probably be much harder than he had imagined.

chapters.title: Chapter 133: The Heavenly Realm
paragraphs: In the early days, everyone thought that only dead monsters were useful, until the summoner class, which is also known as beast tamer, appeared.

Summoners are of two types, those who have the ability to summon spiritual monsters, what type of monster and at what level and rank they can summon depends completely on how many stars their class has and the rank of their innate skills.
Liana is from this type of summoner, she was able to summon two spiritual monsters from the Heavenly Realm and make contracts with them.
The Heavenly Realm is actually a very special place, it is a complete world, exactly like their world or the Ruined Realms.
The Heavenly Realm is a place that awakened ones who have passed at least three evolutions can access, in the early days when the first Ruined Realm appeared, no one knew such a place existed.
Only when the first awakened one who passed three evolutions and reached level 60, did they realize the existence of the Heavenly Realm or Heaven
A mythical world where thousands and millions of intelligent and very powerful races live, a place rich in resources and very powerful creatures.
Of course, their world has been at war with the races of the Heavenly Realm for years, and both sides hate each other.

The reason? In this matter, the fault is theirs, the Heavenly Realm is a very rich world, a world so rich that humans came to the conclusion that they should colonize it, and this caused a war in that world between them and the natives of that world.
If the monsters of the Ruined Realm attacked their world, then they also attacked the Heavenly Realm.
Anyway, until the Heavenly Realm was discovered, summoners thought that the spiritual monsters they summoned came from the Ruined Realm.
It was after that that they actually understood that the origin of those spiritual monsters was the Heavenly Realm.
The second type of summoners are those who are lucky enough to get a skill among their innate skills for taming monsters and making contracts with them.
They have the ability to tame and control monsters... the second type is considerably rarer.
But this same second type led to the formation of the animal taming industry.
The "Golden Horn Beast Consortium" store was much larger than what Lian expected.
Upon entering, the smell of dry grass, monster feed and dense mana was in the air, various sounds could be heard from different sections of the building.
Roars, neighs, the sound of wings flapping, and even screams of creatures that Lian had never seen.
A middle-aged seller with gray hair came to greet him.
"Welcome to the Golden Horn Consortium. Are you looking for a combat monster or a mount? Or a combination of both?"
"A mount." Lian answered without hesitation.
"Only a mount?" The man raised his eyebrow, most people who came here were looking for both.
"Only a mount."
"Then you are one of those people who know what they really need." A faint smile appeared on the seller’s face.
He took Lian to the back section of the store, along the way dozens of different monsters could be seen.
Some were gigantic, some had natural armor, some had horns as big as a full grown human.

But none of them caught his attention, he was not looking for power, monsters that had high power had average speed, what he needed was speed, mobility and a way to cover long distances without wasting energy.
"Most novice awakened ones make a mistake." The seller said as if he had read his mind.
They passed through the cages.
"They see a scary monster and buy it, then three months later they realize all their money has gone into feeding and maintaining that monster."
"I care more about speed and how far it can go." Lian nodded.
"You are making the right choice." The seller led him to another section, in this part, the creatures were calmer and smaller.
"Before you choose, it is better to know the ranks." The man continued.
"Common, cheap, suitable for beginners." He pointed at a horse-like creature.
Then he went to the next section.
"Rare, faster, smarter, more resistant, the most popular choice for hunters." Then he pointed at a massive creature with black skin.
"Elite, for professionals, from here on the prices become insane."
Lian looked at the monster, its power was clear, but he did not need such a thing.

"These three categories I told you about are monsters whose wild counterparts are the same normal and fallen monsters, and depending on their racial abilities and rarity in the market, they can fall into any of these three categories." Then his tone changed a little.
"But from here on, the story is different."
His eyes narrowed.
"Unholy, monsters that have full consciousness, creatures that can think like humans, it is almost impossible to tame them." He was silent for a few seconds.
"And above that... Demons." Even in the crowded store, this word had a special weight.
"They are legendary, the vast majority of awakened ones do not even see one in their entire lives."
Lian involuntarily thought about the Demon core inside his storage space, he had expected that Unholies and Demons would not be that tamable.
He had only seen one living Unholy, and from that meeting he could say that creature was in no way tamable.
"When did this industry start?" His curiosity went toward another topic.
The seller smiled, it was clear he liked this question, because most customers only asked about prices.
"After the discovery of the first Ruined Realm, at first everyone thought monsters were only for killing, but gradually they realized some of them are more valuable than gold."
They passed by several large cages.
"First the skills related to monster control appeared, then guilds formed, then global trade started." He laughed.
"Now billions of dollars are moved every year just in this industry."
Lian looked around, seeing the size of the store, his words did not seem exaggerated, and a few moments later he asked another question.
"What is the highest monster your store has tamed?" The seller’s face immediately brightened.
"An Unholy."
"Really?" Lian was a little surprised.
"Really, and it is now with the head of the consortium." Pride was dripping from his voice.
"A monster that many of the big guilds of the country and the continent made offers to buy, and none of them succeeded."
Lian whistled, an Unholy was no joke, but the more important question still remained.
"What is the highest tamed monster in all of history?"
The seller was silent for a few moments and then said.
"Have you heard the name Astreon Valkris?"
"Of course." Lian answered almost immediately.
How could he not have heard? The most legendary summoner in history, a man who appeared during the third Ruined Realm.
A creature that was said to have single-handedly destroyed four of the seven crystals of the third Ruined Realm.
"He managed to tame one and only one Demon." The seller smiled.
Silence filled the space, for a few seconds even Lian did not say anything, he had expected there to be several cases.
But only one Demon?
The seller continued.
"Unholy monsters and above are not wild animals, they have intelligence, they have pride, they have personality, and most importantly, they have will." His face became serious.
"Many of them prefer to die rather than live under someone’s command, that is why the total number of tamed Unholies in history might not even reach twenty."
"And Demons? One, only that one case."
Lian slowly let out his breath.
In the end, the seller took him to an open area, dozens of riding monsters were there, and among all of them, one caught his attention.
A sleek body, long legs, silver-gray fur, and yellow eyes that showed clear intelligence.
"You have a good eye." The seller smiled.
"Windrunner Strider, Common rank."
"Level eleven, extremely fast, excellent stamina, consumes little food, for long journeys it is almost without rival, but it has no combat power, otherwise it could have been a Rare."
Lian examined the creature for a few minutes, the monster also calmly examined him.
No roar, no display of power, and no extra behavior, just calm and ready, exactly what he needed.
"I want this one."
The seller smiled.
"An excellent choice."
The ownership documents were prepared and transferred, and a few minutes later everything was official, he entered his bank account information and sent a withdrawal request to the bank.
After confirmation and payment, Lian left the building, the monster moved calmly beside him.
Finally he felt truly ready to leave the base.
The massive city was behind him, watchtowers, stone walls, busy markets, and thousands of awakened ones each following their own dream.
But in front of him... the endless land of the Ruined Realm lay ahead.
Finally the time for exploration had come.
