chapters.title: Chapter 147: Disaster Is Here!
paragraphs: Last night, after hours of examining the mysterious Devourer egg and watching the monster corpses being devoured, Lian had finally managed to sleep for a few hours.
When he woke up in the morning, for a few seconds he forgot where he was.
The sunlight was coming through the small window of his room and falling on the metal walls of the accommodation.
Then he heard the sound of people, the sound of footsteps, the sound of conversations, and the sound of cargo carts.
And he remembered that he was still inside the Base, after the big operation yesterday, the base had become full of life again.

Unfortunately, there were casualties yesterday, dozens of awakened ones had been killed, in fact, the number might have reached over a hundred, but because of all the safety and security measures that had been taken, the number of casualties did not reach thousands.
Although among these killed awakened ones, there were several powerful commanders whose deaths were a great loss.
Their bodies had been taken outside and the overall condition of the base had stabilized.
But because of the death of those commanders, the second phase of the cleansing was not going to start anytime soon.
Hunters were preparing for new missions.
Caravans carrying loot were passing through the gates one after another.
Massive pack monsters were moving through the main streets of the base, moving mountains of Ironfang corpses.
In every corner of the base, people were talking about yesterday’s operation.
Some were talking about the money they were going to receive, some about the Fallen monsters, and some about the fact that new routes beyond the hundred kilometer radius would finally open soon.
After having breakfast, Lian left the room, his goal was simple, he wanted to check Kain’s status again.
But before reaching the academy center, something else caught his attention.
A group of people entered the base from the western gate, he immediately recognized a few of them.
Seraphina.
Cassian.
The head of the student council.
And a few other council members.
All of them were covered in dust, their clothes showed signs of a long journey, but from their appearance, it was clear their mission had been successful.
The first person to notice Lian’s presence was Cassian, and his face immediately brightened, he raised his hand and shouted with excitement.
"Lian!"
The head of the council just gave him a quick look and nodded, a simple greeting.
But Seraphina’s reaction was completely different, her eyes widened slightly.
"You are here?"
"Hello." Lian smiled.
They walked a few steps closer, and after a short greeting, the rest of the group gradually moved away.
Cassian, who apparently still had his inexhaustible energy, said a few more words and then headed toward the rest area with the others.
In the end, only Seraphina and Lian remained, and she said with a smile.
"So, how was your birthday ceremony?"
Lian laughed right at that moment, a laugh that made Seraphina even more curious.
"That is a long story, whenever you go back outside, ask your father about it."
Seraphina stared at his face for a few moments and then laughed quietly, she knew when Lian said it like that, it meant the problems had been solved and he had reached his goals.
"I feel like you had a really good time."
"More or less."
"More or less?"
"Considering what happened, yeah." Lian nodded.
Seraphina did not ask more, but her mysterious smile showed that her curiosity had increased.
The conversation quickly turned to their mission.
When Lian found out they had returned from a seven hundred kilometer radius, he unconsciously raised an eyebrow.
"Seven hundred kilometers? You went too far." Even he had only advanced to 400 kilometers, to advance beyond 400 kilometers, they would have had to cross that river path.
It was not the only way, but it was the fastest way, but clearly their group had taken the second way which was more winding.
"It was worth it." Seraphina shrugged.
"Did you find something?"
"Maybe."
Then she started explaining, broken stone pillars, geometric lines on the rocks, metals that had not rusted after years, and remains of walls that did not look natural.
The more she explained, the more Lian fell into thought, and finally he said.
"Based on these signs, it really looks like an ancient ruin, but it is still not possible to be sure."
Seraphina nodded.
"We think the same, we came back today to rest and recharge, we need to upgrade our equipment and buy a few safety talismans... and tomorrow we will go back there." Then she looked directly at him.
"Do you want to come with us?"
Lian was silent for a few seconds, he really had a skill for finding special and unusual places, after all, at one time he even wanted to become an analyzer.
But the current situation was much more complicated than a possible ruin, Kain was missing, the Devourer egg was in his room.
But it was not a bad idea either, maybe there the Celestial Book could find more treasures.
"I will think about it."
"Let me know by tonight." Seraphina smiled.
Then she told him the location of their group’s accommodation, and before parting, Lian asked an important question.
"Did you see Kain?"
"No, he was not there when we left, he was not there when we returned, and he was not there again when we left."
"God knows where he went."
"Don’t worry, he is not stupid enough to get himself killed." Seraphina laughed.
Lian did not say anything, but a few minutes later, he realized how wrong that sentence was.
After saying goodbye, he went straight to the academy information center, like last time, he entered the student system.
He opened Kain’s file, it took a few seconds, and then the information appeared.
Lian did not notice the change at first, but when he looked again, he felt his heart skip a beat.
[ Status: Semi Active / Decreased ]
Lian’s face became completely serious, this was no longer a joke, this status only appeared when a person was in real danger.
He remembered the explanation given by the officer, this situation practically meant one thing, Kain was trapped in a very bad condition and his vital signs were decreasing.
He was alive, but his condition was very bad, probably wounded, or probably trapped, and probably did not have much time.
"I have to find him as soon as possible!" Lian was still staring at the screen when suddenly everything shook.
Woooooooom!
A screeching sound echoed through the entire building, red emergency lights turned on, and everyone present in the hall froze.
Then chaos started.
Employees ran, hunters rushed out of the building, and red notifications appeared on all the screens.
Woooooooom!
Woooooooom!
The sirens were howling without stopping.
"What is going on?" Lian frowned and immediately left the building.
When he reached the main street, he saw a massive crowd moving toward the base’s defensive walls.
He went with them, a few minutes later he was standing on one of the watch platforms.
And he saw something that even made him silent for a moment, the base’s massive screens were on and the map of the area was displayed on them.
But almost the entire screen was covered with red dots.
Thousands of red dots.
Thunder Spine Serpents.
Ironhorn Marsh Drakes.
Two massive armies of monsters had surrounded the base! But this was only the beginning of the story, the image zoomed out further.
And the creature that was at the center of that army appeared.
At that same moment, Lian recognized it, the same monster he had seen in the depths of the river, the same guardian of the egg.
[ Abyssal River Drake ]
[ Rank: Fallen ]
[ Level: 35 ]
Silence fell over the defensive walls, even the high-level hunters lost their color.
Level thirty-five.
In the Base, such a creature was almost considered a disaster.
Lian stared at the monster, then at Kain’s status, then at his storage space, where the Devourer egg still was.
A strange feeling came over him, as if all the problems in the world had decided to come to him at the same time.
His friend was on the verge of death, an army of monsters had surrounded the base.
This was no longer just a simple normal day... this was the beginning of a disaster.

A group of people entered the base from the western gate, he immediately recognized a few of them.
Seraphina.
Cassian.
The head of the student council.
And a few other council members.
All of them were covered in dust, their clothes showed signs of a long journey, but from their appearance, it was clear their mission had been successful.
The first person to notice Lian’s presence was Cassian, and his face immediately brightened, he raised his hand and shouted with excitement.
"Lian!"
The head of the council just gave him a quick look and nodded, a simple greeting.
But Seraphina’s reaction was completely different, her eyes widened slightly.
"You are here?"
"Hello." Lian smiled.
They walked a few steps closer, and after a short greeting, the rest of the group gradually moved away.
Cassian, who apparently still had his inexhaustible energy, said a few more words and then headed toward the rest area with the others.
In the end, only Seraphina and Lian remained, and she said with a smile.
"So, how was your birthday ceremony?"
Lian laughed right at that moment, a laugh that made Seraphina even more curious.
"That is a long story, whenever you go back outside, ask your father about it."
Seraphina stared at his face for a few moments and then laughed quietly, she knew when Lian said it like that, it meant the problems had been solved and he had reached his goals.
"I feel like you had a really good time."
"More or less."
"More or less?"
"Considering what happened, yeah." Lian nodded.
Seraphina did not ask more, but her mysterious smile showed that her curiosity had increased.
The conversation quickly turned to their mission.
When Lian found out they had returned from a seven hundred kilometer radius, he unconsciously raised an eyebrow.
"Seven hundred kilometers?
You went too far." Even he had only advanced to 400 kilometers, to advance beyond 400 kilometers, they would have had to cross that river path.
It was not the only way, but it was the fastest way, but clearly their group had taken the second way which was more winding.
"It was worth it." Seraphina shrugged.
"Did you find something?"
"Maybe."
Then she started explaining, broken stone pillars, geometric lines on the rocks, metals that had not rusted after years, and remains of walls that did not look natural.
The more she explained, the more Lian fell into thought, and finally he said.
"Based on these signs, it really looks like an ancient ruin, but it is still not possible to be sure."
Seraphina nodded.
"We think the same, we came back today to rest and recharge, we need to upgrade our equipment and buy a few safety talismans... and tomorrow we will go back there." Then she looked directly at him.
"Do you want to come with us?"
Lian was silent for a few seconds, he really had a skill for finding special and unusual places, after all, at one time he even wanted to become an analyzer.
But the current situation was much more complicated than a possible ruin, Kain was missing, the Devourer egg was in his room.
But it was not a bad idea either, maybe there the Celestial Book could find more treasures.
"I will think about it."
"Let me know by tonight." Seraphina smiled.
Then she told him the location of their group’s accommodation, and before parting, Lian asked an important question.
"Did you see Kain?"
"No, he was not there when we left, he was not there when we returned, and he was not there again when we left."
"God knows where he went."
"Don’t worry, he is not stupid enough to get himself killed." Seraphina laughed.
Lian did not say anything, but a few minutes later, he realized how wrong that sentence was.
After saying goodbye, he went straight to the academy information center, like last time, he entered the student system.
He opened Kain’s file, it took a few seconds, and then the information appeared.
Lian did not notice the change at first, but when he looked again, he felt his heart skip a beat.
[ Status: Semi Active / Decreased ]
Lian’s face became completely serious, this was no longer a joke, this status only appeared when a person was in real danger.
He remembered the explanation given by the officer, this situation practically meant one thing, Kain was trapped in a very bad condition and his vital signs were decreasing.
He was alive, but his condition was very bad, probably wounded, or probably trapped, and probably did not have much time.
"I have to find him as soon as possible!" Lian was still staring at the screen when suddenly everything shook.
Woooooooom!
A screeching sound echoed through the entire building, red emergency lights turned on, and everyone present in the hall froze.
Then chaos started.
Employees ran, hunters rushed out of the building, and red notifications appeared on all the screens.
Woooooooom!
Woooooooom!
The sirens were howling without stopping.
"What is going on?" Lian frowned and immediately left the building.
When he reached the main street, he saw a massive crowd moving toward the base’s defensive walls.
He went with them, a few minutes later he was standing on one of the watch platforms.
And he saw something that even made him silent for a moment, the base’s massive screens were on and the map of the area was displayed on them.
But almost the entire screen was covered with red dots.
Thousands of red dots.
Thunder Spine Serpents.
Ironhorn Marsh Drakes.
Two massive armies of monsters had surrounded the base!
But this was only the beginning of the story, the image zoomed out further.
And the creature that was at the center of that army appeared.
At that same moment, Lian recognized it, the same monster he had seen in the depths of the river, the same guardian of the egg.
[ Abyssal River Drake ]
[ Rank: Fallen ]
[ Level: 35 ]
Silence fell over the defensive walls, even the high-level hunters lost their color.
Level thirty-five.
In the Base, such a creature was almost considered a disaster.
Lian stared at the monster, then at Kain’s status, then at his storage space, where the Devourer egg still was.
A strange feeling came over him, as if all the problems in the world had decided to come to him at the same time.
His friend was on the verge of death, an army of monsters had surrounded the base.
This was no longer just a simple normal day... this was the beginning of a disaster.

chapters.title: Chapter 148: A New System’s Quest
paragraphs: [ A Quest has been issued for all awakened ones registered at Base #3 ].
[ Break the siege and save the base ].
[ Reward: 250 stats points / 25 fragments / Enough EXP for one level up ].
[ Note: As long as you are in this mission, you cannot leave the Ruined Realm ].
The sound of sirens was still echoing throughout the base.
Woooooooom!
Woooooooom!
The red emergency lights on the walls were on, and every few seconds their red light would fall on people’s faces.
The entire atmosphere of the base had changed within a few minutes, a few hours ago people were talking about the loot from yesterday’s operation.
About the money, about their share of the several tens of millions of dollars reward, about the new routes that had opened up after the Ironfang Ravagers were destroyed.
But now no one was talking about those things, fear had taken the place of everything else.
The massive gates of the base were closed one after another, the defensive walls were activated, and the mana cannons on the towers started charging.
Guard groups were rushing toward defensive positions.
The emergency announcement was broadcast over the base’s speakers again and again.
"All missions are canceled."
"All awakened ones must be ready for defense."
"This is a red-level emergency situation."
Many hunters were still wounded from yesterday’s operation, some had bandages on their arms, some had deep wounds visible on their bodies.
But no one had found time to rest, because this time what was coming toward the base was not just a monster nest.
But a complete army from two monster races.
They had struggled and barely succeeded in defeating one race yesterday, and now two races just as powerful, with several Fallen ones each, had launched an assault on their base and surrounded them.
And among them was a level 35 Fallen one! This was the main reason for everyone’s fear.
Why? What could be the reason? Were they angry about the destruction of their neighbors?
Even now, the system had issued a quest for them, the reward was really great, but the fact that they could not leave the Ruined Realm was like a nightmare.
This meant they either had to die or they had to save this place.
Lian was standing with the crowd on one of the high platforms.
Large holographic screens were displaying new information, red dots covered the entire area around the base.
Thunder Spine Serpents.
Ironhorn Marsh Drakes.
Thousands of monsters, thousands!
And the scary thing was that none of them were attacking, they were just standing there.
Waiting and silent, as if they were watching something or waiting for a command.
A few minutes later, the emergency meeting of the commanders began.
The female commander and the high-ranking hunters present at the base all gathered in one of the central buildings.
Lian was not allowed to attend the meeting, but part of the information was released through public screens.
The more information appeared, the more concerning the situation looked.
The monsters had not come here randomly, they had cut off the supply routes.
They had covered all the exit routes, caravans outside the base were trapped, and no reinforcements could enter, no one could leave.
This was not just an attack, it was a complete siege.
But they were lucky that they did not depend on outside support, all the portals were inside the base, and that was the first thing they did.
They contacted the government and the federation as fast as possible to send help and explained the situation, but unfortunately, help could not arrive that soon.
Many very high-level awakened ones had been involved in conflicts in the Heavenly Realm in recent days, and most of them were not available right now.
Everyone’s hope faded again... was there really nothing they could do?
At that same moment, something sparked in Lian’s mind, he looked at the image of the Abyssal River Drake, the same monster he had seen in the depths of the river.
The same creature that was patrolling around the egg, and then he thought about his storage space.
About the egg, about the Devourer, about that unknown object that even the book of treasure had not been able to analyze.
For the first time, this thought entered his mind, could they have come for the egg? At first glance, this assumption seemed foolish.
But the more he thought, the more he felt everything fit together.
Three different races, three races that should not live together in principle.
Unusual population growth, guarding the river, the presence of a level 35 guardian, and just a few hours after the egg disappeared, a complete siege of the base.
Lian quietly whispered under his breath.
"Damn it... they really came for the egg." Only a fool could not understand that they had come here for this.
And all the evidence was practically screaming that this entire army had come here because of what was now inside his storage space.
Half an hour later, he found Seraphina again.
The student council had also been summoned as backup forces, everyone who could help at this point had been called in.
Level did not matter anymore, whoever could help had to help, they had to save the base.
The council members were preparing their equipment.
"The situation is not good." When Seraphina saw him, she came straight toward him.
"I saw." Lian nodded.
Seraphina looked toward the defensive walls.
"If this siege continues, tomorrow’s trip will be canceled."
Lian did not say anything, but his mind was elsewhere, Kain and his critical status, if he was really wounded... if he was really trapped somewhere... he might only have a few hours left.
"The reward for this quest is very good, if we succeed, it will be a big boost." Seraphina then changed the subject.
"Yeah, 250 stats points is not something you can get every day, along with enough EXP for a level up."
"Exactly! If we succeed in this mission, it could be even more valuable than that ancient ruin." That girl nodded.
The only thing giving everyone hope right now was exactly this system quest reward, otherwise, which sane person would dare to fight ten Fallen ones and two races of monsters?
After separating from Seraphina, Lian went straight to the information center.
He started examining the siege maps, possible routes, monster deployment points, patrol groups, and anything that could help him.
If he wanted to find Kain, he had to leave the base.
But how? After a few hours of examination, he finally noticed something.
The siege was not complete, it was almost complete but not entirely, on the river side, the density of forces was lower.
Much lower, the reason was clear, the monsters considered that area safe, and no one was willing to enter that area again.
But for Lian... that point could be his escape route, if he could reach the river, after that he could move freely.
Also, leaving this place was not hard for him, but immediately another problem appeared, he looked at his skill status.
[ Abyss Veil ]
[ Cooldown Remaining: 5 Hours 42 Minutes ]
Lian frowned, without Abyss Veil, crossing the siege was almost impossible.
And even if he succeeded... the main problem still remained, he had no idea where Kain was, there were no coordinates.
There was no clue, no witness, and only a Semi active status in the academy database.
Night fell.
The sirens could still be heard sometimes, the defensive towers were lit, the guards had doubled, and the base had turned into a war fortress.
Lian finally returned to his room, closed the door, and stood in silence for a few moments.
Then he took the egg out of the storage space, the red light was flowing calmly on the egg’s surface.
But something had changed, he immediately noticed it.
The pulses, they had become stronger, the egg was now pulsing faster than before, each pulse was like the heartbeat of a living creature.
Thump.
Thump.
Thump.
Suddenly a window appeared in front of him.
[ Warning ]
[ Devourer Senses Nearby Hostility ]
[ Devourer Is Hungry ]
Lian just stared at the notification for a few moments, then calmly looked at the egg, he felt that something inside it had awakened.
That previous stillness was no longer there, as if the creature inside the egg had started to feel its surroundings.
As if it was waiting for something or... hungry.
At that same moment... kilometers away from the base...
The Abyssal River Drake suddenly moved, its massive head slowly rose, and its bright red eyes fixed on the base.
It remained completely still for a few seconds, then its mouth opened and it roared, a roar that shook the ground.
A roar that was heard even from several kilometers away.
The base walls trembled, glass vibrated, and terrified people looked at the sky.
And at that same moment... thousands of monsters responded at the same time.
The serpents, the crocodiles, and all the surrounding creatures.
All of them roared together, a sound that rushed toward the base like a storm from every direction.
Even the base commanders understood that not much time remained.
The storm was coming.
( Abyssal River Drake’s Visualization )
( Ironhorn Marsh Drakes’s Visualization )
( Thunder Spine Serpents’s Visualization )

chapters.title: Chapter 149: Searching For Kain
paragraphs: After the terrifying roar of the Abyssal River Drake, sleep no longer had any meaning for Lian.
Every time he closed his eyes, two images appeared before him: Kain’s critical condition and the massive army of monsters that had surrounded the base.
In the end, he only rested for a few hours and woke up before the sun fully rose.
As soon as he saw that his skill’s cooldown had finished, he got up.
And after waking up, he realized that he was not the only one who could not sleep or rest properly.
All the awakened ones in the base had been unable to get proper rest because of worry.
The guards and many of the groups formed for the defense of the base were still making final preparations for the start of a large conflict.
The atmosphere of the base was heavier than ever.
There was no longer any sign of the excitement and joy after the cleansing operation.
Instead, anxiety could be seen on everyone’s faces.
Hunters were moving around in a hurry.
Emergency notifications were flashing on the holographic screens, and in every corner, there was talk of the siege and the monsters outside the walls.
But Lian’s mind was locked on another matter: Kain.
He went to the academy information center without wasting any time.
The information center was busier than ever.
Employees were going back and forth between dozens of emergency requests.
Hunters were checking route information, commanders were receiving patrol reports, but Lian went straight to the student terminals.
He opened Kain’s file once again, and then started searching.
All registered missions, all exit routes, all patrol reports, all traces, and even reports of monsters that had been seen in the past week.
Hours passed, but he found almost nothing.
It was as if Kain had disappeared after leaving the base.
Like a ghost, like someone who had never existed.
Lian leaned back in his chair quietly.
He felt helpless.
If he could not even find his movement path, how was he supposed to save him?
He had no clues.
Even if he somehow managed to get out of this base and the siege, how was he supposed to find his foolish friend in such a vast world?
He could be anywhere! Practically anywhere!
At that moment, a voice was heard from beside him.
"Still looking for your friend?"
Lian raised his head.
One of the senior officials of the information department was standing in front of him.
A middle-aged man with holographic glasses and a tired face.
Lian just nodded.
"His condition is critical."
The man was silent for a few moments and then sighed.
"In normal circumstances, I could not show you this information, but now the circumstances are not normal."
"In normal circumstances, when a student’s condition is in danger, we form a committee to save him."
"But as you can see, the situation is not such that a committee can be formed, and even if your friend is in danger, I doubt you can do anything."
"If I knew which direction he went, I might have a chance." Lian looked at him and said quietly.
"Maybe I can help you." The middle-aged man thought for a moment and then nodded.
A few minutes later, new access was opened on Lian’s terminal.
This time, information appeared that had previously been hidden.
Internal logs, emergency tracking, and the last points where a weak signal from Kain had been received.
And for the first time... the map began to change.
A faint line appeared on the screen, showing the movement path and direction: northwest, much farther than the normal range of student missions.
Lian remained motionless for a few seconds, because he recognized that path.
Very well.
It was the same direction that Seraphina and her group had returned from.
The same area where the signs of an ancient ruin had been found.
"No..." a whisper escaped his mouth.
His mind began to analyze the information at high speed.
Kain was foolish, but not so foolish as to enter a death zone without reason.
Kain loved exploration, loved discovering things that others could not find.
He had studied the Ruined Realms for countless hours, of course after him.
Maybe even more than most academy students.
If anyone could guess the existence of an ancient ruin from a few broken pillars and a few worn signs... that person was Kain, still after him.
And if there really was a ruin there... there was a high chance he had entered it alone.
Lian quietly clenched his fists.
"Damn it..." The more he thought about it, the more logical this possibility seemed.
And that made him even more worried.
A few minutes later, he left the information center.
There was only one person who could give him more information about that area.
Seraphina.
The student council’s location had almost turned into a military warehouse.
Boxes of equipment, armors, weapons, potions, magic scrolls, and everywhere was full of activity.
The council members were preparing for the possible defense of the base.
When Seraphina saw Lian, she immediately realized that something had happened, and her smile faded.
"What happened?"
Lian explained all the information: Kain’s critical condition, the northwest route, and its possible connection to the ancient ruin.
The more he spoke, the more serious Seraphina’s face became.
When he finished, a few seconds of silence passed between them.
"Wait... you want to leave the base?" Seraphina then said slowly.
Lian nodded.
"Now? In the middle of this siege?"
Lian gave the same answer again, a quiet nod.
Real worry could be seen in Seraphina’s eyes.
Not the worry of a classmate, not the worry of a mission companion, but the worry of a friend.
"Then I am coming too."
"No." Lian answered almost immediately.
"Lian—"
"No." He spoke more firmly this time.
"This is a rescue mission.
If Kain is really there, we do not know what he has faced."
Seraphina fell silent, and she knew he was right.
In the end, she just sighed.
"Okay... but take care of yourself."
Then she gave Lian everything she knew about those ruin signs and their location.
That was the least she could do to save their friend.
Lian thanked her and then changed the subject and asked.
"What about the request for help from neighboring bases?"
The base commanders had sent requests for reinforcements.
"The commanders sent requests for reinforcements, but the nearest base is very far.
It will take at least two to three days for the forces to arrive."
Lian frowned, two to three days was a very long time.
"And there is no guarantee that the base will survive until then." Seraphina said this more quietly, but its impact was not less.

Lian thought about the base’s massive walls, about the army of monsters outside, about that level thirty-five monster, and finally he took the possibility of the base falling seriously, but he was not worried.
He was sure that if the situation became too dire, the base definitely had emergency protocols to deal with it.
He was not worried about the base.
First, before leaving, he planned to make a significant contribution, and second, he knew that bases always had ready-made procedures for such conditions.
The question was just how bad the situation would get.
This base should be able to hold out for days without problems.
After all, all those defensive arrays were not for beauty and decoration.
After saying goodbye, he went straight back to his room.
He closed the door and just sat in silence for a few minutes.
Then he looked at the Devourer egg that was in his storage space.
The same massive egg, the same red and black veins, and the same calm pulse.
He did not say anything, just looked at it in silence.
In the end, he kept it inside the storage space.
If there was any safer place than that, he did not know it.
No one could see it, no one could touch it, and more importantly... no one could sense its presence.
Even those monsters, maybe when they could no longer find or sense the egg, they would lift the siege.
But right when he was preparing his equipment... the ground shook.
Boom!
A massive explosion.
Then a second explosion.
Then a third.
Screams rose from outside, and new sirens sounded, louder than before, more dangerous than before, and all the room’s screens suddenly turned on.
A red notification appeared on them.
[Emergency Alert]
[Outer Defensive Line Breached]
For a few seconds, time stopped, then the sound of more explosions was heard.
The monsters had finally launched their attack.
Lian immediately went to the window and saw the scene outside.
The sky was lit up with blue lightning, and columns of fire were rising from different parts of the base.
Explosions were happening one after another, and hundreds of Thunder Spine Serpents had charged onto the defensive walls.
The roars of the monsters had filled the entire base.
Lian stared at that hell for a few seconds, then turned back toward the room’s door, placed his hand on the handle, and whispered under his breath.
"I hope you are still alive when I get there, Kain."
At that same moment, the sound of another explosion shook the entire building, and outside... the battle for the base’s survival had begun.

sentences.text: After the terrifying roar of the Abyssal River Drake, sleep no longer had any meaning for Lian.
Every time he closed his eyes, two images appeared before him: Kain’s critical condition and the massive army of monsters that had surrounded the base.
In the end, he only rested for a few hours and woke up before the sun fully rose.
As soon as he saw that his skill’s cooldown had finished, he got up.
And after waking up, he realized that he was not the only one who could not sleep or rest properly.
All the awakened ones in the base had been unable to get proper rest because of worry.
The guards and many of the groups formed for the defense of the base were still making final preparations for the start of a large conflict.
The atmosphere of the base was heavier than ever.
There was no longer any sign of the excitement and joy after the cleansing operation.
Instead, anxiety could be seen on everyone’s faces.
Hunters were moving around in a hurry.
Emergency notifications were flashing on the holographic screens, and in every corner, there was talk of the siege and the monsters outside the walls.
But Lian’s mind was locked on another matter: Kain.
He went to the academy information center without wasting any time.
The information center was busier than ever.
Employees were going back and forth between dozens of emergency requests.
Hunters were checking route information, commanders were receiving patrol reports, but Lian went straight to the student terminals.
He opened Kain’s file once again, and then started searching.
All registered missions, all exit routes, all patrol reports, all traces, and even reports of monsters that had been seen in the past week.
Hours passed, but he found almost nothing.
It was as if Kain had disappeared after leaving the base.
Like a ghost, like someone who had never existed.
Lian leaned back in his chair quietly.
He felt helpless.
If he could not even find his movement path, how was he supposed to save him?
He had no clues.
Even if he somehow managed to get out of this base and the siege, how was he supposed to find his foolish friend in such a vast world?
He could be anywhere!
Practically anywhere!
At that moment, a voice was heard from beside him.
"Still looking for your friend?"
Lian raised his head.
One of the senior officials of the information department was standing in front of him.
A middle-aged man with holographic glasses and a tired face.
Lian just nodded.
"His condition is critical."
The man was silent for a few moments and then sighed.
"In normal circumstances, I could not show you this information, but now the circumstances are not normal."
"In normal circumstances, when a student’s condition is in danger, we form a committee to save him."
"But as you can see, the situation is not such that a committee can be formed, and even if your friend is in danger, I doubt you can do anything."
"If I knew which direction he went, I might have a chance." Lian looked at him and said quietly.
"Maybe I can help you." The middle-aged man thought for a moment and then nodded.
A few minutes later, new access was opened on Lian’s terminal.
This time, information appeared that had previously been hidden.
Internal logs, emergency tracking, and the last points where a weak signal from Kain had been received.
And for the first time... the map began to change.
A faint line appeared on the screen, showing the movement path and direction: northwest, much farther than the normal range of student missions.
Lian remained motionless for a few seconds, because he recognized that path.
Very well.
It was the same direction that Seraphina and her group had returned from.
The same area where the signs of an ancient ruin had been found.
"No..." a whisper escaped his mouth.
His mind began to analyze the information at high speed.
Kain was foolish, but not so foolish as to enter a death zone without reason.
Kain loved exploration, loved discovering things that others could not find.
He had studied the Ruined Realms for countless hours, of course after him.
Maybe even more than most academy students.
If anyone could guess the existence of an ancient ruin from a few broken pillars and a few worn signs... that person was Kain, still after him.
And if there really was a ruin there... there was a high chance he had entered it alone.
Lian quietly clenched his fists.
"Damn it..." The more he thought about it, the more logical this possibility seemed.
And that made him even more worried.
A few minutes later, he left the information center.
There was only one person who could give him more information about that area.
Seraphina.
The student council’s location had almost turned into a military warehouse.
Boxes of equipment, armors, weapons, potions, magic scrolls, and everywhere was full of activity.
The council members were preparing for the possible defense of the base.
When Seraphina saw Lian, she immediately realized that something had happened, and her smile faded.
"What happened?"
Lian explained all the information: Kain’s critical condition, the northwest route, and its possible connection to the ancient ruin.
The more he spoke, the more serious Seraphina’s face became.
When he finished, a few seconds of silence passed between them.
"Wait... you want to leave the base?" Seraphina then said slowly.
Lian nodded.
"Now?
In the middle of this siege?"
Lian gave the same answer again, a quiet nod.
Real worry could be seen in Seraphina’s eyes.
Not the worry of a classmate, not the worry of a mission companion, but the worry of a friend.
"Then I am coming too."
"No." Lian answered almost immediately.
"Lian—"
"No." He spoke more firmly this time.
"This is a rescue mission.
If Kain is really there, we do not know what he has faced."
Seraphina fell silent, and she knew he was right.
In the end, she just sighed.
"Okay... but take care of yourself."
Then she gave Lian everything she knew about those ruin signs and their location.
That was the least she could do to save their friend.
Lian thanked her and then changed the subject and asked.
"What about the request for help from neighboring bases?"
The base commanders had sent requests for reinforcements.
"The commanders sent requests for reinforcements, but the nearest base is very far.
It will take at least two to three days for the forces to arrive."
Lian frowned, two to three days was a very long time.
"And there is no guarantee that the base will survive until then." Seraphina said this more quietly, but its impact was not less.

Lian thought about the base’s massive walls, about the army of monsters outside, about that level thirty-five monster, and finally he took the possibility of the base falling seriously, but he was not worried.
He was sure that if the situation became too dire, the base definitely had emergency protocols to deal with it.
He was not worried about the base.
First, before leaving, he planned to make a significant contribution, and second, he knew that bases always had ready-made procedures for such conditions.
The question was just how bad the situation would get.
This base should be able to hold out for days without problems.
After all, all those defensive arrays were not for beauty and decoration.
After saying goodbye, he went straight back to his room.
He closed the door and just sat in silence for a few minutes.
Then he looked at the Devourer egg that was in his storage space.
The same massive egg, the same red and black veins, and the same calm pulse.
He did not say anything, just looked at it in silence.
In the end, he kept it inside the storage space.
If there was any safer place than that, he did not know it.
No one could see it, no one could touch it, and more importantly... no one could sense its presence.
Even those monsters, maybe when they could no longer find or sense the egg, they would lift the siege.
But right when he was preparing his equipment... the ground shook.
Boom!
A massive explosion.
Then a second explosion.
Then a third.
Screams rose from outside, and new sirens sounded, louder than before, more dangerous than before, and all the room’s screens suddenly turned on.
A red notification appeared on them.
[Emergency Alert]
[Outer Defensive Line Breached]
For a few seconds, time stopped, then the sound of more explosions was heard.
The monsters had finally launched their attack.
Lian immediately went to the window and saw the scene outside.
The sky was lit up with blue lightning, and columns of fire were rising from different parts of the base.
Explosions were happening one after another, and hundreds of Thunder Spine Serpents had charged onto the defensive walls.
The roars of the monsters had filled the entire base.
Lian stared at that hell for a few seconds, then turned back toward the room’s door, placed his hand on the handle, and whispered under his breath.
"I hope you are still alive when I get there, Kain."
At that same moment, the sound of another explosion shook the entire building, and outside... the battle for the base’s survival had begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 150: Ancient Ruins I
paragraphs: From the top of Base’s massive walls, a scene could be seen that would make any sane person think about running away.
Endless waves of Thunder Spine Serpents were flowing through the plains like a living river.
Their bodies covered with blue and purple scales were shining under the sunlight.
Among them, Ironhorn Marsh Drakes with their massive bodies and natural armor were charging at the defensive walls again and again.
Each collision shook the ground, but despite all of this... the base had still not fallen.
The mana towers were firing without stopping, blue, red, and golden beams were exploding among the monsters one after another.
On the walls, high-ranking mages were raining down fire, ice, and lightning on the attackers.
The level thirty-seven commander was personally present in the center of the field, and whenever a dangerous attack formed, she would step in herself.
On one of the defensive lines, Kael and his group could also be seen, Bren was standing like a steel wall in front of several monsters.
Rhea and Zak were moving non-stop among the enemies, Elias was helping other healers treat the wounded.
And Kael himself, every few minutes, would bring down a massive thunderbolt from the sky that would destroy dozens of monsters at once.
The battle was heavy, it was bloody, but they had not lost yet, and they were not going to lose at all, their enemy was certainly powerful, but they were sure that in the end they would win.
Lian looked at the battlefield for a few minutes and then whispered quietly.
"At least one day." His gaze moved across the defensive lines.
"If this continues like this... they will hold out for at least one more day." He paused briefly.
"I have to be back by then." He had no plan to run away like a coward and leave the base alone.
But unfortunately, when Kain’s condition is critical, he could not ignore his friend either, his priorities were completely clear.
He had to save his friend first, and then he could come back here and help in defeating these monsters.
It was not like he was not helping right now either, he planned to at least reduce the number of monsters a little before leaving here.
Before leaving the base, he checked Kain’s status once more, the holographic screen appeared in front of him.
A few seconds passed, and then the information appeared.
[Status: Semi active/Decreased]
He took a deep breath, fortunately the condition had not worsened, Kain was still alive, and he still had time, and that was enough.
A few minutes later, he was standing on one of the remote towers.
Below him... thousands of monsters could be seen, a sea of flesh, scales, horns, and teeth, everywhere he looked, only monsters could be seen.
But a faint smile appeared on Lian’s lips.
"Time to go." Mana began to flow in his body.
[Abyss Veil Activated]

Shadows rose from around him, crawling over his body like black liquid, his presence faded, the sounds around him disappeared, and a few moments later, even the sense of his existence was removed from the environment.
Then he activated the second skill.
[Fallen Wolf Speed]
Mana exploded, his muscles stretched, his bones trembled, the wind around him began to move, and the next moment... he jumped off the tower.
No monster noticed his passing, his speed was so high that even the eyes of many hunters could not follow him.
He moved among thousands of monsters, like a shadow passing through fog.
Like a ghost that does not exist, but every time the system found a suitable target... the story changed.
[Thunder Spine Serpent - Level 21]
The massive serpent raised its head, its forked tongue moved in the air, but before it could sense anything...
Glacial Reaper Claw was activated.
An ice claw shot out from the darkness, a blue line formed in the air, and the serpent’s head was severed.
Its massive body moved a few meters forward and then finally fell to the ground.
A few seconds later.
[Ironhorn Marsh Drake - Level 20]
The giant crocodile was busy attacking the wall.
Thunder Calamity gathered in Lian’s fist, white and blue lightning twisted around his arm.
Then the strike, the sound of an explosion echoed in the air, and the monster’s skull shattered like glass, its body was dragged several meters on the ground and remained lifeless.
One.
Two.
Three.
Ten.
Twenty.
Monsters fell one after another, without even understanding what had killed them.
All their attention was on the base, no one noticed the invisible hunter among them.
EXP was received.
Stats were received.
Notifications appeared one after another, and Lian continued moving without stopping, killing every monster below level 22 that he saw without hesitation.
Minutes passed, kilometers were left behind.
Dark forests, rocky hills, small rivers, burned plains, all passed by his eyes at high speed.
Along the way, every monster that got in his way was killed.
Not for revenge, not to be a hero, just because it was in his way, and when he finally distanced himself from the last ring of the siege...
For the first time, he stopped, there were no monsters around him, no sound of battle could be heard, only wind and silence.
He opened his status screen.
[ Stats points : 503 ]
There was no reason to keep them, and with the current situation he was in, the best thing to do was to use all of them to increase his power.
He immediately started distributing.
100 → Mana
100 → Physical Strength
100 → Resistance
50 → Spirit
77 → Speed
At that same moment, a wave of power covered his entire body.
His mana became denser, his muscles became more compact, his endurance increased, and his speed... his speed entered a new level.
He opened and closed his fists, the feeling of increasing power was intoxicating every time, but now was not the time to get addicted and drown in it.
He looked at the remaining amount and decided to keep the rest for when he needed it.
[ Stats points : 76 ]
"I have to get there faster." And he moved again.
This time he chose the river route, in normal conditions it was more dangerous but shorter, although now that no monsters were left there, it was considered completely safe.
And now time was the most important thing. Along the way, he saw signs of old battles many times.
Giant bones, claw marks carved into rocks, and trees whose halves had been destroyed.
And sometimes remains of creatures that he could not even identify.
But he did not stop.
The sun was slowly moving toward the horizon, orange light was falling on the river, and after hours of running... he finally reached his destination.
Lian landed on the branch of one of the massive trees, his breath was completely calm, and his body still had plenty of energy.
And his gaze fixed on the area ahead, broken pillars, carved stones, architectural traces that nature could not have created.
The signs were real, the same things Seraphina had described.
"So this is it." He had reached exactly the destination he was aiming for, he could easily see all the signs.
These were really classic signs of ancient ruins and remnants of destroyed civilizations.
But there was one problem, the ruin had still not been found, and this was only the area where the signs were seen.
The ruin itself could be hidden kilometers away, and he was now more than seven hundred kilometers from the base, but the real search had just begun.
The evening breeze moved among the branches, Lian looked at the horizon, then remembered Kain’s condition.
"I hope you are really here..." he whispered under his breath.

The problem was that he had not come here because he was sure his friend had come here, he came here because the only documents and information he had showed that this place was the most likely location for Kain.
Any possibility existed, Kain could have completely changed his path before reaching here and gone another way.
And all his efforts would be completely meaningless... but he had no choice, he could only hope that his friend was here.
